W1-040.evidence: src/app/(auth)/login/login-client.tsx:385-397 `const code = (result as { code?: string | null }).code; setError(code === "rate-limited" ? RATE_LIMITED : code === "bot-check" ? BOT_CHECK_FAILED : "Invalid email or password.");` — the fall-through claims a credential failure for every unrecognised error, including NextAuth's Configuration/CallbackRouteError shapes produced by an authorize() throw. src/lib/auth.ts:15-26 documents that only CredentialsSignin subclasses carry clean codes, i.e. every other throw arrives here code-less.
W1-040.reproPlan: Local dev: point DATABASE_URL at an unreachable host (or drop network mid-request via chrome-devtools), submit the login form, observe 'Invalid email or password.' — read-only, no shared-DB writes.
W1-040.fixDirection: In the login client, distinguish NextAuth's non-credentials error strings (result.error === "Configuration" / "CallbackRouteError", or simply: code undefined AND result.error not "CredentialsSignin") and show the transient-failure sentence instead. Optionally catch unexpected throws inside authorize() and rethrow a dedicated CredentialsSignin subclass with code "server-error" so the channel carries it cleanly like rate-limited/bot-check already do.
W1-040.gateOrTest: Unit test on the error-mapping helper (extract the ternary into a testable function) covering codes: rate-limited, bot-check, undefined-with-CredentialsSignin, undefined-with-Configuration.

W1-041.title: The deletion-scheduled email renders the purge date in server UTC (toLocaleDateString with no timeZone), so IST members deleting between 05:30–24:00 IST are told a purge day one day earlier than their local day-of-purge
W1-041.expected: Dates shown to members reflect their timezone (members are in IST, +5:30; servers run UTC) — the codebase knows this rule elsewhere: nextBudgetResetAt() is 'returned as a Date and formatted in the BROWSER's timezone by whoever shows it'.
W1-041.actual: requestAccountDeletion computes `purgeAt = new Date(Date.now() + DELETION_GRACE_DAYS * 86_400_000)` and formats it SERVER-side into the email: `purgeAt.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })` — no timeZone option, so on Vercel this renders the UTC calendar day. A member confirming deletion any time from 05:30 IST onward has a purgeAt whose IST date is one day later than its UTC date; the mail (their only written record, and 'the takeover alarm') names a day that, in their timezone, is the day BEFORE the purge moment. Off-by-one in the safe direction (they believe they have less time, not more), but it is a wrong date in the one message that exists to state a deadline, and the audit-log detail (`purgeAt.toISOString().slice(0, 10)`) records the same UTC day, so the two 'receipts' agree with each other and disagree with the member's calendar.
W1-041.evidence: src/components/settings/actions.ts:315 `const purgeAt = new Date(Date.now() + DELETION_GRACE_DAYS * 86_400_000);` and :344-348 `purgeDate: purgeAt.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" }),` — no timeZone, evaluated in the server's zone (UTC on Vercel). Compare src/lib/email-queue.ts:517-519 which deliberately defers formatting to the browser for exactly this reason.
W1-041.reproPlan: Code-argument-only (deterministic from the Intl call; a live proof would schedule a real account's deletion).
W1-041.fixDirection: Pass `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` to the toLocaleDateString call (the membership is IST by charter), or format with an explicit zone in the email template layer alongside a time-of-day, matching the 'a real clock time is a promise somebody can check' principle.
W1-041.gateOrTest: Unit test on the purge-date formatting with a fixed timestamp of 20:00 UTC asserting the IST day is rendered.

W1-042.title: requestVerification ignores the conditional updateMany count, so two simultaneous requests both notify the admins; and the delete-then-recreate place writers can duplicate rows under two-tab saves
W1-042.expected: The conditional write is the dedupe: whoever loses the updateMany race skips the side effect (the pattern tryRosterAutoVerify itself uses correctly at roster.ts:77-85); wholesale list replacement is atomic against a concurrent replacement of the same list.
W1-042.actual: Two independent small races. (1) requestVerification: `const already = session.user.verifyState === "pending"; if (!already) { await prisma.user.updateMany({ where: { id: ..., verifyState: "unverified" }, data: { verifyState: "pending" } }); await notifyAdmins(...); }` — two concurrent invocations (double-click before the dialog's pending state lands, or two tabs) both read verifyState 'unverified' from their request-cached sessions, both run updateMany (one matches, one matches zero rows), and BOTH call notifyAdmins because the count is never checked → duplicate admin notifications for one person. (2) saveOnboardingRegister and updateUserPlaces both replace UserPlace rows via deleteMany-then-createMany inside a transaction; UserPlace has no unique on (userId, position), so two overlapping saves at READ COMMITTED can interleave as T1-delete, T2-delete(sees 0 after T1 commits or concurrently), T1-create, T2-create → the member's city list holds both sets, showing duplicate city chips on the profile and doubled pins on the map until the next save wholesale-replaces them. Both are self-limiting (a repeat click / a re-save heals them) — hence Low — but both are the exact 6c lost-update/double-submit shape with one-line guards available.
W1-042.evidence: src/components/auth/verification-actions.ts:51-62 `const already = session.user.verifyState === "pending"; if (!already) { await prisma.user.updateMany({ where: { id: session.user.id, verifyState: "unverified" }, ... }); await notifyAdmins(...) }` — updateMany's count discarded; notifyAdmins unconditional inside the branch. src/components/onboarding/actions.ts:92-105 `await tx.userPlace.deleteMany({ where: { userId } }); if (cleanedPlaces.length > 0) { await tx.userPlace.createMany({...}) }` and src/components/settings/actions.ts:162-181 same delete/create pattern; prisma/schema.prisma:659-677 UserPlace has `@@index([userId])` but no unique constraint that a doubled insert would violate.
W1-042.reproPlan: Local dev with own test account (shared DB — self-healing writes only): fire requestVerification twice in parallel from the console and observe two admin notifications; fire updateUserPlaces twice in parallel with different lists and read the doubled UserPlace rows, then re-save once to heal.
W1-042.fixDirection: (1) Use the updateMany result: `const changed = await prisma.user.updateMany(...); if (changed.count > 0) await notifyAdmins(...)` — the row transition becomes the dedupe, exactly like the roster verify. (2) Add `@@unique([userId, position])` to UserPlace (makes the doubled createMany fail loudly instead of silently duplicating) and/or take a per-user advisory-free guard such as deleteMany-with-createMany keyed on a version column; at minimum disable the save buttons while pending.
W1-042.gateOrTest: Unit test asserting notifyAdmins is skipped when updateMany reports 0; schema constraint on UserPlace doubles as the test for (2).

W1-043.title: Signup derives batchType from an unvalidated (yearLeft, batchYear) pair: batchTypeFromLeaving happily returns 'ISC' for impossible inputs (batchYear earlier than yearLeft), unlike its sibling computeBatchFromSchooling which rejects them
W1-043.expected: The same sanity window the derive-from-schooling path enforces ('Those years add up to past 12th grade' when gradeAtLeaving > 12): a member's batchYear cannot be before their yearLeft, and a typo produces an error, not a silently wrong board credential.
W1-043.actual: signupSchema validates each year only against absolute bounds (1926..now+1 / now+7) and the action checks only `yearLeft < yearJoined`; nothing relates batchYear to yearLeft. registerUser then calls `batchType = batchTypeFromLeaving(parsed.data.yearLeft!, batchYear)` where `const gradeAtLeaving = 12 - (batchYear - yearLeft)` — a member who fat-fingers batchYear 2015 with yearLeft 2018 gets gradeAtLeaving 15 → 'ISC' stored; batchYear 2035 with yearLeft 2010 gets a negative grade → null batchType (reads as 'mid-school leaver'). Both are silently wrong facts on the profile and in directory filters, and the same unchecked pair flows through updateUserProfile (settings/actions.ts:86-91) on every later edit. computeBatchFromSchooling proves the intended envelope exists (`if (gradeAtLeaving > 12) return { ok: false, error: "Those years add up to past 12th grade..." }`) — the direct-entry path just never got it.
W1-043.evidence: src/lib/utils.ts:250-258 `export function batchTypeFromLeaving(yearLeft: number, batchYear: number): "ISC" | "ICSE" | null { const gradeAtLeaving = 12 - (batchYear - yearLeft); if (gradeAtLeaving >= 12) return "ISC"; ... }` — no upper bound on gradeAtLeaving. src/components/auth/actions.ts:90-93 `batchYear = parsed.data.batchYear!; batchType = batchTypeFromLeaving(parsed.data.yearLeft!, batchYear);` with no batchYear>=yearLeft refinement anywhere in src/lib/validators.ts:14-45. Contrast src/lib/utils.ts:322-328 (computeBatchFromSchooling) rejecting gradeAtLeaving > 12.
W1-043.reproPlan: Code-argument-only (pure function; a unit assertion demonstrates it: batchTypeFromLeaving(2018, 2015) === 'ISC').
W1-043.fixDirection: Add a refine to signupSchema (and profileSchema/updateUserProfile's batch block): batchYear >= yearLeft, and optionally batchYear - yearLeft <= 11 (cannot leave more than 11 years before your batch finishes 12th, i.e. gradeAtLeaving >= 1). Or make batchTypeFromLeaving return null (with the caller surfacing an error) when gradeAtLeaving > 12 or < 1, mirroring computeBatchFromSchooling's envelope.
W1-043.gateOrTest: Extend batch-line.test.mjs / a utils test with the impossible pairs pinning the rejection; schema refine test for signupSchema.

W1-044.title: confirmEmailToken and resetPassword burn the single-use token before applying its effect, outside any transaction: a crash or DB error in the gap consumes the member's link with nothing to show for it
W1-044.expected: 6d: the token consume and the write it authorizes either both land or neither (or the consume happens last), so a transient failure never leaves a member holding a dead link that did nothing.
W1-044.actual: confirmEmailToken: `const read = await readToken(token, "verify", { consume: true });` marks the AuthToken used, THEN `await prisma.user.update({ ..., data: { emailVerified: new Date() } })` — a serverless timeout, DB blip or crash between the two leaves the token spent and the email unconfirmed; the member's next click says 'already confirmed' (the used-token branch returns "already" without verifying the address actually is confirmed — the comment claims 'if the address really is confirmed, say so plainly' but the code never checks) while the gate still blocks them, a genuinely confusing contradiction. resetPassword has the same shape: consume at :252, bcrypt.hash (~100ms window) and the user.update at :266 after it — a failure in between burns the reset link with the password unchanged. Both have recovery paths (resend, re-request) so this is Low, but the recovery is rate-limited (verify 5/hour, reset 4/30min) and the 'already' lie in confirmEmailToken turns a transient blip into a support ticket.
W1-044.evidence: src/components/auth/email-actions.ts:104-121: `const read = await readToken(token, "verify", { consume: true }); if (!read.ok) { if (read.reason === "used") { return "already"; } ... } await prisma.user.update({ where: { id: read.userId }, data: { emailVerified: new Date() } });` — consume and effect are two separate awaits with no transaction; the "already" branch never verifies emailVerified is actually set. src/components/auth/email-actions.ts:252-282: consume (`readToken(..., { consume: true })`), then `const hashed = await bcrypt.hash(input.password, 12); await prisma.user.update({...})`. src/lib/auth-tokens.ts:183-191 shows the consume is its own updateMany.
W1-044.reproPlan: Code-argument-only (needs a fault injected between two awaits).
W1-044.fixDirection: For confirmEmailToken: perform the consume and the emailVerified update in one prisma.$transaction (both are simple updates — batch form works through pgbouncer), and make the "used" branch honest by checking the row's user.emailVerified before claiming "already" (readToken already selects the user relation; add emailVerified to that select). For resetPassword: hash BEFORE consuming (moves the long await out of the gap), then transaction the consume + user.update together; burnTokens can stay after.
W1-044.gateOrTest: Unit test on the "already" outcome asserting it reflects the row's emailVerified state; integration test with a mocked failing user.update asserting the token remains redeemable.

W1-045.title: A Catch-up whose Round publishes while paused never schedules another Round; resume does not re-arm nextOpensAt and there is no manual recovery
W1-045.expected: Pausing suspends the rhythm; resuming restores it. After resume, the next Round should eventually open on the cadence.
W1-045.actual: If the live Round crosses answering->preparing->published while the Catch-up is paused (the clock advance in advanceEdition does not stop for paused Catch-ups), nextOpensAt is never written. resumeCatchup only flips status back to active. openNextRoundIfDue requires a non-null nextOpensAt, and nothing else in the codebase ever sets it, so the Catch-up sits 'active' forever with no future Round, no error, and no Keeper control to start one.
W1-045.evidence: In applyEditionAction the publish transition guards the schedule write on live status: `if (action.setsNextOpensAt && meta.catchupStatus === "active") { await tx.catchup.update({ where: { id: meta.catchupId }, data: { nextOpensAt: addCadenceGap(now, meta.cadence) } }); }` (catchups.ts:802-806); publishNow has the identical guard `if (edition.catchup.status === "active")` (actions.ts:1054). pauseCatchup writes only `data: { status: "paused" }` (actions.ts:591) and resumeCatchup writes only `data: { status: "active" }` (actions.ts:618) — neither touches nextOpensAt. openNextRoundIfDue begins `const opensAt = catchup.nextOpensAt; if (!opensAt || now.getTime() < opensAt.getTime()) return;` (catchups.ts:908-909), and a repo-wide grep shows the ONLY writers of nextOpensAt are the two publish paths (both gated on active) and endCatchup (sets null). advanceDueCatchups also filters `where: { status: "active", nextOpensAt: { lte: now } }` (catchups.ts:971), so a null nextOpensAt is permanently invisible to the sweep. Meanwhile editions of paused Catch-ups DO keep advancing: the editions query at catchups.ts:956-964 does not filter on catchup.status, so a Round in flight at pause time will publish (members even get the catchup_published notification) — exactly the sequence that strands the series.
W1-045.fixDirection: In resumeCatchup, after flipping status to active, backfill the schedule when it is missing: read the latest edition; if it is published and nextOpensAt is null, set nextOpensAt = max(now, addCadenceGap(latest.publishedAt, cadence)) (or simply addCadenceGap(now, cadence) to restart the rhythm from resume). Alternatively/additionally have the publish transition write nextOpensAt unconditionally and let the status:'active' filter in advanceDueCatchups/openNextRoundIfDue be the sole pause gate — that second shape also removes the stale-meta corner where a pause/resume racing the publish transaction picks the wrong branch.
W1-045.gateOrTest: New integration-style test (or a node:test against a stubbed prisma) : pause -> clock-publish -> resume -> assert nextOpensAt is non-null; plus a regression assertion that resumeCatchup on a series whose latest edition is published never leaves nextOpensAt null.
W1-045.reproPlan: Code-argument-only in this shared DB (would require creating and pausing a real Catch-up). The grep for nextOpensAt writers plus the quoted guards is a complete proof.

W1-046.title: Changing cadence does not reschedule an already-set nextOpensAt, so the new rhythm silently takes effect only after the NEXT publish
W1-046.expected: A Keeper switching a quarterly Catch-up to biweekly expects the next Round to open ~14 days after the last publish, not ~3 months later.
W1-046.actual: updateCatchupCadence writes only the cadence column. nextOpensAt was already computed at the previous publish from the OLD cadence (`nextOpensAt: addCadenceGap(now, meta.cadence)`), and nothing recomputes it, so the pending open keeps the old rhythm for one full cycle. Worst case quarterly->biweekly: the group waits ~3 months for a 'biweekly' Catch-up, and the Round footer keeps announcing the stale date ('Next Round opens 20 November').
W1-046.evidence: `await prisma.catchup.update({ where: { id: catchupId }, data: { cadence: parsedCadence.data } });` (actions.ts:564) is the entire mutation — no nextOpensAt recompute. The pending date was fixed at publish time: `data: { nextOpensAt: addCadenceGap(now, meta.cadence) }` (catchups.ts:805). openNextRoundIfDue then trusts the stored value verbatim (catchups.ts:908-919). The stale date is member-visible via footer-tease.tsx:26 ('Next Round opens {date}').
W1-046.fixDirection: In updateCatchupCadence, when the Catch-up is active and nextOpensAt is non-null, recompute it from the latest published edition's publishedAt with the new cadence: nextOpensAt = max(now, addCadenceGap(latestPublishedAt, newCadence)). Clamp to now so shortening the cadence past an already-elapsed gap opens the next Round on the next sweep rather than backdating.
W1-046.gateOrTest: Unit test on the recompute helper (pure), plus an action-level test: publish (monthly), switch to biweekly, assert nextOpensAt == publishedAt + 14d.
W1-046.reproPlan: Code-argument-only (write path on the shared production DB).

W1-047.title: Server-rendered Catch-up dates show the UTC calendar day, one day earlier than the IST day members live in
W1-047.expected: All members are IST (UTC+5:30). A Round that publishes at 01:00 IST on 21 August should read 'Published 21 August 2026', and 'Next Round opens' should name the IST day it actually opens.
W1-047.actual: RoundMasthead, FooterTease and FreshOffThePress are server components; toLocaleDateString runs on Vercel in UTC with no timeZone option, so any timestamp falling in 18:30-24:00 UTC (00:00-05:30 IST) renders as the previous day. The lazy advance makes such timestamps common: a transition fires whenever the first page view lands after a deadline, so a night-owl member opening the app at 00:30 IST stamps publishedAt/nextOpensAt in exactly the shifted window. The masthead date is permanent archive copy, so the wrong day is engraved forever; the footer promises 'Next Round opens 20 September' when it opens on the 21st IST.
W1-047.evidence: masthead.tsx:50: `new Date(publishedAt).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })` — no timeZone, no "use client" directive in the file, imported by the (server) round page. footer-tease.tsx:26 is identical for nextOpensAt; fresh-off-the-press.tsx:23 identical for publishedAt (en-US). Concrete failure: publishedAt = 2026-08-20T19:30:00Z is 01:00 IST on 21 Aug; server renders 'Published 20 August 2026'. Contrast: the countdown copy (daysUntilLabel/describeEditionStatus in catchups.ts:550-601) is deliberately relative and immune — only these absolute-date renders shift.
W1-047.fixDirection: Pass timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata" to every toLocaleDateString/Intl.DateTimeFormat that renders a Catch-up timestamp in a server component (a small shared formatCatchupDate helper next to catchupTitle would end the per-file drift, and would also unify the currently inconsistent en-GB/en-US/en-IN locales). Members are a single-timezone community, so a fixed zone is correct here.
W1-047.gateOrTest: Unit test on the shared formatter: new Date('2026-08-20T19:30:00Z') formats to '21 August 2026'. The visual suite will not catch this (baselines are generated in the same TZ).
W1-047.reproPlan: Orchestrator can prove read-only: TZ=UTC node -e "console.log(new Date('2026-08-20T19:30:00Z').toLocaleDateString('en-GB',{day:'numeric',month:'long',year:'numeric'}))" prints 20 August 2026.

W1-048.title: A wholesale Catch-up engine failure is invisible: every error is swallowed to console.error, Sentry never sees it, and the tick cron always answers 200 ok
W1-048.expected: If the engine starts failing persistently (schema drift, permission change, a bad deploy), something should alarm: a Sentry event, a failing cron, anything. The project's own CLAUDE.md rule: 'A guard that hides its own breakage is worse than no guard.'
W1-048.actual: advanceEdition and advanceDueCatchups catch everything and only console.error (`console.error("[catchups] advanceEdition failed", err)` at catchups.ts:887; same at 983 and 989). Sentry is initialized without any console-capture integration (instrumentation.ts registers Sentry.init with no consoleLoggingIntegration), so those lines never become events. The tick route then reports success unconditionally: `await advanceDueCatchups(); return NextResponse.json({ ok: true });` — Vercel cron monitoring shows green while every Round in the community silently stops advancing. Detection currently depends on the owner happening to open /admin/catchups (which does list overdue Rounds) or on members complaining. Compounding it: until CRON_SECRET is set (still owed by the owner), the nightly tick 401s every night with the same zero telemetry, so the belt-and-braces layer is already silently off.
W1-048.evidence: catchups.ts:885-888: `} catch (err) { if (isMissingCatchupTable(err)) return; console.error("[catchups] advanceEdition failed", err); }` — swallow-and-continue is correct for the page-view piggyback but is the ONLY handling on the cron path too. tick/route.ts:31-32: `await advanceDueCatchups(); return NextResponse.json({ ok: true });` with no way for failures to surface. instrumentation.ts:42-72 shows the full Sentry config: dsn/enabled/environment/sendDefaultPii/tracesSampleRate/debug/ignoreErrors — no captureConsole/consoleLogging integration, so console.error is not captured.
W1-048.fixDirection: Inside the catch blocks (after the isMissingCatchupTable early-return) call Sentry.captureException(err) in addition to console.error — the engine already imports lazily, so a small dynamic import of @sentry/nextjs there keeps the pure-test property. Separately, make advanceDueCatchups return a { advanced, failed } summary and have the tick include it in the JSON (and return 500 or a distinct field when failed > 0) so Vercel cron logs show real health. Keep the layout call fire-and-forget on the summary.
W1-048.gateOrTest: A unit test that advanceDueCatchups returns a failure count when advanceEdition throws (stubbed prisma); plus eyeballing one induced Sentry event in preview.
W1-048.reproPlan: Code-argument-only; inducing a real engine failure against the shared DB is not acceptable.

W1-049.title: Reminder compare-and-swap omits the status guard, so a daily reminder can fire just after the Round closed or was closed by the Keeper
W1-049.expected: A 'N days left to answer' nudge must only ever commit while the Round is still answering — the sibling extend branch encodes exactly this with status in its WHERE.
W1-049.actual: The reminder branch CASes only on remindersSent: `where: { id: editionId, remindersSent: before.remindersSent }` (no status). Two concurrent drivers (the layout piggyback runs on every authenticated page view, the cron sweeps with a single now for its whole run, and closeAndPrepare is a Keeper click) can interleave: driver A plans a reminder while the Round is answering; driver B commits answering->preparing (which does not change remindersSent — preparingPatch touches only status/publishAt, and closeAndPrepare's CAS at actions.ts:937-940 likewise); A's reminder CAS still matches and commits, sending 'Last day to answer / N days left' notifications for a Round whose answers just closed, linking to an answer page that will refuse.
W1-049.evidence: catchups.ts:827-832: `const cas = await tx.catchupEdition.updateMany({ where: { id: editionId, remindersSent: before.remindersSent }, data: action.patch }); if (cas.count === 0) return false; await notify.notifyReminder(...)`. Contrast the extend branch three lines above: `where: { id: editionId, status: "answering", remindersSent: before.remindersSent }` (catchups.ts:818). The transition that races it leaves remindersSent untouched: preparingPatch returns `{ status: "preparing", publishAt: ... }` only (catchups.ts:439-444), and closeAndPrepare's non-extend path updates with that patch under `where: { id: editionId, status: "answering" }` (actions.ts:937-940). The plan-time guard (dueReminder requires status === "answering", catchups.ts:374) does not survive the gap between plan and apply, and the cron's single `now` for a whole sweep (catchups.ts:951) widens the divergence window between drivers.
W1-049.fixDirection: Add `status: "answering"` to the reminder branch's WHERE, matching the extend branch. One-line change; the losing driver already handles cas.count === 0 by re-reading and replanning.
W1-049.gateOrTest: Code-review pin plus a stubbed-prisma test: apply a reminder action against a row whose status already moved to preparing and assert no notification write.
W1-049.reproPlan: Code-argument-only; the race window is milliseconds and forcing it live needs writes.

W1-050.title: The (main) layout comment claims the Catch-up advance cannot hold up page render, but it is awaited in the render-blocking Promise.all
W1-050.expected: Per the comment ('it also runs concurrently with (not blocking) the count query, so a slow or stale advance can never hold up page render'), the advance should not delay TTFB.
W1-050.actual: advanceDueCatchups(session.user.id) sits inside the awaited Promise.all, so every authenticated page view waits for it to settle. Normally that is two indexed queries, but the unlucky first request after a boundary pays the whole transition inline: entry count, the CAS transaction, group-member fetch, reminder deleteMany + notification createMany for the whole group — before their page renders. The comment documents an intent (after()-style, like drainMailQueue ten lines below) that the code does not implement, which invites the next editor to trust the wrong contract.
W1-050.evidence: layout.tsx:35-52: `const [unreadCount, mailState] = await Promise.all([ prisma.notification.count({...}), ..., advanceDueCatchups(session.user.id), touchLastSeen(...) ]);` — Promise.all resolves only when ALL settle, so render waits on the advance. The mail queue, by contrast, is correctly deferred: `after(async () => { await drainMailQueue(); ... })` (layout.tsx:63-69) precisely because 'every page in the app would wait on somebody else's welcome email' — the same argument applies to somebody else's Round transition.
W1-050.fixDirection: Either move advanceDueCatchups into the same after() block (it makes no network calls, only DB writes, so after() is safe and the notification count already races it today), or fix the comment to state honestly that render waits on it. Preferred: after(), keeping the awaited path to the count + mailState reads only.
W1-050.gateOrTest: None mechanical; verify by reading the diff and one TTFB spot-check on a page view that triggers a publish in dev-style conditions.
W1-050.reproPlan: Code-argument-only (timing proof would need a live transition).

W1-051.title: void recordView on the Round page (and three sibling pages) is a fire-and-forget DB write that serverless may kill after the response
W1-051.expected: A write started during render either completes or is scheduled via after()/waitUntil so the platform keeps the instance alive for it.
W1-051.actual: `void recordView(session?.user?.id, "round", edition.id)` floats a Prisma upsert with no await and no after(). On Vercel, once the RSC response finishes streaming the function may be suspended before the upsert reaches Postgres, so 'round' view counts (and the same pattern on profile/letters/collection) silently undercount in production — precisely the failure mode the audit brief's 6a row names. The in-code comment ('the page renders at the same speed either way') optimizes latency but picks the one mechanism with no completion guarantee when after() gives the same latency WITH the guarantee.
W1-051.evidence: round/[editionId]/page.tsx:193-194: `/* Not awaited: the page renders at the same speed either way. */ void recordView(session?.user?.id, "round", edition.id);`. content-view.ts:28-33 shows it is a real DB write: `await prisma.contentView.upsert({ where: { viewerId_kind_targetId: {...} }, create: {...}, update: { count: { increment: 1 }, lastAt: new Date() } })`. The codebase itself models the correct pattern one layer up: layout.tsx wraps drainMailQueue in `after(...)` for exactly this reason.
W1-051.fixDirection: Wrap the call in next/server's after(): `after(() => recordView(...))` at all four call sites (recordView already never throws). Zero latency change, guaranteed execution.
W1-051.gateOrTest: A grep-style regression check (like security-regressions.test.mjs) asserting no `void recordView(` remains outside an after() callback.
W1-051.reproPlan: Code-argument-only; the loss is probabilistic on production infrastructure and unobservable locally.

W1-052.title: toggleEntryLove races surface a raw 'Something went wrong' on double-click, and notifyLove's check-then-insert can double-notify
W1-052.expected: A double-tap on a heart settles to a consistent state with no error toast; the love notification is coalesced to at most one unread per author per Round.
W1-052.actual: toggleEntryLove is check-then-act with no P2002/P2025 handling: two rapid taps both read `existing` as null, both create; the second hits the @@unique([userId, entryId]) and runAction converts it to the generic 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' toast (and the client's toggle state can end opposite to reality). The mirrored delete path can throw P2025 the same way. Separately, notifyLove coalesces via findFirst-then-create (`const existing = await db.notification.findFirst({... read: false }); if (existing) return;`) with no unique backstop and called on the shared client (not a transaction), so two members hearting the same answer concurrently produce two notifications — the comment's 'cannot spam' claim holds per-day practically but the invariant is not enforced.
W1-052.evidence: actions.ts:1213-1221: `const existing = await prisma.catchupEntryLove.findUnique({ where: { userId_entryId: {...} } ... }); if (existing) { await prisma.catchupEntryLove.delete({ where: { id: existing.id } }); } else { await prisma.catchupEntryLove.create({ data: {...} });` — no isUniqueConstraintError branch (the helper exists at actions.ts:174 and is used by createCatchup only). runAction's fallback (actions.ts:169-170) is the generic error. catchups-notify.ts:197-201: `const existing = await db.notification.findFirst({ where: { userId: ctx.authorId, type: "catchup_love", link, read: false }, select: { id: true } }); if (existing) return; // coalesce` — classic TOCTOU with no constraint behind it.
W1-052.fixDirection: In toggleEntryLove, treat P2002 on create as 'already loved' and P2025 on delete as 'already unloved' (return the truthful loved state instead of an error). For notifyLove, either accept the rare duplicate explicitly in the comment or make it race-safe with deleteMany-then-create of the single coalesced row (matching notifyReminder's replace pattern).
W1-052.gateOrTest: Action-level test: two concurrent toggles on one entry resolve without an error return; a stubbed test that a P2002 from create yields { success, loved: true }.
W1-052.reproPlan: Live proof possible on a demo/test account: double-click a heart fast on a published Round and watch for the error toast; but code argument suffices.

W1-053.title: submitPrompt assigns position by count outside any transaction: concurrent submissions get duplicate positions and an unstable question order
W1-053.expected: Each accepted question gets a distinct position so the Round renders in one stable order everywhere.
W1-053.actual: Two members submitting simultaneously both read acceptedCount = N and both insert position N. There is no unique on (editionId, position), so both commit; every surface ordering by position asc then breaks the tie nondeterministically, so the question order can differ between the home console, the answer page, and successive loads — until a Keeper reorder rewrites positions. The MAX_ACCEPTED_PROMPTS cap is the same read-then-write, so the 40 ceiling can be pierced by one under concurrency (harmless — it is a runaway guard).
W1-053.evidence: actions.ts:707-710: `const acceptedCount = await prisma.catchupPrompt.count({ where: { editionId, accepted: true } });` then actions.ts:714-724: `await prisma.catchupPrompt.create({ data: { ... position: acceptedCount } })` — no transaction, no unique constraint (schema.prisma CatchupPrompt has only `@@index([editionId, position])`, line 768). Reads order by `{ position: "asc" }` with no secondary key (answer/page.tsx:179).
W1-053.fixDirection: Cheapest complete fix: add a stable secondary sort (position asc, createdAt asc, id asc) at every prompt read so duplicate positions can never reorder between loads; optionally also compute position inside a short $transaction or via `position: { set: }`-free create with a subquery-style raw insert. The secondary sort alone removes the member-visible symptom.
W1-053.gateOrTest: Unit-level: two creates with equal position render in a fixed order given the added tiebreaker; grep gate that every catchupPrompt.findMany orderBy includes the tiebreaker.

W1-054.title: 'Answers close today' is a 24-hour-window claim wearing calendar-day words: it shows a day early for deadlines that fall tomorrow morning IST
W1-054.expected: 'Answers close today' should be true in the member's calendar: the close instant falls before their next midnight.
W1-054.actual: closesLabel computes days = ceil(diff/24h) and prints 'Answers close today.' whenever diff <= 24h. A window closing at 09:00 IST tomorrow, read at 10:00 IST today (diff 23h), reads 'close today' — factually wrong by the member's calendar, though it errs on the rush-them side. The engine's own copy elsewhere says 'last day' for this exact state (daysUntilLabel, catchups.ts:556-557), which is accurate language for a 24h bucket; this one surface upgraded it to a calendar claim.
W1-054.evidence: answer/page.tsx:56-63: `const diff = at.getTime() - Date.now(); if (diff <= 0) return "Answers are closing."; const days = Math.ceil(diff / (24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)); if (days <= 1) return "Answers close today."; return `Answers close in ${days} days.`;` — pure duration math, no calendar/timezone awareness, while the string asserts a calendar day.
W1-054.fixDirection: Change the copy to the bucket-truthful 'Last day to answer.' (matching daysUntilLabel and the reminder copy), or compute the member-calendar day with Asia/Kolkata and say today/tomorrow correctly. Copy change is one line and keeps the no-timezone-machinery fence.
W1-054.gateOrTest: Unit test on closesLabel at the 23h boundary once extracted or duplicated into the tested lib.
W1-054.reproPlan: Read-only proof trivial: evaluate the function with a close 23h away.

W1-055.title: createCatchupWithPeople has no server-side idempotency: a duplicated invocation mints two whole Catch-ups and double-notifies up to 100 people
W1-055.expected: Taxonomy 6c: for every 'create exactly one' action, a DB unique constraint is the real guard behind the disabled button. createCatchup (group-based) has it — Catchup.groupId is unique and P2002 is handled (actions.ts:366-372).
W1-055.actual: createCatchupWithPeople creates a brand-new Group each call, so no unique can fire: two executions of the same submission yield two private groups, two Catchups, two Round-1s, and two notifyQuestionsOpen fanouts to every invited member. The rate limit ('catchups: { tokens: 5, window: "1 h" }') admits both, and it fails open when Upstash blinks. The only guard is the client's `disabled={submitting}` — which covers the human double-click in practice but nothing else (a second tab, a replayed POST, a future second caller of the action).
W1-055.evidence: actions.ts:441-452: `const catchupId = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { const group = await tx.group.create({ data: { name, visibility: "private", creatorId, members: { create: memberRows } } ... }); const catchup = await tx.catchup.create({ data: { groupId: group.id, ... } });` — fresh group per call, so the groupId unique that protects createCatchup can never collide here. rate-limit.ts:75 shows the 5/h budget. The form's guard is client state only: `setSubmitting(true); const result = await createCatchupWithPeople({...})` with `disabled={submitting || !trimmedName}` (create-catchup-form.tsx:69-71,132).
W1-055.fixDirection: Lightweight server-side dedupe: before creating, refuse (returning the existing id) if this creator already created a Catchup with an identical group name within the last few minutes; or accept a client-generated idempotency key in the input and stash it on the Catchup row with a unique. Either turns a duplicate into a friendly no-op like createCatchup's raced branch.
W1-055.gateOrTest: Action test: two sequential identical calls within the window return the same catchupId (second one via the dedupe branch).

W1-056.title: Client components format Catch-up dates during SSR with server timezone/locale, guaranteeing hydration mismatches around IST midnights
W1-056.expected: A date rendered in a "use client" component should produce identical text on server and client, or be deliberately client-only.
W1-056.actual: console-published and archive-shelf call `toLocaleDateString("en-IN", {...})` and extend-deadline-card calls `toLocaleDateString(undefined, { weekday, day, month })` with no timeZone. During SSR these evaluate in the server's UTC (and, for the undefined locale, the server's ICU default rather than the member's), then hydrate to the browser's IST/locale. Whenever the timestamp falls 00:00-05:30 IST the server HTML shows the previous day: the member sees the wrong date flash (and React logs a hydration text mismatch) before it corrects. extend-deadline-card is the Keeper's 'Closes Tuesday 12 Aug' line — the fact the four extend buttons hang off — so the flash shows the wrong weekday exactly when it matters.
W1-056.evidence: console-published.tsx:31-36: `return new Date(iso).toLocaleDateString("en-IN", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" });` inside a file whose first line is "use client". extend-deadline-card.tsx:48-52: `return at.toLocaleDateString(undefined, { weekday: "long", day: "numeric", month: "short" });` — undefined locale + no timeZone in a "use client" file. Client components render on the server first in the App Router, so both halves execute.
W1-056.fixDirection: Same shared formatter as the server-component finding: fixed locale + timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata" makes server and client output byte-identical, killing both the mismatch and the flash. (suppressHydrationWarning would hide the warning but keep the wrong first paint; prefer the deterministic formatter.)
W1-056.gateOrTest: The shared-formatter unit test from the masthead finding covers this; optionally a dev-console check that no hydration warnings fire on /catchups/[id] with a 01:00-IST publishedAt.
W1-056.reproPlan: Orchestrator could reproduce read-only in dev chrome-devtools: load a Catch-up home whose publishedAt sits in the shifted window and read the hydration warning in the console.

W1-057.title: Purging (or admin-deleting/merging) a Catch-up creator's account cascades away the entire Catch-up: every Round, every member's published answers, permanently
W1-057.expected: A Catch-up survives its creator leaving. The schema comment says Catchup.createdById is 'nullable so the Catch-up survives if they leave' (SetNull); removal copy promises 'their words stay where they are'; spec 2.2 says published Rounds are 'readable forever'.
W1-057.actual: The hidden Group under every Catch-up is created with creatorId = the Catch-up creator, and Group.creatorId is onDelete: Cascade. prisma.user.delete (the 60-day retention purge, adminDeleteUser, and adminMergeUsers all end in it) deletes the Group, cascading Catchup (groupId Cascade) -> CatchupEdition -> CatchupPrompt -> CatchupEntry -> loves/prefs. Everyone else's published answers and the whole archive vanish. createdById SetNull is unreachable in practice because the Group dies first. Bonus damage: collectImageUrls() in account-purge.ts only collects the purged member's OWN entry images (catchupEntry.findMany where authorId=userId), so every other member's answer images in the cascaded rows become orphaned R2 bytes nothing can ever find again.
W1-057.evidence: schema.prisma:201 'creator  User @relation(fields: [creatorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)' on model Group; actions.ts:442-449 'const group = await tx.group.create({ data: { name, visibility: "private", creatorId, ... } })' with creatorId = session.user.id, then 'tx.catchup.create({ data: { groupId: group.id, ... } })'; schema.prisma:717 'group Group @relation(fields: [groupId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)' on Catchup, and CatchupEdition/Prompt/Entry each cascade down from there; account-purge.ts:99-102 'await prisma.$transaction([ prisma.report.deleteMany(...), prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } }) ])'; admin/people/actions.ts:315 'prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: sourceId } })' inside adminMergeUsers, which reassigns catchupPrompt/catchupEntry authorship (296-297) but never reassigns Group.creatorId, so the reassigned rows are cascade-deleted a statement later if the duplicate created the group.
W1-057.fixDirection: Change Group.creatorId to a nullable FK with onDelete: SetNull (mirroring Catchup.createdById), via a dated idempotent file in prisma/migrations-manual/ (ALTER COLUMN DROP NOT NULL + drop/re-add FK), and make purge/merge reassign or null creatorId first. Then implement the spec's 'any remaining member may re-adopt' rule or at least keep the group alive. Also make collectImageUrls collect images for ALL entries that will cascade (entries under editions of catchups on groups the user created), or stop the cascade so the question does not arise.
W1-057.gateOrTest: New unit/integration test: create user A, catchup via createCatchupWithPeople with member B, B submits an entry, purgeUserAccount(A), assert B's CatchupEntry and the CatchupEdition still exist. Pin the schema with a security-regressions-style test asserting Group.creatorId is not Cascade.
W1-057.reproPlan: code-argument-only (the live proof is destructive: it deletes real rows in the shared production database).

W1-058.title: Deleting any member's account cascades away every question they ever asked, taking every OTHER member's answers to it out of published Rounds
W1-058.expected: Account deletion removes the member's own content. Other members' answers in a published Round (a keepsake, 'readable forever') survive; a question with a gone asker can render as 'asked by someone who left'.
W1-058.actual: CatchupPrompt.authorId is onDelete: Cascade, and CatchupEntry.promptId is onDelete: Cascade. Purging member A deletes every prompt A authored in ANY catch-up (not just ones A created), which cascades every entry anyone wrote answering those prompts. In a 30-person Round where A asked one of the questions, 30 people's answers (text, photos, hearts) silently disappear from the published Round. The cascaded entries' images are also not collected by collectImageUrls (it only reads entries where authorId = the purged user), so those photos are stranded in R2.
W1-058.evidence: schema.prisma:765 'author  User @relation("CatchupPromptsAuthored", fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)'; schema.prisma:785 'prompt  CatchupPrompt @relation(fields: [promptId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)'; account-purge.ts:45 collects only 'prisma.catchupEntry.findMany({ where: { authorId: userId }, select: { images: true } })' before the delete at 101.
W1-058.fixDirection: Make CatchupPrompt.authorId nullable with onDelete: SetNull (migration in prisma/migrations-manual/), and teach the three asker-render sites (round page, loadPublishedIssue, home consoles) to render a null author as anonymous/'a member who left' (they already have a null-author branch for anonymity, so the render path exists). Alternatively reassign prompts to a tombstone user during purge.
W1-058.gateOrTest: Integration test: A asks a prompt, B answers it, purge A, assert B's entry still exists and the round renders the prompt with a null asker.
W1-058.reproPlan: code-argument-only (destructive against the shared production database).

W1-059.title: Pausing or ending a Catch-up does not stop the in-flight Round: it keeps advancing, keeps sending daily reminders, and publishes itself while the home shows only a paused/ended banner
W1-059.expected: After the Keeper pauses (or ends) a Catch-up, members stop being nudged and the live cycle visibly freezes (or, if 'the current round finishes' is the intended semantics, the home keeps showing the live console so members can still answer from it).
W1-059.actual: advanceDueCatchups selects live editions with no filter on catchup.status, and applyEditionAction only consults catchupStatus for setsNextOpensAt. So a paused/ended Catch-up's Round keeps auto-advancing collecting->answering->preparing->published, keeps firing catchup_answers_open/catchup_published to every member, and non-answerers keep receiving a DAILY catchup_reminder for the whole 7-10 day window. Meanwhile the home replaces the entire console with 'This Catch-up is paused.' (no Answer CTA, no question list), yet the page header still prints the live countdown ('{name} · 3 days left') above that banner, the notification links to /catchups/[id]/answer still work, and submitEntry accepts answers (it checks only membership + edition.status). Pause also does not stop the clock: a Keeper pausing mid-answering to 'freeze' silently loses the window, and resume does not shift deadlines.
W1-059.evidence: catchups.ts:956-963 'const editions = await prisma.catchupEdition.findMany({ where: { status: { in: ["collecting", "answering", "preparing"] }, catchup: scope } ...' where scope filters only membership; catchups.ts:802 'if (action.setsNextOpensAt && meta.catchupStatus === "active")' is the ONLY status check in applyEditionAction, and the reminder branch at 826-833 fires notify.notifyReminder unconditionally; catchup-home-shell.tsx:57-63 'catchupStatus !== "active" ? <PausedOrEndedBanner .../>' replaces the whole left console; [catchupId]/page.tsx:512-516 header title uses result.edition?.countdownLabel with no catchupStatus guard; actions.ts submitEntry 1115-1121 checks membership and edition.status !== "answering" but never edition.catchup.status; answer/page.tsx has no catchup.status check either. The banner's own copy 'No new Round opens until it is resumed' admits pause only gates openNextRoundIfDue.
W1-059.fixDirection: Decide the semantics and enforce them in one place: either (a) exclude paused/ended catchups from advanceDueCatchups' edition query and from advanceEdition (freeze), shifting deadlines by the pause duration on resume; or (b) let the current Round finish but keep rendering the live console + countdown under a slim paused banner and keep reminders consistent with what the page shows. Also gate submitEntry and the /answer page on catchup.status if (a).
W1-059.gateOrTest: Unit test on planNextAction/advanceEdition with a paused catchup asserting no transition and no reminder fires; e2e: pause mid-answering, assert no new notification rows appear after a simulated day.
W1-059.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev: pause a test catch-up mid-answering, set answersCloseAt into the past via a test row, load any page as another member, read the Notification table (read-only inspection) and the home page.

W1-060.title: A Catch-up nobody adds questions to still runs the full cycle forever: answering opens with zero questions, everyone gets daily reminders to answer nothing, an empty Round publishes, and the next Round opens on cadence, repeating monthly for eternity
W1-060.expected: A Round with no accepted questions should not open answering on the clock (there is nothing to answer), should not nudge every member daily about it, and should not publish an empty keepsake; an abandoned Catch-up should quiesce, not loop.
W1-060.actual: computeStatus/planNextAction advance collecting->answering purely on questionsCloseAt with no prompt-count guard, firing catchup_answers_open to all members. With zero prompts nobody CAN answer, so every member is a non-answerer and receives a daily catchup_reminder for the 7-day window; at close, the too-few rule extends once (+3 more days of dailies, another answers-open blast), then it publishes an empty Round ('This Round did not gather any questions.') and notifies 'ready to read'. openNextRoundIfDue only requires latest.status === 'published', so a fresh empty Round opens next cadence and the whole loop repeats forever until a human ends the catch-up. The /answer page's zero-prompt state even says 'Check back once the Keeper has added a few questions' during answering, when adding questions is impossible (submitPrompt requires status collecting). Note the UI knows better: OpenAnsweringButton only renders when a prompt exists (shell line 121-125), but the clock path has no such guard.
W1-060.evidence: catchups.ts:505-514 'if (next === "answering") { return { kind: "transition", ..., patch: answeringPatch(ed, now), notify: "catchup_answers_open" ... } }' with no prompt count in scope (planNextAction's inputs are timing + entryCount only); catchups.ts:908-913 'if (!latest || latest.status !== "published") return;' is openNextRoundIfDue's only content gate; catchups-notify.ts:139-141 non-answerers = all members when entries are zero; answer/page.tsx:199-207 zero-prompt card copy 'Check back once the Keeper has added a few questions to answer.' while edition.status === 'answering'; actions.ts:692-694 submitPrompt refuses when status !== 'collecting'.
W1-060.fixDirection: In planNextAction (or advanceEdition, which already counts entries lazily), when the collecting window lapses with zero accepted prompts, either extend the question window once (mirroring the too-few-answers rule) and then auto-pause the catchup, or skip straight to a quiet no-op state that never notifies; and make openNextRoundIfDue refuse (or auto-pause) after publishing an edition with zero entries, so an abandoned catch-up goes dormant instead of looping. Fix the /answer zero-prompt copy to not promise an impossible action.
W1-060.gateOrTest: Unit tests on planNextAction: (collecting, 0 prompts, past close) does not transition to answering / does not notify; (published empty, nextOpensAt past) does not open the next Round.
W1-060.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev with a test catch-up: create one, add no questions, backdate questionsCloseAt, load a page, inspect edition.status and Notification rows (read-only after setup).

W1-061.title: A member cannot leave a Catch-up, and enrolment is unilateral: anyone can be added by a Keeper and then receives cycle notifications forever with no self-service exit
W1-061.expected: Someone enrolled in a Catch-up (they never accepted an invite; createCatchupWithPeople and addCatchupMembers enrol up to 100 people without consent) can remove themselves, or at minimum silence it completely.
W1-061.actual: The only membership-removal path is removeCatchupMember, which is Keeper-only (loadKeeperScope) and explicitly refuses self-removal ('You cannot remove yourself.'); no leave/exit action exists anywhere in the feature (the only groupMember.deleteMany in the app is that Keeper action). The reminder pref 'off' silences only the daily catchup_reminder, and even that is bypassed by Keeper nudges (bypassOff); catchup_questions_open, catchup_answers_open and catchup_published go to ALL group members unconditionally, every cycle, on a recurring cadence, forever. So a member who wants out of a monthly catch-up they were added to must personally ask a Keeper, and until then keeps being notified monthly for life.
W1-061.evidence: actions.ts:1355 'if (userId === session.user.id) return { error: "You cannot remove yourself." };' inside the Keeper-gated removeCatchupMember; grep confirms no other groupMember delete in src/ outside demo seed; catchups-notify.ts:82-93 notifyQuestionsOpen and 177-188 notifyPublished derive recipients from groupMemberIds with no pref filter; 142 'if (!ctx.bypassOff)' shows the off pref is skipped for Keeper nudges; actions.ts:420-434 createCatchupWithPeople enrols invitedIds directly as GroupMember rows with no acceptance step.
W1-061.fixDirection: Add a leaveCatchup(catchupId) server action: auth + membership check, refuse only when the caller is the creator (offer end/handover instead), delete own GroupMember row and own pending catchup notifications, revalidate. Surface it in PeoplePanel ('Leave this Catch-up'). Optionally make questions_open/answers_open/published respect reminderMode 'off' as a full mute.
W1-061.gateOrTest: Unit test on the new action (member can leave; creator refused; notifications cleared); e2e: leave, assert home shows the not-member card.
W1-061.reproPlan: code-argument-only until the action exists; the absence is provable by grep.

W1-062.title: Anonymous question askers are unmasked to Keepers in published Rounds with no visual cue, while being hidden from the same Keepers during collecting, when curation actually needs it
W1-062.expected: One consistent anonymity rule. Either 'showAsker=false hides the asker from everyone in the UI' (what the 'Ask anonymously' toggle implies and what the home's own comment demands: 'never send another member's identity for a question they asked anonymously'), or Keeper-visibility everywhere, clearly labelled as Keeper-only.
W1-062.actual: Two contradictory rules ship. During collecting/answering the home sends author: null unless showAsker or isOwn, so even Keepers see 'Someone in the group' while deciding what to remove. But once published, both the round reader and the home's inline issue compute askerVisible = p.showAsker || keeper and render a plain 'asked by {name}' with the asker's avatar, identical to a named question. A Keeper (including anyone later handed the hat via setCatchupKeeper) has no way to know this identity is private to them, and can casually out the anonymous asker in conversation or a screenshot. The unmask also reaches co-Keepers who were not moderating anything.
W1-062.evidence: round/[editionId]/page.tsx:295 'const askerVisible = p.showAsker || keeper;' and [catchupId]/page.tsx:150 'const askerVisible = p.showAsker || isKeeper;' (published paths) versus [catchupId]/page.tsx:318-319 comment 'Anonymity boundary: never send another member's identity for a question they asked anonymously' and line 331 'const revealAsker = p.showAsker || isOwn;' (collecting path). question-section.tsx:91-108 renders prompt.asker with no keeper-only marker. catchups-types.ts:132 documents the keeper unmask as intended, directly contradicting the home comment.
W1-062.fixDirection: Pick one rule. Simplest and safest: drop '|| keeper' from both published-path askerVisible computations so anonymity is absolute in the UI (authorId stays stored for admin moderation). If Keeper visibility is truly wanted, apply it in collecting too and render a distinct '(visible only to you as Keeper)' treatment in QuestionSection/AnswerCard so it cannot be mistaken for public attribution.
W1-062.gateOrTest: Unit test on the section-building code: showAsker=false + keeper viewer yields asker null (or the labelled variant); e2e reading a published round as keeper.
W1-062.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev: submit an anonymous question in a test catch-up, publish, view as the Keeper and as a plain member; compare the 'asked by' line.

W1-063.title: Published/next-Round dates render in server UTC, so members in IST see the wrong calendar day for anything that happens between midnight and 5:30am IST
W1-063.expected: 'Published 21 August' and 'Next Round opens {date}' match the member's calendar (all members are IST, UTC+5:30).
W1-063.actual: RoundMasthead, RoundFooterTease and FreshOffThePress are server components (no 'use client'), so toLocaleDateString with no timeZone runs on the UTC server: a Round published at 00:30 IST on the 21st prints 'Published 20 August' for everyone, permanently; 'Next Round opens' can likewise show the previous day. Window times inherit the creation/open hour, so any catch-up whose Keeper acts between 00:00 and 05:30 IST (late-night usage is normal for alumni) has EVERY subsequent date in this band. The client-side copies (ConsolePublished en-IN, ArchiveShelf, ExtendDeadlineCard's closesLine) SSR with the UTC value then hydrate with the browser value, producing a hydration text mismatch plus a visible day flicker in the same band, and the two surfaces (masthead vs console) can disagree about the same Round's date.
W1-063.evidence: masthead.tsx:49-55 'const dateLabel = publishedAt ? new Date(publishedAt).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" }) : null;' in a file with no 'use client'; footer-tease.tsx:24-31 same pattern for nextOpensAt; fresh-off-the-press.tsx:21-24 same with en-US; console-published.tsx:30-37 and archive-shelf.tsx:19-22 are 'use client' so they SSR-UTC/hydrate-IST. Servers run UTC (audit brief), members IST.
W1-063.fixDirection: Format all Catch-up dates with an explicit timeZone: 'Asia/Kolkata' (the spec's 'single community timezone' fence makes this legitimate), ideally via one shared helper in lib so masthead/footer/rail/archive/console cannot drift; that also makes SSR and hydration agree for the client components.
W1-063.gateOrTest: Unit test on the shared formatter: an ISO instant at 19:30Z prints the next IST day. Visual suite covers the render.
W1-063.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev: publish a test round with publishedAt set to ~20:00Z and read the masthead.

W1-064.title: Catch-up home archive is an N+1 that fetches every entry body of every published Round on every home view; the index rail similarly over-fetches all entries of 6 editions
W1-064.expected: Computing a 140-char teaser and a contributor count per archived Round costs a bounded query, not one sequential full-table pull per Round growing linearly with the catch-up's age.
W1-064.actual: loadHome loops 'for (const ed of publishedEditions) { const entries = await prisma.catchupEntry.findMany({ where: { editionId: ed.id }, select: { authorId: true, body: true, _count: {...} } }) }' - sequential awaits, one query per published Round, each fetching EVERY entry's full body (up to 6000 chars each) just to pick the most-loved teaser. A 2-year-old monthly catch-up with 100 members and ~15 questions/Round means 24 sequential queries moving up to ~36k rows of prose on every single home visit, added to page latency. The index's freshEditions query has the same shape (entries with body, no take, for 6 editions) once per index view. At 2,000 users this is the page members hit most.
W1-064.evidence: [catchupId]/page.tsx:374-396 the for-await loop quoted above (note also publishedEditions itself has no take); catchups/page.tsx:199-213 'entries: { select: { authorId: true, body: true, _count: { select: { loves: true } } } }' nested with no take inside the freshEditions findMany.
W1-064.fixDirection: Compute teasers at publish time (store teaser + contributorCount on CatchupEdition when it publishes - publishNow/applyEditionAction are the two writers), or replace the loop with one groupBy for contributor counts plus one query fetching only the top-loved entry per edition (orderBy loves count, take 1 per edition via a raw query or per-edition take inside a single include). At minimum, Promise.all the loop and select a truncated substring instead of full bodies.
W1-064.gateOrTest: A query-count assertion in a unit/integration test around loadHome (e.g. Prisma query event counter: home view issues O(1) archive queries regardless of published count).
W1-064.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev with Prisma query logging while loading a catch-up home that has several published rounds.

W1-065.title: Answering UI marks a question 'shared' and shows the completion card even when the save failed, so a member can leave believing an unsaved answer was submitted
W1-065.expected: The progress ring, the per-question check, and 'That is you in this Round.' reflect what the server actually stored; a failed autosave leaves the question visibly unsaved.
W1-065.actual: handleBodyBlur calls updateEntry(promptId, { body }) BEFORE the async persist, and a persist error only toasts and resets saveStatus to idle - the optimistic entries state is never rolled back. answeredIds (which drives the rail checks, the ring, the mobile dots, and the CompletionCard's 'That is you in this Round') is computed from that local entries state. So when submitEntry fails - body over the 6000-char Zod cap ('Keep it under 6000 characters.'), the window auto-closing at answersCloseAt mid-session ('Answering is not open...'), the member having been removed, or a network drop - the question still turns green, the count still increments, and finishing shows the completion moment while the server has nothing. A sonner toast is the only counter-signal and is easy to miss on mobile; closing the tab loses the text entirely (drafts live only in client state).
W1-065.evidence: answer-experience.tsx:104-107 'function handleBodyBlur(promptId, body) { updateEntry(promptId, { body }); void persist(promptId, { body }); }' and persist's error branch (96-99) only toasts + sets saveStatus idle, never reverts entries; 51-55 'answeredIds' derives from entries via isMeaningfulEntry; completion-card.tsx:48 'answeredCount > 0 ? "That is you in this Round."'. handleImagesChange has the same shape (109-112).
W1-065.fixDirection: Track per-prompt saved-vs-draft state: only add a prompt to answeredIds when its last persist resolved success (e.g. keep a savedEntries map updated in persist's success branch and derive answeredIds from it), and render a visible failed-save state on the card/rail row (red dot + retry) instead of relying on a toast. Enforce the 6000 cap in the editor (live counter) so the common failure cannot occur.
W1-065.gateOrTest: Component test: persist rejection leaves the rail row unchecked and completion card unreachable; e2e with a stubbed failing action.
W1-065.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev: type >6000 chars into an answer, blur, watch the rail tick green while the toast reports the rejection; reload to see the empty entry.

W1-066.title: adminMergeUsers aborts wholesale when both accounts answered the same Catch-up prompt, and silently drops the survivor from every Catch-up the duplicate belonged to
W1-066.expected: Merging duplicate accounts preserves catch-up participation: entries dedupe like the other unique-keyed engagement, and the surviving account keeps the duplicate's memberships.
W1-066.actual: Two defects. (1) 'prisma.catchupEntry.updateMany({ where: { authorId: sourceId }, data: { authorId: targetId } })' violates @@unique([promptId, authorId]) the moment both accounts answered the same prompt, aborting the entire merge transaction with 'Could not merge those accounts.' - exactly the duplicate-account pair most likely to exist (one human, both accounts in the same batch catch-up). (2) GroupMember is in neither the kept nor the dropped list, so the source's memberships die in the user.delete cascade and the target is never enrolled: after a merge, the person silently vanishes from every catch-up (and its notifications) that only the duplicate was in, while their reassigned prompts/entries remain inside rounds they can no longer open.
W1-066.evidence: admin/people/actions.ts:290-316 transaction: kept list has catchupPrompt/catchupEntry updateMany (296-297) but no groupMember reassignment; dropped list (302-309) deletes loves/prefs but not memberships; user.delete at 315 cascades GroupMember (schema @@unique(groupId,userId) plus onDelete: Cascade on user). schema.prisma:789 '@@unique([promptId, authorId])' is what the entry updateMany trips.
W1-066.fixDirection: Before the updateManys: delete source entries whose (promptId, targetId) already exists (keep the target's), then reassign the rest; and add 'reassign GroupMember where no (groupId, targetId) row exists, else delete' using createMany skipDuplicates + deleteMany, keeping it inside the one transaction.
W1-066.gateOrTest: Integration test: two users answer the same prompt and share a group; merge succeeds, one entry survives, target is a member of the group.
W1-066.reproPlan: code-argument-only (merge is destructive on the shared database).

W1-067.title: 'Everyone from my batch' can hand the create form more than 100 people, and submission then fails flat against the max-100 cap with no guidance

W1-069.title: Rapid double-click on the love heart can strand the UI out of sync with the database and surface 'Something went wrong' for a benign race
W1-069.expected: toggleEntryLove is idempotent under the double-fire every button gets; the @@unique constraint outcome is absorbed, not surfaced as an error.
W1-069.actual: The action is read-then-write: findUnique then create or delete-by-id, with no P2002/P2025 handling of its own, so two overlapping toggles race. Concurrent creates: the loser throws P2002, runAction returns the generic 'Something went wrong. Please try again.', and the client rolls back its optimistic flip - toast + count flicker for a state that is actually fine. Concurrent deletes: the loser throws P2025 on the stale id, same toast, and the rollback leaves the button showing loved while the row is gone until a reload. EntryLoveButton has no in-flight guard (handleToggle is not disabled while awaiting).
W1-069.evidence: actions.ts:1213-1233 'const existing = await prisma.catchupEntryLove.findUnique(...); if (existing) { await prisma.catchupEntryLove.delete({ where: { id: existing.id } }); } else { await prisma.catchupEntryLove.create(...)' - no unique/not-found catch (isUniqueConstraintError exists in the file but is unused here); entry-love-button.tsx:30-40 optimistic flip + rollback on any error, no busy guard.
W1-069.fixDirection: Treat P2002 as 'already loved' and P2025 as 'already unloved' (return success with the settled state instead of an error), or replace with deleteMany/createMany+skipDuplicates keyed on the unique; optionally ignore clicks while a toggle is in flight in EntryLoveButton.
W1-069.gateOrTest: Unit test invoking the action twice concurrently for both directions, asserting neither returns an error.
W1-069.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev: throttle the network in devtools and double-click a heart on a published round.

W1-070.title: Invite flow dead-ends for brand-new signups at the Stage-2 gate with a message about 'posting', and the invite context is lost by the time they are verified
W1-070.expected: The owner's stated flow: 'if they don't have an account, it takes you through the entire process and then brings you to catch ups' - ending in a join, or at least in a message that explains what happens next for THIS invite.

W1-071.title: Concurrent question submissions produce duplicate positions and can overshoot the 40-question ceiling (count-then-insert TOCTOU)
W1-071.expected: Each accepted prompt gets a distinct position and the MAX_ACCEPTED_PROMPTS_PER_EDITION cap holds under concurrency.
W1-071.actual: submitPrompt does 'const acceptedCount = await prisma.catchupPrompt.count(...)' then creates with 'position: acceptedCount' - two members submitting in the same instant both read N and both write position N, so the Round's order has a tie that renders in arbitrary DB order (both list surfaces sort by position alone) and flips between loads until a Keeper reorders. The same read-then-write lets the count pass at 39 twice, landing 41 accepted prompts past the cap; the reorder schema (max 40 ids) then rejects any reorder of that Round with 'Invalid request.' until one is removed. Low because the cap is a runaway guard and duplicate positions self-heal on reorder, but the arbitrary flip is member-visible.
W1-071.evidence: actions.ts:707-712 count + cap check; 714-724 create with 'position: acceptedCount'; ordering consumers sort only by position ([catchupId]/page.tsx:322-324 '.sort((a, b) => a.position - b.position)'; round reader orderBy position asc); curateReorderSchema max is MAX_ACCEPTED_PROMPTS_PER_EDITION (actions.ts:143).
W1-071.fixDirection: Compute position in the insert itself (raw INSERT ... SELECT COALESCE(MAX(position)+1,0), or use createdAt as the tiebreaker in every orderBy: [position, createdAt]), and either accept mild cap overshoot explicitly or move the cap check into the same statement.
W1-071.gateOrTest: Unit/integration test firing two submitPrompt calls concurrently and asserting distinct positions.
W1-071.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev by dispatching two submissions in parallel against a test round and reading the two rows.

W1-072.title: recordView on the round reader is fire-and-forget during a serverless render, so round-view telemetry is silently lossy in production
W1-072.expected: Work that must outlive the response on Vercel goes through after()/waitUntil (the codebase already does this for drainMailQueue in (main)/layout.tsx:63).

W1-072.reproPlan: code-argument-only (loss is probabilistic on Vercel's freeze timing; not reproducible locally).

W1-073.title: A member who erases their answer still publishes as an empty card and is counted in 'N of the group wrote in'; there is no way to withdraw an answer before the Round seals
W1-073.expected: Clearing everything you wrote before answers close withdraws you from the Round: no card, not counted as a contributor, and the too-few-answers rule sees the true count.
W1-073.actual: submitEntry upserts; clearing a field nulls it but the CatchupEntry row is never deleted, and no delete path exists. A member who wrote something personal and then erased every field before close is still published: an answer card reading 'Showed up for this Round without adding anything here.', their bird in the masthead strip, and inclusion in the contributor count ('12 of the group wrote in' can include people who wrote nothing). The empty row also counts as an entry for shouldExtendForTooFew (entryCount is a bare count), so a Round whose only 'entry' is an erased one skips the zero-answers extension and publishes with nothing readable. The 'Showed up' copy shows empty cards were anticipated, but as a state you can end up trapped in, not choose.
W1-073.evidence: actions.ts:1160-1178 upsert with update-only-sent-fields, no delete branch anywhere in the file for entries; round page 335-341 contributorMap iterates ALL entries including empty ones; answer-card.tsx:93-96 the 'Showed up for this Round without adding anything here.' branch; actions.ts:907 'const entryCount = await prisma.catchupEntry.count({ where: { editionId } })' and catchups.ts:382-384 shouldExtendForTooFew uses that raw count.
W1-073.fixDirection: In submitEntry, delete the row when the update leaves body, images, and song all null (one post-update check inside the same call), which fixes withdrawal, the contributor count, and the too-few evaluation at once. Alternatively filter meaningless entries out of contributors/counts at read time and in the entryCount query.
W1-073.gateOrTest: Unit test: save then clear an answer, assert the row is gone and the member is absent from the published contributors.
W1-073.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev: answer, erase, publish a test round, read the masthead count and the empty card.

W1-074.title: Autosave has no ordering guarantee: a slow earlier save can overwrite a newer one after the member saw 'Saved'
W1-074.expected: The last thing the member typed is what persists; concurrent saves of the same field resolve newest-wins.
W1-074.actual: persist() fires submitEntry per blur with no sequence number, no abort of the in-flight save, and no per-prompt queue. Two blurs on the same prompt in quick succession (edit, blur, refocus, fix a typo, blur) put two upserts in flight; server actions can complete out of order (separate lambdas), so save A (older body) can commit after save B (newer body), silently persisting the typo'd version while the UI shows the corrected text and 'Saved'. The two-tab variant of the same class also applies (each tab's blur last-writes its own stale field). Field-level patches limit the blast to one field. Suspected: the code has no defense, but the window needs out-of-order completion to manifest.
W1-074.evidence: answer-experience.tsx:93-102 'async function persist(promptId, patch) { setSaveStatus(..."saving"); const result = await submitEntry({ promptId, ...patch }); ... }' - no versioning, no serialization; answer-card.tsx flushBody only dedupes identical values, not orderings; actions.ts submitEntry upsert applies whatever it was sent.
W1-074.fixDirection: Serialize saves per prompt client-side (a per-prompt promise chain, or drop the in-flight save when a newer one starts), which is sufficient for a single-author row; a monotonic client sequence echoed through the action and compared in the update would harden the two-tab case.
W1-074.gateOrTest: Component test with two stubbed submitEntry calls resolving in reverse order, asserting the final persisted payload is the newer body.
W1-074.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev with devtools request blocking: hold the first save, let the second land, release the first, reload and read the row.

W1-075.title: Teasers slice raw markdown mid-character: formatting markers print verbatim and a cut inside an emoji/surrogate pair renders a broken glyph
W1-075.expected: The archive/rail teaser ('a one-line teaser pulled from the most-loved answer') reads as prose.
W1-075.actual: Answer bodies are markdown (RichTextArea writes markers; the reader honours them via renderRichText), but both teaser builders slice the raw body: truncate() at page.tsx:55 ('clean.slice(0, max)') and the home archive's 'top.body.slice(0, 140)'. A bolded most-loved answer shows '**We finally moved to...' in the rail, and String.prototype.slice cuts UTF-16 units, so a boundary landing inside an emoji or ZWJ sequence prints U+FFFD. Cosmetic-with-teeth: it sits on the index rail, the most-seen catch-ups surface.
W1-075.evidence: page.tsx:55-58 truncate() slicing raw body chosen at 215-227 from e.body; [catchupId]/page.tsx:384-388 'top.body.length > 140 ? `${top.body.slice(0, 140).trimEnd()}...`'; answer-card.tsx:100-106 shows bodies are markdown rendered with renderRichText elsewhere.
W1-075.fixDirection: Strip markdown markers before truncating (a tiny stripRichText helper next to renderRichText) and slice with Array.from(clean).slice(0, max).join('') or Intl.Segmenter to respect grapheme boundaries; share the one helper between both call sites.
W1-075.gateOrTest: Unit test on the shared teaser helper with a bolded body and an emoji at the boundary.
W1-075.reproPlan: Live-provable in dev: love an answer containing bold text + emoji past position 110 and read the index rail.

W1-076.title: "Most loved" sort has no deterministic tiebreaker, so offset pagination duplicates and drops photos (and produces duplicate React keys)
W1-076.expected: Sorting by "Most loved" and pressing Load more walks the collection exactly once: every approved photo appears once across pages.
W1-076.actual: Rows tied on love count (which is almost all of them: most photos have 0-2 loves) are returned in arbitrary, non-stable order per query. Page 2 (skip 24) re-runs the sort and can return rows already shown on page 1 and omit others. The client appends with setPhotos(prev => [...prev, ...data.photos]) keyed by key={p.id}, so duplicates also collide as React keys.
W1-076.evidence: actions.ts:466-471: `const orderBy = opts?.sortBy === "oldest" ? { createdAt: "asc" as const } : opts?.sortBy === "loved" ? { loves: { _count: "desc" as const } } : { createdAt: "desc" as const };` then 473-480: `prisma.photo.findMany({ where, include: includeFor(...), orderBy, take: PAGE_SIZE + 1, skip: page * PAGE_SIZE })`. For "loved" the ONLY sort key is the aggregate count; Postgres gives no stable order for ties, and each page is a fresh query, so tied rows shuffle between pages. collection-client.tsx:399-402 renders `photos.map((p, i) => (<Tile key={p.id} ...>))` after handleLoadMore's `setPhotos((prev) => [...prev, ...data.photos])` (line 167), so a repeated id is a duplicate key. Reachable the moment the collection holds more than PAGE_SIZE=24 approved photos and someone opens the "Most loved" sort and loads more. ("newest"/"oldest" sort on createdAt is also un-tiebroken but ms-precision ties are rare; the loved sort is tied by construction.)
W1-076.fixDirection: Add a secondary deterministic key to every orderBy in loadPhotos, e.g. orderBy: [{ loves: { _count: "desc" } }, { createdAt: "desc" }, { id: "desc" }] (and [{ createdAt }, { id }] for newest/oldest). Optionally dedupe by id in handleLoadMore as a belt (`const seen = new Set(prev.map(p=>p.id))`).
W1-076.gateOrTest: New unit/e2e test: seed 25+ photos with equal love counts, fetch page 0 and page 1 via loadPhotos({sortBy:"loved"}), assert the id sets are disjoint and their union covers take*2 distinct rows.
W1-076.reproPlan: Live proof possible read-only once >24 approved photos exist: open /collection, sort Most loved, Load more, look for repeated tiles / React duplicate-key console warning. Until then: code-argument-only.

W1-077.title: Direct-upload staged originals (full-EXIF, GPS-bearing) leak permanently in R2: several refusal paths skip cleanup and no sweep exists for abandoned/crashed uploads
W1-077.expected: A presigned original staged under collection/<id>/...-o.jpg or staging/<id>/... either becomes a photo (and is deleted) or is cleaned up; nothing EXIF-bearing sits at a public URL indefinitely, and storage cost does not accrete from abandoned uploads.
W1-077.actual: The raw original (which still carries EXIF/GPS — the exact thing audit M12 re-encodes to remove, per the comment at actions.ts:243-248 "a phone photo's EXIF carries the GPS coordinates... serving the untouched original published those") stays in the bucket forever, publicly fetchable at its R2 URL, whenever: (a) contributePhotoDirect is refused by the rate limiter, (b) contributePhotoDirect is refused by Zod validation, (c) /api/upload/finalize 429s before reading keys, (d) the member closes the tab between the PUT and the finalize/contribute call (the everyday case), or (e) the function crashes/times out mid-processing. There is no lifecycle sweep: vercel.json's only crons are /api/catchups/tick and /api/demo/reset, and `staging` appears only in presign/finalize/storage.ts.
