W1-107.evidence: collection/actions.ts:131-132: `if (file.size > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES) { return { error: \`Photo is over the 20MB limit...\` }; }` — a check that can never run on Vercel for the 4.5-20MB range because the platform rejects the body first. next.config.ts:111-122 raises only Next's own limits. contribute-dialog.tsx:126-144: `if (staged) { result = await contributePhotoDirect({...}) } else { const fd = new FormData(); fd.set("file", file); ... result = await contributePhoto(fd); }` — the >4.5MB fallback path is reachable whenever presign is unavailable, and its failure surfaces as the generic error at lines 149-157.
W1-107.fixDirection: Two-part: (1) operational — finish the R2 bucket CORS rule (the known blocked task) so the direct path actually works from the production origin; verify with a >5MB upload from a phone. (2) code — in the fallback branch, check `file.size` CLIENT-side against ~4MB before building the FormData and show a specific message ("this photo is too large to send the slow way; try again shortly / resize"), so the platform 413 is never the member's first signal. Optionally detect the 413 (the thrown action error) and name the size cause explicitly.
W1-107.gateOrTest: Playwright spec (after live confirmation, per house rules) uploading a 6MB fixture through the dialog against a preview deployment: asserts either direct-path success or the specific size message — never the generic connection toast.
W1-107.reproPlan: Live, safe on the real app with a test account: open the Collection contribute dialog on production with DevTools network tab, attempt an ~8MB JPG; observe whether the PUT goes to R2 (CORS fixed) or a POST to the page returns 413 (fallback + cap). No data is written on the failing path.

W1-108.title: Nine fire-and-forget database writes rely on post-response execution without after()/waitUntil, so on serverless they are stochastically frozen mid-flight: telemetry rows (SearchLog, ContentView, LoginAttempt) and the AuthToken sweep silently under-record
W1-108.expected: "Not awaited so it never blocks" writes still eventually commit — the mental model in the comments (e.g. auth-tokens.ts:105 "a slow delete never holds up the mail") is background execution.
W1-108.actual: On Vercel, once the response completes, execution not registered via after()/waitUntil may be frozen; a `void somePrismaCall()` immediately before `return NextResponse.json(...)` (places/users search route handlers) has essentially zero guaranteed runway, and the in-render `void recordView(...)`/`void logSearch(...)` calls in four pages only survive if the remaining render outlasts their 1-3 round trips. The codebase already knows the correct tool — the layout wraps drainMailQueue in `after()` (layout.tsx:63) precisely because "it must run AFTER the response has been streamed" — but these nine sites do not use it. Consequences are bounded and silent by design: lost SearchLog rows (the owner's "most common searches" answer skews), lost ContentView increments (profile/letter view counts under-read), lost LoginAttempt rows (the admin analytics login-health view undercounts, including the failure reasons it exists to surface), and an AuthToken expiry sweep that fires less often than intended (table growth only — the weekly-past-expiry rows are also cleared by consumption paths). All are telemetry/cleanup; none corrupts member-facing state, hence Low — but it is the taxonomy's missing-await row and the comments show the survivability assumption is wrong, so it should be a deliberate decision rather than an accident.

W1-109.title: Admin analytics rhythm heatmap applies AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata' in the wrong direction, shifting every hour bucket by -11 hours
W1-109.expected: loadRhythm() buckets visits into IST hour-of-day and weekday, so the 8pm IST evening rush shows at hour 20; the code comment states this is the whole point: "IST, not UTC ... a UTC heatmap would put the evening rush at 2pm and make the whole thing meaningless."
W1-109.actual: Every bucket is shifted -11 hours (and DOW shifts across the boundary). A visit at 20:00 IST is stored as naive 14:30 (UTC wall time, since Visit.endedAt is TIMESTAMP(3) without time zone); `"endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'` INTERPRETS that naive 14:30 as IST wall time, producing the instant 09:00 UTC; EXTRACT(HOUR FROM timestamptz) then converts using the session TimeZone (UTC on Supabase, node-postgres never sets one), yielding hour 9. The 5:30 offset is applied twice in the wrong direction instead of once forward. The heatmap and its "peak" tile are systematically wrong yet look plausible, which is worse than obviously broken: the owner built this to decide when the community is awake.
W1-109.evidence: src/lib/admin-analytics.ts:583-585: `SELECT EXTRACT(DOW  FROM "endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::int AS dow, EXTRACT(HOUR FROM "endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::int AS hour`. The column is naive: prisma/migrations-manual/2026-08-19-presence.sql:18: `"endedAt"   TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` — and Prisma writes UTC wall-time into naive columns (bugs.md item 6 documents the app's columns are `timestamp without time zone`). Postgres semantics: naive AT TIME ZONE zone = "interpret this wall time as being IN zone, return timestamptz"; EXTRACT on a timestamptz renders in the session TimeZone first. So stored 14:30 (true instant 14:30 UTC = 20:00 IST) → interpreted as 14:30 IST → 09:00 UTC instant → EXTRACT under UTC session = 9. Correct value is 20; the correct expression needs the naive value anchored to UTC first.
W1-109.fixDirection: Change both expressions to double conversion: `EXTRACT(DOW FROM ("endedAt" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')` (same for HOUR). The inner AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' turns the naive UTC wall time into a real timestamptz; the outer one converts it to IST wall time (a naive value, on which EXTRACT is session-independent).
W1-109.gateOrTest: A node --test unit in the src/lib/*.test.mjs style cannot run SQL; instead pin it with a read-only SQL assertion in a script test or add a JS-side sanity check: insert-free — SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (TIMESTAMP '2026-08-21 14:30:00' AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') must be 20. At minimum, a comment-pinned example in loadRhythm and a one-off verification query in the fix session.
W1-109.reproPlan: Read-only: run `SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM TIMESTAMP '2026-08-21 14:30:00' AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') AT TIME ZONE ...` — concretely, `SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (TIMESTAMP '2026-08-21 14:30:00') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') AS wrong, EXTRACT(HOUR FROM ((TIMESTAMP '2026-08-21 14:30:00') AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') AS right;` via a read-only session — expect wrong=9, right=20. No table access needed.

W1-122.title: drainMailQueue can never select 'deletion-scheduled' rows: the account-deletion confirmation/takeover-alarm email is queued and never sent

W1-122.actual: The ONLY selector that pulls rows out of the queue filters on kind IN eligibleKinds, and eligibleKinds is always either ["verify", "reset", "password-changed"] or ["reset", "password-changed"]. 'deletion-scheduled' appears in neither list, so the row sits status='queued' forever. The member never gets the written confirmation, a victim of an account takeover never gets the alarm during the 60-day window in which sign-in undoes the deletion, and mailHealth/backlog counts the stuck row as 'waiting' permanently.

But inside drainMailQueue: `const eligibleKinds = live.verifyRemaining > 0 ? ["verify", "reset", "password-changed"] : ["reset", "password-changed"];` followed by `const next = await prisma.outboundEmail.findFirst({ where: { status: "queued", kind: { in: eligibleKinds }, ... } })`. Every send path funnels here: enqueueMail calls scheduleDrain() (line 350) which calls drainMailQueue; the (main) layout's after() calls drainMailQueue; verificationMailState only fast-paths kind='verify' rows. W1-122.fixDirection: Add "deletion-scheduled" to both branches of eligibleKinds (it is a security notice, so it belongs beside "reset" and "password-changed" in the reserve-only branch too). Then sweep existing stuck rows: any OutboundEmail with kind='deletion-scheduled' and status='queued' will start draining on the next page view once deployed.
W1-122.gateOrTest: A unit test in src/lib (mjs, alongside gate-coverage.test.mjs) asserting every member of MailKind is selectable by the drain filter — i.e. the union of the two eligibleKinds arrays equals the MailKind set — so the next added kind cannot silently strand either.

W1-123.title: All 12 /admin pages rely solely on the layout gate, which does not run on page-segment RSC requests: demoted admins keep reading admin data during a session, and a crafted router-state request may fetch admin page data with only a member session
W1-123.expected: Every admin page render re-establishes that the requester is an admin before returning member emails, verification states, login attempts, audit rows, reports and analytics.
W1-123.actual: requireAdminPage() runs only in admin/layout.tsx. Grep confirms none of the 12 admin page.tsx files (nor their query helpers, e.g. lib/admin-people-query.ts) call auth()/requireAdminPage — they are bare prisma reads. In App Router partial rendering, a navigation request renders only the segments the client's Next-Router-State-Tree marks as changed: node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/walk-tree-with-flight-router-state.js gates rendering on `renderComponentsOnThisLevel` derived from the client-sent flightRouterState, and the staleTimes doc states 'shared layouts won't automatically be refetched on every navigation, only the page segment that changes'. Two consequences: (1) an admin demoted mid-session who is already inside /admin keeps soft-navigating between admin subpages and receiving fresh admin data — the layout gate never re-runs and the pages never check (role demotion does not bump credentialVersion, and even if it did, no code on these renders reads the session at all); (2) a regular member who crafts an RSC request whose router-state-tree marks the admin layout segment as already-known may receive the page segment's flight data — the proxy only checks that a session cookie EXISTS, and nothing else in the render path checks anything.
W1-123.evidence: src/app/(main)/admin/layout.tsx: `await requireAdminPage(); const counts = await loadAdminCounts();` is the only gate. src/app/(main)/admin/people/page.tsx: `const [page, total] = await Promise.all([loadPeoplePage(filters), prisma.user.count({ where: peopleWhere(filters) })]);` — no session read. lib/admin.ts's own comment concedes the design: 'A layout guard is navigation, not authorisation' — but applies that reasoning only to server actions, while the PAGES render the same protected data. walk-tree-with-flight-router-state.js:58-119: `const renderComponentsOnThisLevel = ...` / `if (renderComponentsOnThisLevel) {` — the server renders only what the client's header claims is missing.
W1-123.fixDirection: Call requireAdminPage() at the top of every admin page (or, cheaper, inside the shared data helpers: loadPeoplePage, the audit/reports/analytics/mail/content/messages/support/catchups loaders), exactly as every admin server action already calls requireAdmin(). Keep the layout call for the counts. This is one line per page and removes both the demotion window and the crafted-request question entirely.
W1-123.gateOrTest: Extend src/lib/gate-coverage.test.mjs to assert every file matching src/app/(main)/admin/**/page.tsx contains a requireAdminPage( call (same pattern the repo already uses to pin deleted routes deleted).
W1-123.reproPlan: Live, read-only: sign in via /api/dev-login as a NON-admin member on the local dev server, then GET /admin/people with headers `RSC: 1` and a Next-Router-State-Tree copied from a real admin session's request but with the layout segment marked unchanged; if member data comes back, the crafted-request half is proven. The demoted-admin half is provable from the quoted code alone.

W1-124.title: The notification bell badge is frozen for the entire browsing session: the (main) layout only computes unreadCount on hard loads, and NotificationBell ignores every later value
W1-124.expected: The bell badge reflects unread notifications with reasonable freshness: it rises when a like/comment/catch-up notification arrives during a session (the component even ships a shake animation for exactly that: 'Shakes the bell when the unread count RISES'), and falls when notifications are read on another device or tab.
W1-124.actual: Three compounding facts make the badge correct only at the moment of a full page load. (1) unreadCount is computed in the (main) layout, and shared layouts are not re-rendered on soft navigation (staleTimes doc: 'shared layouts won't automatically be refetched on every navigation, only the page segment that changes'), so browsing feed→directory→letters never recomputes it. (2) Even when the layout IS re-rendered server-side (any server action that calls revalidatePath re-renders the full current route), `useState(initialUnreadCount)` only reads the prop at mount — the persistent sidebar/mobile-band bell instance never takes the new value. (3) There is no polling anywhere (grep for setInterval/useSWR across components: none), and handleOpen() fetches the notification list but never recomputes unreadCount from it, so the panel can show unread rows while the badge says nothing, and vice versa. Net: the shake-on-rise effect at line 110 is unreachable dead code (unreadCount only ever decreases after mount), a member browsing for an hour never learns of new notifications, and marking things read on the phone leaves the laptop badge lit until reload. There is no /notifications page — the bell is the only notifications surface, so nothing corrects it. Side inconsistency: pages that mount the header-variant bell (e.g. /feed passes a freshly-queried unreadCount through PageHeader) remount per navigation via (main)/template.tsx, so the header bell and the rail bell can show different counts simultaneously.
W1-124.evidence: layout.tsx:35: `const [unreadCount, mailState] = await Promise.all([prisma.notification.count({ where: { userId: session.user.id, read: false } }), ...])` — layout-scoped. notification-bell.tsx:98: `const [unreadCount, setUnreadCount] = useState(initialUnreadCount);` — prop read once. Lines 160-177: setUnreadCount is only ever called with decrements (`c - 1`) or 0. handleOpen (134-145) sets notifications/nextCursor/hasMore but never unreadCount.
W1-124.fixDirection: Have the bell own its count: on mount and on a modest interval (or at least on every dropdown open and on window focus), fetch the unread count via the existing getNotifications action (add a count to its return) and setUnreadCount from the server value. That single change fixes the frozen badge, the cross-device case, the panel/badge disagreement, and resurrects the shake animation. Optionally also sync state from initialUnreadCount when the prop changes (an effect comparing prop to a ref) so action-triggered layout re-renders propagate.
W1-124.gateOrTest: Playwright: sign in, mark all read via a direct server call, poll the badge geometry/count to assert it clears without a reload; and the inverse (insert a notification row, assert the badge appears within the refresh interval).
W1-124.reproPlan: Live, own-account-only writes on local dev: open two tabs as the same dev-login user; in tab A open the bell and 'Mark all read'; observe tab B's badge stays lit indefinitely through soft navigations and only clears on hard reload.

W1-125.title: Root layout reads the theme cookie, making every route dynamic — including the landing page the code explicitly promises stays static
W1-125.expected: The signed-out landing page '/' (and /privacy, /terms, /guidelines) is statically rendered and served from cache. proxy.ts:140-146 documents this as a deliberate decision: 'Handled here rather than in app/page.tsx so the landing page stays statically rendered for logged-out visitors: calling auth() in the page would opt the whole route into dynamic rendering for everyone.'
W1-125.actual: The ROOT layout awaits cookies() on every request: layout.tsx:68 `const theme = (await getThemeCookie()) ?? "light";` where theme.ts:23 is `const value = (await cookies()).get(THEME_COOKIE)?.value;`. cookies() in the root layout opts the ENTIRE route tree into dynamic rendering (no PPR/cacheComponents is enabled in next.config.ts), so '/' — the most-shared public URL, hit by every prospective member, link preview and crawler — is a full serverless render per request, as are the three policy pages. The care taken in the proxy to avoid auth() in page.tsx buys nothing. Verify with `next build` output showing '○ (Static)' for /, /privacy, /terms, /guidelines.
W1-125.gateOrTest: A check in scripts/qa (or a build assertion) that the build manifest marks '/' as static, so a future request-API read in a shared layout cannot silently regress it again.
W1-125.reproPlan: Read-only: run `next build` locally and read the route summary table ('ƒ' vs '○' for /). No DB writes involved (build does not seed).

W1-126.title: verificationMailState performs a blocking Resend send inside the (main) layout's awaited Promise.all — the exact network call the same file's after() comment forbids in the render path
W1-126.expected: Page render never waits on the mail provider. The layout's own comment (lines 58-62) states the rule: the drain runs 'Inside after(), unlike the catch-up advance, because this one makes network calls to Resend: it must run AFTER the response has been streamed, or every page in the app would wait on somebody else's welcome email.'
W1-126.actual: For any signed-in member whose email is unconfirmed, the layout awaits verificationMailState(session.user.id) inside the render-blocking Promise.all (layout.tsx:44-46). When the newest verify row is status='queued' and budget remains, that function calls claimAndSend(row) synchronously: 2 DB writes, a token mint, then `await sendMail(...)` — a live Resend API round trip — before the page can render. The Resend SDK's fetch has no timeout, so a hung provider connection stalls the page toward the function ceiling. This hits exactly the newest members (everyone is unconfirmed on signup day), and while Resend is erroring, EVERY page load for such a member retries the send in-path until the row burns its 4 attempts.
W1-126.evidence: layout.tsx:44-46: `session.user.emailConfirmed ? Promise.resolve(null) : verificationMailState(session.user.id),` inside `await Promise.all([...])`. email-queue.ts:592-596: 'Budget is available, so nothing may sit queued: send it now.' `if (row.status === "queued") { const outcome = await claimAndSend(row); ... }`. claimAndSend (159-240) performs `await sendMail({ to: row.to, ...built })` plus three prisma writes.
W1-126.fixDirection: Split the function: the layout should only READ state (row status + budget arithmetic, all DB-local) to choose the banner, and the actual send should be scheduled via the existing scheduleDrain()/after() path (the drain already prioritises reset over verify; add a targeted claimAndSend inside after() if first-page-view immediacy matters). The banner can honestly say 'imminent' for a queued row it just scheduled.
W1-126.gateOrTest: A unit test asserting verificationMailState never invokes sendMail (mock the module and call with a queued row), or an integration assertion that layout render time for an unconfirmed user is independent of Resend latency.
W1-126.reproPlan: Live, local, own account: create an unconfirmed dev account with EMAIL_DEV_SEND=1 and a deliberately slow/unreachable Resend stub; time any page load — it inherits the provider latency. (Uses the shared DB only for the account's own rows.)

Number(filters.year) : null` — Number("abc") is NaN, `typeof NaN === "number"` is true, so line 47 sets `where.batchYear = NaN`; same for yearFrom/yearTo at lines 29-30/49-54 (`gte: NaN`). W1-128.title: Fire-and-forget telemetry writes (login attempts, search log, token sweep) are not scheduled via after(): on Vercel the instance can freeze before they land
W1-128.expected: Bookkeeping writes that must not block the response still reliably execute — on serverless that means after()/waitUntil, which this codebase already uses correctly for the mail drain (layout.tsx:63) and scheduleDrain (email-queue.ts:373 with its `after(run)` + fallback).
W1-128.actual: Five write paths use bare `void promise` instead: login-attempt.ts:46 `void prisma.loginAttempt.create(...)` (called from authorize() — the data feeding the admin 'who cannot sign in' panel the file's own comment calls the one place the owner would notice a locked-out member); search-log.ts is `void logSearch(...)`-ed from users/search:72, places/search:127 and the feed page render at feed/page.tsx:31; auth-tokens.ts:107 `void prisma.authToken.deleteMany(...)` (the only sweep keeping the token table bounded — 'a project that has no cron'). On Vercel, execution freezes when the response finishes; work merely detached with void has no guarantee of completing, so these rows are dropped intermittently — worst exactly under burst/cold-start conditions, which is when login-failure analytics matter most, and the token sweep silently never running lets AuthToken grow unbounded.
W1-128.evidence: login-attempt.ts:44-59: 'Deliberately not awaited... A statistics row must never be able to delay, or fail, a sign-in' — the intent is right, the mechanism is wrong for serverless. Contrast email-queue.ts:364-373 which does `try { after(run); } catch { void run(); }` — the codebase already owns the correct pattern.
W1-128.fixDirection: Wrap each in the same after()-with-void-fallback helper scheduleDrain uses (extract it to a shared lib). recordLoginAttempt runs inside NextAuth's authorize where after() is available in Next 16 (server function context); keep the void fallback for contexts without a request scope.
W1-128.gateOrTest: Grep-based gate in the unit tests: no `void prisma.` outside an after() wrapper in src/lib and src/app (the repo already runs source-grep tests in security-regressions.test.mjs).
W1-128.reproPlan: code-argument-only: platform freeze behavior cannot be reproduced meaningfully on a local long-lived dev server; the argument rests on Vercel's documented freeze-after-response semantics plus the quoted code.

W1-129.title: Visit/page-view analytics undercount structurally: touchLastSeen fires only on layout renders, so soft navigations are never counted and lastPath is wrong
W1-129.expected: The Visit row records page views and the path the member is on: proxy.ts mints x-visit-id 'to attribute page views to one Visit row', last-seen.ts documents 'Visit is NOT throttled: it counts views and follows the path, which is the whole point', and the layout comment claims it runs on 'essentially every authenticated page view'.

An SPA session of 30 page views registers as views:1 (the initial hard load) plus one view per server-action-triggered refresh; Visit.lastPath and the x-pathname the admin room displays stay pinned to the entry page; entry/exit analysis, average-views-per-visit and the per-page popularity numbers in /admin/analytics are all systematically wrong — biased toward hard-loading and mutating users. The client reporter is the smaller change and also fixes lastPath.
W1-129.gateOrTest: e2e assertion: sign in, soft-navigate across 4 routes, read the Visit row (views >= 4, lastPath = final route).
W1-129.reproPlan: Live, own-account: on local dev, sign in, soft-navigate 5 pages, then query the Visit row (read-only inspection via prisma studio is pre-approved) — views will be 1.

W1-130.title: Server-rendered display dates show the UTC calendar day to IST members: letters, collection photos and admin lists date content written 00:00-05:29 IST on the previous day

W1-131.title: Clicking a notification whose row was pruned or deleted does nothing: markNotificationRead throws P2025 and the navigation never runs

In the client, handleClickNotification (bell.tsx:160-171) does `await markNotificationRead(notif.id);` BEFORE `router.push(notif.link)`; the rejection aborts the handler, so the tap is silently dead. Reachable whenever the panel holds rows the DB no longer has: the KEEP=100 prune (actions.ts:44-57) runs on every first-page open in any OTHER tab/device, and getNotifications caps a session at 100 visible rows across two surfaces (header bell + rail bell keep independent lists), so a stale second panel is a normal state, not an exotic one. Also note both mark actions call revalidatePath("/") (actions.ts:82,95) — the landing page, not any surface that renders notifications; under Next 16 semantics its only real effect is forcing a full re-render of whatever page the member is on for every single notification click.

W1-131.fixDirection: Use updateMany (returns count 0 instead of throwing) or catch P2025 and return success; in the client, run router.push regardless of the mark call's outcome. W1-131.reproPlan: Live, own-account, local dev: open the bell in two tabs with >100 notifications, open tab A (prunes), then in tab B click a pruned row — nothing happens; console shows the rejected action.

W1-132.title: setTheme's cookie write triggers the exact full-page action refresh the like-button work removed: toggling theme mid-scroll re-renders the whole route and can scroll-jump
W1-132.expected: Theme toggling is client-side and cosmetic: the action's own comment says 'Deliberately revalidates nothing: theme is cosmetic... the client flips the class instantly via next-themes' own setTheme.'
W1-132.actual: Setting a cookie in a server action marks the request as revalidated regardless of any revalidatePath call: node_modules/next/dist/server/web/spec-extension/adapters/request-cookies.js:130 sets `workStore.pathWasRevalidated = ActionDidRevalidateStaticAndDynamic` on any mutable-cookie write, and action-handler.js then re-renders the full current route in the action response (skipPageRendering false) and instructs the client to drop its router cache (NEXT_ACTION_REVALIDATED_HEADER). So every theme toggle server-re-renders the current page (layout queries included) and applies a fresh tree — the same mechanism feed/actions.ts:514-517 documents as 'landing as an occasional scroll-to-top on the heart click (root cause of the heart scroll-jump bug)'. W1-132.fixDirection: Set the cookie client-side (it is deliberately httpOnly:false and holds only 'light'/'dark') via document.cookie in the same client handler that calls next-themes setTheme, and let the server action persist only User.theme. W1-132.gateOrTest: chrome-devtools check pinned by a Playwright spec: toggle theme at scrollY>0 on /feed, expect.poll scrollY unchanged and no full RSC page payload in the action response.
W1-132.reproPlan: Live, read-only-ish (writes only the member's own theme): on local dev, scroll the feed, toggle theme, watch the network tab — the action response carries the full flight tree, and scroll position occasionally resets.

W1-134.title: Like has no postId-leading index: every feed page's like-counts and the 'Most liked' sort scan the entire Like table, and deleting a prolific author's account cascades through hundreds of full-table scans
W1-134.expected: Counting likes per post (WHERE postId = ?) and the FK cascade from Post deletion should be index lookups. Postgres does not auto-index FK columns; a child-side index on Like.postId is required.
W1-134.actual: Like's only index is `@@unique([userId, postId])` (schema.prisma:465), which leads with userId and cannot serve postId-only predicates. Every feed page (`_count: { select: { comments: {...}, likes: true } }`, feed/actions.ts:859), the letters index (letters/page.tsx:58), saved posts (feed/actions.ts:996), and the 'liked' sort (`orderBy: { likes: { _count: "desc" } }`, feed/actions.ts:893) all count likes per post. Prisma executes relation counts as a grouped aggregate/lateral count on Like WHERE postId — with no usable index that is a full scan of the Like table per request. Plausible 2,000-user row count: ~20k posts x ~10 likes = ~200k Like rows, rescanned on every feed/letters/saved page load; the offset-paged 'liked' sort additionally re-aggregates the whole table per page. Worse: `prisma.$transaction([report.deleteMany, user.delete])` in account-purge.ts:99 cascades User→Post→Like; Postgres runs the FK cascade per deleted Post row, each doing an unindexed lookup WHERE postId = <id> — an author with 500 posts triggers ~500 sequential full scans of a 200k-row table inside one transaction, which can run for minutes, hold a pgbouncer pooled connection, and fail the retention sweep's purge.
W1-134.evidence: schema.prisma Like model in full: `model Like { id String @id @default(cuid()); userId String; postId String; user User @relation(...); post Post @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade); @@unique([userId, postId]) }` — no other index. Feed include at feed/actions.ts:859: `_count: { select: { comments: { where: { isHidden: false, deletedAt: null } }, likes: true } }` runs on every loadPosts call (PAGE_SIZE 20, line 762). Sort at :891-894: `sortBy === "liked" ? { likes: { _count: "desc" } } : ...` with `skip: offset` (:900). A btree on (userId, postId) can only satisfy WHERE postId=? via a full index scan; the comments count by contrast has `@@index([postId, isHidden])` (schema:454), showing the pattern was applied to Comment but missed on Like.
W1-134.fixDirection: Add `@@index([postId])` to Like in schema.prisma via a dated idempotent file in prisma/migrations-manual/ (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS), run npx prisma generate, apply with scripts/dev/run-sql.mjs per the repo's schema-change protocol. While in there, add the sibling child-side FK indexes from the companion findings in one migration.
W1-134.gateOrTest: Extend the schema-assertion style of src/lib/security-regressions.test.mjs: a unit test that reads prisma/schema.prisma and fails if Like lacks a postId-leading @@index. Orchestrator can confirm live read-only with EXPLAIN on `SELECT "postId", COUNT(*) FROM "Like" WHERE "postId" IN ('x') GROUP BY 1` (Seq Scan today, Index Only Scan after).
W1-134.reproPlan: Read-only: EXPLAIN the aggregate above against the live DB, or time /feed with Prisma query logging on localhost. Code-argument is sufficient.

W1-135.actual: Comment's indexes are `@@index([postId, createdAt])` and `@@index([postId, isHidden])` only. loadComments' second query (feed/actions.ts:1147-1152) is `where: { OR: [ { id: { in: rootIds }, ...VISIBLE_COMMENT }, { parentId: { in: rootIds }, ...VISIBLE_COMMENT } ] }` — no postId filter at all, so the parentId branch has no usable index and the whole query degrades to a scan of the full Comment table (plausible ~100k rows at 2,000 users: 20k posts x ~5 comments) on EVERY thread open. The roots query (:1134) also embeds `{ replies: { some: VISIBLE_COMMENT } }`, an EXISTS on parentId with the same gap. Comment.deleteMany cascades and the author-side cascade (User delete → Comment.authorId, also unindexed) compound it.

Schema Comment model lines 431-455 carry only the two postId-leading indexes; `parent Comment? @relation("CommentReplies", fields: [parentId], references: [id])` has no @@index([parentId]).

W1-136.title: Directory page ships every located member to the browser on every load and every filter change: the map pin query has no take and buildPins serializes each person once per listed city
W1-136.expected: The directory should stay usable at 2,000 members: bounded payloads, and per-interaction cost independent of total membership.
W1-136.actual: `prisma.user.findMany({ where: pinWhere, select: PIN_SELECT, orderBy: [...] })` (directory/page.tsx:294-298) has no `take` — it fetches every non-blocked member who has any UserPlace, with ~10 scalar fields plus their full places array. buildPins (:92-169) then pushes a full PinPerson object into `people` for EVERY resolvable city the member lists (`existing.people.push(person)` :160), so a member with 3 cities is serialized 3 times. The whole structure is passed as props to the client component `<DirectoryClient users cityPins unmappedPeople ...>` (:344-350), i.e. serialized into the RSC payload of every directory load. At 2,000 members with places this is on the order of 0.5-1.5MB of flight payload per view — on every filter change too, since filters navigate via searchParams and re-run the entire 7-query Promise.all (two full groupBys, a count, the pins, the city facet) server-side each time. Members on Indian mobile connections will feel this directly; it also multiplies function memory/CPU per request. (Below Stage 1 `people` is stripped (:333-335) but the query and buildPins still run.)
W1-136.evidence: directory/page.tsx:294-298 quoted: `prisma.user.findMany({ where: pinWhere, select: PIN_SELECT, orderBy: [{ batchYear: "desc" }, { name: "asc" }] })` — the only findMany in the Promise.all without take. PIN_SELECT (:42-57) includes `places: { select: { city: true, lat: true, lng: true }, orderBy: { position: "asc" } }`. :159-162: `existing.count += 1; existing.people.push(person)`.
W1-136.fixDirection: Cap what ships: send pins as {city, lng, lat, count} only and lazy-load a pin's people on drilldown via a server action (paginated), or cap people-per-pin (e.g. first 12 + count). Keep the aggregate count server-side. Also consider caching the unfiltered pin aggregation (it is identical for every viewer above Stage 1) with a short revalidate.
W1-136.gateOrTest: An e2e assertion on /directory response size (fail above e.g. 300KB), seeded with a few hundred members; or a unit test on buildPins output size bounds.
W1-136.reproPlan: Read-only: load /directory with chrome-devtools MCP and read the document+RSC transfer size from list_network_requests; compare against member count.

W1-141.title: Remaining unindexed FK columns make account purge and per-user lookups table-scans: CatchupEntryLove.entryId, Bookmark.postId, GroupMember.userId, Comment.authorId, Photo.uploaderId, CatchupEntry.authorId, CatchupPrompt.authorId
W1-141.expected: Every FK that is queried from the child side (counts, per-user lists, ON DELETE CASCADE) needs a child-side index; the purge transaction in particular must not degrade to a chain of sequential scans.
W1-141.actual: All of these uniques lead with the wrong column for their hot read: CatchupEntryLove `@@unique([userId, entryId])` — the round page counts loves per entry (`_count: { select: { loves: true } }`, round/[editionId]/page.tsx:275) and the archive teaser does too, both WHERE entryId; Bookmark `@@unique([userId, postId])` — the Post→Bookmark cascade scans on post delete; GroupMember `@@unique([groupId, userId])` — `groupMember.findMany({ where: { userId } })` runs on every saved-posts load (feed/actions.ts:955) and catchups home (catchups/page.tsx:65), userId not leading; Comment.authorId, Photo.uploaderId, CatchupEntry.authorId, CatchupPrompt.authorId have no index at all and are hit by the export route, photoQuotaError (`photo.count({ where: { uploaderId } })`, collection/actions.ts:96) and the User-delete cascade inside `prisma.$transaction([...])` (account-purge.ts:99). Individually these tables are smaller than Like/Comment, but the purge fires them all inside one transaction over a pgbouncer pooled connection: at 2,000-user table sizes a purge of an active member becomes a multi-second-to-minutes transaction, and the retention sweep runs purges in sequence (retention.ts:120-126) inside one cron invocation against Vercel's function duration ceiling.
W1-141.evidence: Schema quoted: CatchupEntryLove `@@unique([userId, entryId])` (no entryId index); GroupMember `@@unique([groupId, userId])`; Bookmark `@@unique([userId, postId])`; Comment/Photo/CatchupEntry/CatchupPrompt author/uploader columns have no @@index. account-purge.ts:99: `await prisma.$transaction([ prisma.report.deleteMany({ where: { reporterId: userId } }), <user.delete cascade> ])`.
W1-141.fixDirection: Same manual migration batch: @@index([entryId]) on CatchupEntryLove, @@index([postId]) on Bookmark, @@index([userId]) on GroupMember, @@index([authorId]) on Comment, @@index([uploaderId]) on Photo, @@index([authorId]) on CatchupEntry and CatchupPrompt. Cheap to write, and they close the purge-transaction risk in one stroke.
W1-141.gateOrTest: One schema-assertion unit test covering the full FK-index list pins all of these at once.
W1-141.reproPlan: Read-only EXPLAIN per shape; or time purgeUserAccount against a seeded throwaway user in dev (write — orchestrator's call, not mine).

W1-143.title: Seven fire-and-forget telemetry writes (recordView x4, logSearch x3) run without after(): on Vercel the write races response completion and is silently dropped, so view counters and search logs undercount in production only
W1-143.expected: On serverless, nothing is guaranteed to run after the response unless scheduled with after()/waitUntil. The codebase knows this — the mail drain (layout.tsx:63) and the collection intake (feed/actions.ts:180) both use after() — and the ContentView/SearchLog tables exist specifically to answer the owner's analytics questions.
W1-143.actual: All seven sites fire the promise bare: `void recordView(session.user.id, "profile", user.id)` (profile/[id]/page.tsx:117, with the comment 'Not awaited: a profile must render at the same speed...'), same shape in letters/[id]:85, collection/[id]:58, round/[editionId]:194, and `void logSearch({...})` in users/search:72, places/search:127, feed/page.tsx:31. When the RSC render or route response finishes before the DB round trip does, Vercel freezes the instance and the write is lost. The loss is probabilistic (fast DB round trips sometimes win the race), so the symptom is production counters that are mysteriously lower than dev — exactly the failure class CLAUDE.md's own guard-that-hides-its-breakage note warns about, and invisible because both helpers swallow errors in production (content-view.ts:34-38, search-log.ts:80-84).
W1-143.evidence: profile/[id]/page.tsx:114-117 quoted: `/* Not awaited: ... */ void recordView(session.user.id, "profile", user.id);`. Contrast layout.tsx:63: `after(async () => { await drainMailQueue(); ... })` — the pattern exists in the same tree and is not used here.
W1-143.fixDirection: Wrap each call in next/server after(): `after(() => recordView(...))` in the four pages, and in the two route handlers plus the feed page use after() as well (route handlers support it). No behavior change for the member; the write is guaranteed to complete post-response.
W1-143.gateOrTest: Grep-gate in the unit tests: fail on `void recordView(` / `void logSearch(` outside an after() callback; or simply verify ContentView rows increment on the deployed site after a profile visit.
W1-143.reproPlan: Live proof on production is read-write telemetry; safer code-argument-only. Orchestrator could compare ContentView.count deltas against PostHog pageview counts for the same period (read-only).

W1-144.title: SearchLog's keystroke dedupe does not do what its comment guarantees: each prefix of a typed query is a distinct string, so type-ahead writes a row (plus a dedupe read) per keystroke, into a table the retention sweep never prunes
W1-144.expected: Per the in-file comment (search-log.ts:22-29): 'typing "Bengaluru" would otherwise write nine rows, of which eight are prefixes nobody searched for. Debouncing in the browser helps but cannot be trusted, so the dedupe lives here where it is guaranteed.' The table should grow with searches, not keystrokes, and old rows should age out.
W1-144.actual: The implemented dedupe (search-log.ts:50-58) matches on EXACT query equality: `where: { userId, scope, query, createdAt: { gte: ... } }`. 'Ben' ≠ 'Beng' ≠ 'Benga', so every keystroke of a type-ahead surface (users/search and places/search both call logSearch per request, and both back per-keystroke pickers — the 'search' rate limit comment at rate-limit.ts:88 says 'one request per keystroke') still writes its own row, exactly the nine-rows-for-Bengaluru case the comment claims is prevented. Each miss also costs an extra findFirst before the create. Compounding it: runRetentionSweep (retention.ts:74-110) prunes AdminMessage, Report, Contribution, Notification, LoginAttempt, AuditLog and OutboundEmail — but neither SearchLog nor Visit appears in KEEP_DAYS, so both grow without bound on a 500MB-class Supabase plan (SearchLog at keystroke rate; Visit at ~one row per member-sitting). The 'most common searches' analytics is also polluted by prefix fragments.
W1-144.evidence: search-log.ts:50-55 quoted: `const recent = await prisma.searchLog.findFirst({ where: { userId: input.userId, scope: input.scope, query, createdAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now() - DEDUPE_MS) } } ...)` — `query` is the exact trimmed string (:45). retention.ts KEEP_DAYS block lists seven tables; SearchLog and Visit are absent from both KEEP_DAYS and the sweep steps.
W1-144.fixDirection: Two independent fixes: (1) make the dedupe prefix-aware — before insert, delete (or update-in-place) a recent row from the same user+scope whose query is a PREFIX of the new one (`WHERE query = left(:new, length(query))` via startsWith), or debounce server-side by keying on (userId, scope) within the window and keeping only the longest query; (2) add SearchLog (e.g. 365 days) and Visit (e.g. 365 days) to KEEP_DAYS and the sweep.
W1-144.gateOrTest: Unit test on logSearch: log 'Be' then 'Ben' then 'Beng' within a second and assert one surviving row; a retention test asserting the sweep deletes old SearchLog/Visit rows.
W1-144.reproPlan: Read-only: count SearchLog rows grouped by user+minute on the live DB and observe prefix chains ('Be','Ben','Beng' with ascending createdAt).

W1-145.title: Resend launch math, quantified: 95/day cap minus the 20-message reset reserve leaves 75 verification emails per day, so 400 day-one signups means the last member waits 5-6 days for their link — locked below Stage 1 (no directory names, no profiles) the entire time
W1-145.expected: The owner accepted queuing beyond 100/day (OutboundEmail model comment: 'Launch is expected to put more than 100 signups through in the first day... The rest wait for tomorrow'). What has not been surfaced is the compounding tail: 'tomorrow' is only true for the first 75 in line.
W1-145.actual: DAILY_CAP = 95 (email-queue.ts:80), RESET_RESERVE = 20 (:91), and the drain's eligibility filter (:468-469: `live.verifyRemaining > 0 ? ["verify", "reset", "password-changed"] : ["reset", "password-changed"]`) means at most 75 verify messages leave per UTC day. Queue math for the owner's own launch estimate: 400 signups day one → day 1 sends 75, backlog 325; day 2: 250; day 3: 175; day 4: 100; day 5: 25; day 6: clear — before counting days 2-5's NEW signups, which join the same FIFO behind them. Every waiting member is meanwhile held below Stage 1: requireVerifiedEmail gates the directory names, profile pages, people search and users-by-batch (directory/page.tsx:196 `namesLocked = !IS_DEMO && !session?.user?.emailConfirmed`; users/search/route.ts:18), so the first-week experience for most of the launch cohort is a browsable shell with no people in it, with the banner honestly reporting the budget is spent (verificationMailState 'queued'). The queue mechanics themselves are sound (claim CAS, token minted at send, reserve protects resets) — the finding is the number.

W1-145.fixDirection: A launch-week decision, not code: either pay for one month of Resend's first paid tier (raises the daily cap ~50x; DAILY_CAP could then read from env), or pre-verify the roster-matched cohort (RosterEntry emails whose signup address matches could skip the mail gate), or temporarily relax which surfaces Stage 1 gates during launch week. W1-147.title: Production images are served from pub-*.r2.dev, which Cloudflare rate-limits and documents as not for production; mostly shielded by the Vercel image optimizer's cache, but unoptimized call sites and first-fetches bypass the shield
W1-147.expected: At 2,000 users, image-heavy surfaces (feed, collection) need an origin that is not rate-limited. Cloudflare's docs state r2.dev URLs are rate-limited and intended for development; the custom-domain step is acknowledged in AGENTS.md ('a custom domain can be added before launch') but is not on the bugs.md open list and has no tracking item.

W1-148.title: Deleting or merging a member cascades away every Group they created — including whole Catch-ups and other members' posts and answers
W1-148.expected: A member leaving (self-deletion after the 60-day grace, an admin delete, or a duplicate-account merge) removes THEIR content. Shared containers survive: the schema itself says so — Catchup.createdById is `String?` with `onDelete: SetNull`, commented "the Keeper; nullable so the Catch-up survives if they leave" (schema.prisma:702).
W1-148.actual: Group.creator is `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:201: `creator User @relation(fields: [creatorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)`). `purgeUserAccount` runs a bare `prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } })` (account-purge.ts:101) with no group handling, so the delete cascades: every Group the member created → its Catchup (schema:717 `group Group @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade)`) → every CatchupEdition, CatchupPrompt, CatchupEntry (everyone's answers, every published Round), every Post with that groupId (schema:406, other members' posts included), all GroupMember rows and invites. Three trigger paths all hit it: (1) the unattended retention sweep (retention.ts:121 calls purgeUserAccount 60 days after a self-request — nobody is even watching); (2) adminDeleteUser (admin-actions.ts:59); (3) adminMergeUsers, which deletes the source user at the end of its transaction (admin/people/actions.ts:315) — destroying even the posts/entries it just carefully moved to the target if they live in a group the source created. The blast radius is systemic, not an edge: createCatchupWithPeople makes the Keeper the group creator (catchups/actions.ts:441-449), so EVERY Catch-up dies with its Keeper's account; and joinBatchGroup makes the first-to-sign-up member of each batch the creator of the whole "Batch of {year}" group (auth/actions.ts:221-229), so a batch group dies with one arbitrary member. Secondary corruption: collectImageUrls (account-purge.ts:37-46) collects only the deleted member's OWN rows, so the R2 bytes behind other members' cascaded posts/entries become permanently unreachable orphans — the exact H9 failure mode the purge was built to close, reintroduced via the cascade.
W1-148.evidence: schema.prisma:199-201: `creator  User @relation(fields: [creatorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)` on Group. schema.prisma:702: `createdById String?  // the Keeper; nullable so the Catch-up survives if they leave` with `onDelete: SetNull` — direct proof of contradicted intent. account-purge.ts:99-102: `await prisma.$transaction([ prisma.report.deleteMany({ where: { reporterId: userId } }), prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } }) ]);` — no group reassignment anywhere. catchups/actions.ts:442-449: `const group = await tx.group.create({ data: { name, visibility: "private", creatorId, members: { create: memberRows } } })` — the Keeper is always the group creator. auth/actions.ts:221-229: `group = await prisma.group.create({ data: { name, ..., creatorId: userId } })` — first batch member owns the batch group. admin/people/actions.ts:290-316 moves posts/comments/entries to the target and then `prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: sourceId } })` in the same transaction — the cascade then deletes any of those rows sitting in a source-created group.
W1-148.fixDirection: Change Group.creatorId to nullable with onDelete: SetNull (mirroring Catchup.createdById), via a dated idempotent file in prisma/migrations-manual/ (ALTER the FK constraint) plus `npx prisma generate`; audit every reader of group.creatorId for null-handling. Alternatively (no schema change) have purgeUserAccount and adminMergeUsers reassign `Group.creatorId` to another group admin/member (or a system account) before the user.delete, and refuse deletion of accounts whose groups have no other member. Also extend collectImageUrls to enumerate images in soon-to-be-cascaded groups if any cascade path is intentionally kept.
W1-148.gateOrTest: New unit/integration test: create user A, have A create a Catch-up with member B, B submits an entry; purge A; assert the Group, Catchup, and B's CatchupEntry still exist. Pin the schema with a test asserting Group.creator's referential action is not Cascade (read prisma/schema.prisma in security-regressions.test.mjs style).
W1-148.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would destroy real rows in the shared production database).

W1-149.title: joinBatchGroup check-then-insert with no unique: concurrent same-batch signups create duplicate 'Batch of {year}' groups and permanently split the batch
W1-149.expected: One "Batch of {year}" group per batch, with every alumnus of that batch auto-joined into the same group — the rule the code's own comment states ("The first person from a batch creates the group").
W1-149.actual: The rule is backed by nothing: Group has no unique on name (schema.prisma:191-208 — the code admits it: "Group.name is not unique in the schema, so match by exact name"). auth/actions.ts:215-230 is a findFirst → create with no P2002 possible: two members of the same batch registering concurrently (launch day is explicitly expected to exceed 100 signups) both miss the findFirst and both create a group named "Batch of 2010". From then on every later signup's `findFirst({ where: { name } })` — with no orderBy, so arbitrary but sticky — lands members in one or the other: the batch is permanently split into two groups whose members cannot see each other's group posts (loadPosts requires GroupMember membership for group feeds, feed/actions.ts:784-790). Nothing ever detects or repairs the split.
W1-149.evidence: auth/actions.ts:215-230: `let group = await prisma.group.findFirst({ where: { name }, select: { id: true } }); if (!group) { group = await prisma.group.create({ data: { name, ..., creatorId: userId }, ...}); }` — classic TOCTOU. schema.prisma Group model (lines 191-208) carries only `@@index([visibility, createdAt])`, no @@unique on name. Contrast with the same file's registerUser, which the same commit hardened with a P2002 catch for the user-email race (auth/actions.ts:164-169) — the group half of the same signup flow was left unguarded.
W1-149.fixDirection: Give the batch group an enforceable identity: either a partial/expression unique in a manual migration (e.g. UNIQUE on name for rows where name LIKE 'Batch of %', or better a dedicated nullable `batchYear Int? @unique` column on Group written only by joinBatchGroup), then convert joinBatchGroup to create-with-catch-P2002-then-findFirst (mirror the createCatchup pattern at catchups/actions.ts:326-372). Also add a one-off dedupe script for any duplicates already in the table before the constraint lands.
W1-149.gateOrTest: Unit test firing two concurrent joinBatchGroup calls for the same fresh batchYear against a test DB and asserting exactly one Group row; a data-integrity check in the admin panel (or npm run check script) asserting no duplicate 'Batch of %' names.
W1-149.reproPlan: code-argument-only against production; provable live only against a disposable DB by issuing two concurrent registerUser calls with the same fresh batchYear.

W1-150.title: Older verification link falsely reports 'Already confirmed' after any resend, leaving the member unverified while being told they are done
W1-150.expected: Clicking a verification link that has been superseded by a newer one tells the member the link is out of date and points them at the newer mail (or a resend). "Already confirmed" is shown only when the address is actually confirmed — the code's own comment says: "Used token: if the address really is confirmed, say so plainly."
W1-150.actual: The claim is never checked. mintToken burns ALL outstanding tokens of the kind on every mint (auth-tokens.ts:91-99: `updateMany({ where: { userId, kind, usedAt: null }, data: { usedAt: new Date() } })`), and because the queue mints the token at SEND time (email-queue.ts:402-403 `const minted = await mintToken(row.userId, kind, row.to)`), every resend — the button, or a second queue row from the enqueue-fold race (email-queue.ts:308-317 findFirst→create is itself TOCTOU) — marks the earlier mail's token usedAt. The member now has two mails in their inbox; opening the older one hits readToken → `if (row.usedAt) return { ok: false, reason: "used" }` (auth-tokens.ts:174) → confirmEmailToken returns "already" unconditionally (email-actions.ts:107-110: `if (read.reason === "used") { return "already"; }`) → the page renders "Already confirmed / This address was confirmed earlier. Nothing left to do." with GOOD styling and NO resend button (verify-client.tsx:31-34, 55, 76: `canResend = signedIn && !alreadyVerified && !good` — "already" is in GOOD). emailVerified is still null; every Stage-2 write (posting, commenting, uploading) keeps refusing them with no path offered from the page that just said nothing is left to do. The same unconditional "already" also masks the narrower crash-window half-write: readToken consumes the token and the separate `prisma.user.update({ data: { emailVerified: new Date() } })` (email-actions.ts:118-121) can fail after it, with the retry click again answering "already".
W1-150.evidence: email-actions.ts:103-116: `const read = await readToken(token, "verify", { consume: true }); if (!read.ok) { if (read.reason === "used") { // Used token: if the address really is confirmed, say so plainly. return "already"; } ... }` — the comment promises a check the code does not perform; readToken's "used" result carries no userId so it could not check. auth-tokens.ts:91-98 (burn on mint), email-queue.ts:402-409 (mint at send). verify-client.tsx COPY.already = "This address was confirmed earlier. Nothing left to do."
W1-150.fixDirection: On reason "used", look up the token row by hash again (or extend readToken's failure results to carry userId) and read User.emailVerified: return "already" only when actually verified; otherwise return a new outcome ("superseded") whose copy says a newer link replaced this one, with the resend button enabled. Optionally stop burning verify tokens on remint (burn is a security necessity for reset, but multiple live verify links to the same inbox are harmless) — that removes the trap at the source.
W1-150.gateOrTest: Unit test on confirmEmailToken: mint token A, mint token B (burning A), redeem A, assert outcome is not "already" while user.emailVerified is null; redeem B → "confirmed"; redeem B again → "already".
W1-150.reproPlan: Live: on a test account, press resend twice (two mails), click the older mail's link, observe 'Already confirmed' while the feed still shows the confirm-your-email gate. Read-only inspection of AuthToken rows would also show usedAt set by the mint, not by redemption.

W1-151.title: All five like/vote toggle actions are check-then-insert with no P2002/P2025 handling: a double-tap throws a raw server-action error and desyncs the optimistic UI
W1-151.expected: Per the app's own contract (stated at the top of catchups/actions.ts) actions return "a loose { error } / { success } shape rather than throwing to the client", and every one-row-per-pair rule is settled by its unique index with the P2002 loser answered gracefully — the pattern reportUser (report-action.ts:185-193) and registerUser (auth/actions.ts:164-169) already implement.
W1-151.actual: toggleLike, toggleBookmark, toggleCommentLike, votePoll (feed/actions.ts) and togglePhotoLove (collection/actions.ts) each do findUnique → create/delete/update with NO try/catch. Two rapid invocations (mobile double-tap, two tabs — post-card.tsx handleLike at 134-145 has zero in-flight guard: no busy state, no disable) both read `existing = null` and both create; the loser throws PrismaClientKnownRequestError P2002 out of the action. Symmetrically, both reading `existing` and both deleting throws P2025. The client code only handles `result.error` (post-card.tsx:140 `if (result.error)`), so the throw becomes an unhandled promise rejection: no toast, no revert, and the two optimistic flips leave the heart showing the opposite of the database (handleLike toggled state twice while the DB holds one like). Additionally togglePhotoLove does not verify the photo exists, so a stale photoId (photo declined meanwhile) throws P2003 the same unhandled way. The catchups counterpart toggleEntryLove has the identical race but is wrapped in runAction (catchups/actions.ts:162-172), degrading to a friendly `{ error }` — the feed/collection five lack even that. Complete class-1 uniqueness map produced by this sweep: BACKED+HANDLED: User.email (registerUser P2002 catch), Catchup.groupId (createCatchup P2002 catch), Report[reporterId,reportedUserId] (reportUser P2002 catch), GroupMember[groupId,userId] (upsert in joinCatchupByToken/joinBatchGroup; createMany skipDuplicates in addCatchupMembers), CatchupEntry[promptId,authorId] (upsert), CatchupPref (upsert), ContentView (atomic upsert), Visit (upsert), Contribution.razorpayOrderId (idempotency key), CatchupEdition[catchupId,number] (CAS + tx backstop). BACKED+UNHANDLED (this finding): Like, Bookmark, CommentLike, PollVote, PhotoLove; CatchupEntryLove (generic catch only). UNBACKED ENTIRELY: the one-batch-group rule (separate High finding). NO-UNIQUE-BY-DESIGN (duplicate rows on double-submit possible, bounded only by rate limits and client pending state): Post (createPost), Comment (createComment), AdminThread (startThread), Photo (contributePhoto), Report on posts (reporterId+postId deliberately unconstrained).
W1-151.evidence: feed/actions.ts:477-494: `const existing = await prisma.like.findUnique({ where: { userId_postId: ... } }); if (existing) { await prisma.like.delete({ where: { id: existing.id } }); } else { await prisma.like.create({ data: { userId: session.user.id, postId } });` — no try/catch anywhere in the function; schema.prisma:465 `@@unique([userId, postId])` guarantees the loser throws. post-card.tsx:134-145: `async function handleLike() { const next = !liked; setLiked(next); setLikeCount(...); const result = await toggleLike(post.id); if (result.error) {...} }` — a thrown action means `result` never exists and the rejection escapes the handler.
W1-151.fixDirection: Make the five toggles race-proof at the server: replace check-then-act with delete-first semantics or wrap create in try/catch treating P2002 as success-liked and P2025 as success-unliked (idempotent toggle), returning the loose { success, liked } shape; add an existence check (or P2003 catch) in togglePhotoLove. Optionally add an in-flight guard to handleLike/handleBookmark like poll-display.tsx's `submitting` ref.
W1-151.gateOrTest: Unit tests invoking each toggle twice concurrently (Promise.all) against a test DB asserting neither call rejects and the final row state is consistent; a lint-style grep gate asserting no bare prisma.<model>.create for models with @@unique inside actions files without an enclosing try/P2002 handler.
W1-151.reproPlan: Live on a test account: chrome-devtools double-click the heart with network throttled to Slow 3G; observe the unhandled rejection in list_console_messages and the heart state diverging from a reload's server state.

W1-152.title: adminMergeUsers aborts wholesale when both accounts answered the same Catch-up prompt (CatchupEntry unique collision on the move)
W1-152.expected: The merge folds a duplicate account into the real one; per its own doc-comment, everything carrying a `@@unique([userId, thingId])` that could collide is DROPPED rather than moved precisely so the merge cannot throw.
W1-152.actual: CatchupEntry carries `@@unique([promptId, authorId])` (schema.prisma:789) but sits in the MOVED list: `prisma.catchupEntry.updateMany({ where: { authorId: sourceId }, data: { authorId: targetId } })` (admin/people/actions.ts:297). The duplicate-account scenario the merge exists for — one human using both accounts — is exactly the case where both accounts answered the same prompt, and the updateMany then violates the unique, throwing P2002 and rolling back the entire transaction. The admin sees only "Could not merge those accounts. Nothing was changed. Check the server log." with no path forward from the UI. CatchupPrompt (also moved) has no unique and is safe; every other moved model (Post, Comment, Photo, Contribution, AdminThread, AdminMessage) is collision-free.
W1-152.evidence: admin/people/actions.ts:296-297 inside the $transaction: `prisma.catchupPrompt.updateMany({ where: { authorId: sourceId }, data: { authorId: targetId } }), prisma.catchupEntry.updateMany({ where: { authorId: sourceId }, data: { authorId: targetId } }),` versus the comment at 258-263: "DROPPED the duplicate's engagement ... Every one of these carries a @@unique([userId, thingId]), so moving them throws the moment both accounts touched the same post". CatchupEntry was missed by that reasoning. schema.prisma:789: `@@unique([promptId, authorId])`.
W1-152.fixDirection: Before the transaction, delete (or skip moving) source CatchupEntry rows whose (promptId) already has an entry by the target — e.g. `deleteMany({ where: { authorId: sourceId, prompt: { entries: { some: { authorId: targetId } } } } })` then move the remainder; or move per-row with P2002-skip. Decide explicitly whether the source's or target's answer wins (target's, to match 'the real account keeps its own').
W1-152.gateOrTest: Unit test: two users answer the same prompt, merge one into the other, assert success and exactly one surviving entry.

W1-153.title: adminSetRole last-admin guard is check-then-act: two concurrent demotions can leave zero admins (permanent moderation lockout)
W1-153.expected: "Refuses to remove the LAST admin" (the function's own doc): after any sequence of role changes, at least one admin row remains, because — as the same comment says — losing the last admin locks everybody out of moderation permanently with no door back but hand-editing the database.
W1-153.actual: The guard is a non-atomic count-then-update: `const admins = await prisma.user.count({ where: { role: "admin" } }); ... if (target?.role === "admin" && admins <= 1) return error; ... await prisma.user.update({ where: { id: userId }, data: { role } })` (admin/people/actions.ts:216-227). With exactly two admins, each demoting the other (or a double-fired demotion of two different admins) both count 2, both pass, both write → zero admins. Nothing else can re-mint one: the C1-b bypass is deleted by design.
W1-153.evidence: admin/people/actions.ts:216-227 as quoted; no transaction, no conditional updateMany, no serialization. The stakes are stated in the function's own comment (lines 202-208): "demoting the only admin locks everybody out of moderation permanently, and the only way back would be editing the database by hand."
W1-153.fixDirection: Make the demotion conditional in one statement, e.g. run inside a $transaction: `updateMany({ where: { id: userId, role: "admin" } })` only after a `SELECT count(*) FROM User WHERE role='admin' AND id != userId` style check inside the same transaction — or simpler, a single conditional `updateMany({ where: { id: userId, role: 'admin' }, data: { role: 'member' } })` followed by a post-write count; if the count is 0, revert the row in the same transaction and return the error.
W1-153.gateOrTest: Unit test with two admins issuing concurrent adminSetRole(other, "member") and asserting at least one admin survives.
W1-153.reproPlan: code-argument-only (role writes on the shared production DB).

W1-154.title: Razorpay webhook's payment.failed branch is check-then-update and can overwrite a concurrent 'paid' with 'failed'
W1-154.expected: "Everything here is idempotent... 'paid' is terminal" (the route's own header): once any confirming path records paid, no later or concurrent event may change it.
W1-154.actual: The from-created guard is enforced by a read at line 59-62 (`findUnique ... select: { id: true, status: true }`) and a separate unconditional update at 87-95. Interleaving: a delayed payment.failed webhook (from the payer's first failed attempt on the order) reads status "created"; the browser callback (confirmContribution, support/actions.ts:170-175) or a captured webhook writes "paid"; the failed handler then executes its update and overwrites status to "failed", replacing razorpayPaymentId with the failed attempt's id and setting failureReason. A real captured payment is then recorded as failed: the /support recovered figure undercounts it and chooseBird's `status: "paid"` aggregate (support/actions.ts:214-217) denies the supporter their perk. The safe out-of-order case (failed arriving after paid is already committed) is handled; only the read-write gap is not.
W1-154.evidence: webhook/route.ts:84-95: `} else if (contribution.status === "created") { // Only from "created"... await prisma.contribution.update({ where: { id: contribution.id }, data: { status: "failed", ... } }); }` — the status condition lives in JS, not in the WHERE clause. Compare the row's own schema comment (schema.prisma:859-860): razorpayOrderId is "the idempotency key. The browser callback and the webhook both race to confirm the same order, and only one of them may win."
W1-154.fixDirection: Make both webhook branches conditional writes: `updateMany({ where: { id, status: "created" }, data: { status: "failed", ... } })` for the failed branch and `updateMany({ where: { id, status: { not: "paid" } }, ... })` for the captured branch (confirmContribution can take the same shape for symmetry). No transaction needed — a single conditional UPDATE is atomic.
W1-154.gateOrTest: Unit test simulating the interleave: set row created → run failed-branch write after externally setting paid → assert status stays paid once the WHERE-clause fix lands.

W1-155.title: submitPrompt assigns position = count of accepted prompts, producing duplicate positions deterministically after any removal (and under concurrency)
W1-155.expected: Each new question lands at the end of the Round's list in a stable order (positions are the rendered/reorderable order per the code's own comment: "position is the Round's rendered/reorderable order... this is simply 'next in line'").
W1-155.actual: position is `acceptedCount` from a prior count (catchups/actions.ts:707-710, 723). Two paths break it: (1) deterministic — curatePrompt's remove is a hard delete (line 820) with no re-packing, so after removing the first of prompts at positions 0,1,2 the count is 2 and the next submission also gets position 2, tying with the existing row; ties under `orderBy: position asc` have no secondary key, so the two questions can render in different relative order across page loads and viewers until the Keeper manually reorders. (2) concurrent — two simultaneous submissions both read count N and both write position N (and both pass the 40-cap check at count 39, a harmless overshoot of the runaway guard).
W1-155.evidence: catchups/actions.ts:707-724: `const acceptedCount = await prisma.catchupPrompt.count({ where: { editionId, accepted: true } }); ... const prompt = await prisma.catchupPrompt.create({ data: { ..., position: acceptedCount } });` and 820: `await prisma.catchupPrompt.delete({ where: { id: promptId } });` — no position compaction. schema.prisma:768 orders only by `@@index([editionId, position])`.
W1-155.fixDirection: Assign position as max(position)+1 (`aggregate({ _max: { position } })`) instead of count — removals then never create ties; add `{ id: 'asc' }` as a orderBy tiebreaker wherever prompts are sorted for render.
W1-155.gateOrTest: Unit test: create 3 prompts, remove the first, submit a new one, assert all positions distinct.
W1-155.reproPlan: Live on a test Catch-up: add three questions, remove the first, add a fourth, reload the round page twice and compare question order.

W1-156.title: markNotificationRead throws P2025 for a pruned/foreign notification id, killing the click (navigation never happens)
W1-156.expected: Clicking a notification always navigates to its link; marking it read is best-effort bookkeeping.
W1-156.actual: notifications/actions.ts:77-81 uses `prisma.notification.update({ where: { id: notificationId, userId: session.user.id }, data: { read: true } })` — update throws P2025 when no row matches. Rows legitimately vanish under a live bell: getNotifications prunes everything older than the 100th-newest on every first-page open (actions.ts:44-57), and extendDeadline/removeCatchupMember/notifyReminder deleteMany reminder rows outright (catchups/actions.ts:1006-1009, 1366-1372; catchups-notify.ts:160-164). Two-device scenario: bell open on the phone showing an old row, laptop opens the bell (prune fires), phone clicks the row → the action throws → in the client, `await markNotificationRead(notif.id)` (notification-bell.tsx:162, no try/catch) rejects and `router.push(notif.link)` at line 169 never runs: the tap does nothing, with an unhandled rejection in the console.

W1-156.gateOrTest: Unit test: markNotificationRead with a nonexistent id returns { success } (or at least does not throw).
W1-156.reproPlan: Live: open the bell, delete the target row via a second session's catch-up reminder cleanup (or just call the action with a made-up id from the console) and observe the rejection.

W1-157.title: deletePost/deleteDraft delete the R2 images before the database row: a failed row-delete leaves a live post with permanently broken images
W1-157.expected: A delete that fails partway leaves nothing member-visible broken: either the post is gone, or it is intact.
W1-157.actual: Order is images-first: `await deletePostImages(post.images); await prisma.post.delete({ where: { id: postId } });` (feed/actions.ts:337-339; same shape in deleteDraft at 250-252). delImage never throws (storage.ts:218-228 catches), so the images are gone even when the subsequent post.delete fails (transient DB error, or P2025 from a concurrent delete — also uncaught here, surfacing as a raw action error). The post then remains published for everyone with dead image URLs forever; nothing retries the cleanup. The reverse order (row first, best-effort bytes after) is the pattern purgeUserAccount already documents as correct (account-purge.ts:74-86: "bytes are deleted only AFTER the row delete succeeds, because if the delete throws and rolls back, the member still exists and their images must keep rendering") — these two actions predate it.
W1-157.fixDirection: Swap the order in deletePost and deleteDraft: delete the row first, then best-effort delImage (matching purgeUserAccount); catch P2025 from the row delete as already-deleted success.
W1-157.gateOrTest: Unit test with a delImage spy asserting the row delete precedes image deletion; concurrent double-delete test asserting no throw.

W1-158.title: Legacy /onboarding updateProfile action writes bio/city/socials with no length or format validation
W1-158.expected: Every profile writer validates through a schema — settings' updateUserProfile uses profileSchema (about capped at 4000, socials format-checked), updateProfileField hand-caps every field (name 80, about 4000, jobTitle 120).
W1-158.actual: The old onboarding action — still live, imported by src/app/(auth)/onboarding/page.tsx:16 and a public POST endpoint regardless — copies seven fields (`bio, currentCity, workplace, jobTitle, phone, instagram, linkedin`) straight from FormData with only `.trim()` and no Zod, no length caps, no normalization (actions.ts:12-27: `if (value && value.trim()) { data[field] = value.trim(); }` then `prisma.user.update`). W1-159.title: Onboarding photo step ships the raw file (up to 15MB) through a Server Action; anything over ~4.5MB dies at Vercel's platform body cap with no error shown and the button stuck on busy
W1-159.expected: A new member uploading a normal 5-12MB phone photo during onboarding either succeeds (via crop/downscale so the wire bytes are small) or sees a clear error.
W1-159.actual: The step validates only `if (file.size > 15 * 1024 * 1024)` and then sends the ORIGINAL bytes: `const fd = new FormData(); fd.set("file", file); const result = await updateAvatar(fd);`. Server Actions are Vercel function invocations, hard-capped at ~4.5MB request body regardless of next.config's `serverActions.bodySizeLimit: "25mb"`. The platform answers 413 before the action runs, the awaited action call rejects, and `handlePick` has NO try/catch — so the rejection is unhandled, `setBusy(false)` never runs, and the member stares at a permanently busy button with no toast. Any photo between 4.5MB and 15MB (most phone photos) reproduces it.

The codebase itself documents this exact failure mode as a bug it fixed elsewhere: letterhead-profile.tsx:363-366 "the old path shipped the ORIGINAL bytes to a hard-coded centre crop... a 6MB phone photo could die on Vercel's ~4.5MB serverless body cap" — the profile surface got the crop-dialog fix (uploads a tiny 512px WebP blob), the onboarding surface did not. W1-159.gateOrTest: New e2e/manual check: onboarding photo step with a >4.5MB fixture image against a production build; assert an error toast appears and the button re-enables. A unit test on the step's handler asserting the file handed to updateAvatar is <4.5MB.
W1-159.reproPlan: Test-account write via the app UI on the production deployment: sign up a throwaway account, reach the onboarding photo step, pick a 6MB JPEG, observe the hang and the 413 in the network tab.

W1-161.title: purgeUserAccount deletes R2 objects one at a time after the DB rows are already gone; a duration-ceiling timeout mid-loop permanently orphans a purged member's publicly-fetchable images, and the retention sweep multiplies the exposure by running every due purge in one invocation
W1-161.expected: Account purge (GDPR Art. 17, audits H9/M35) removes all of a member's stored images even for a prolific account, and survives a function timeout resumably.
W1-161.actual: account-purge.ts:99-102 first commits `prisma.$transaction([report.deleteMany, user.delete])` — cascading away every row that points at the images — then loops `for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; }` sequentially. MAX_PHOTOS_PER_ACCOUNT is 1000 and each Photo carries 2-3 objects (thumbUrl, url, originalUrl) plus post/catch-up images, so a heavy account is hundreds to thousands of sequential DeleteObject round-trips at ~50-300ms each — minutes of runtime. No maxDuration is configured anywhere (vercel.json sets only regions+crons; no route exports maxDuration), so the deploy rides the platform default (300s Fluid / 60s legacy Hobby). On timeout: the user row is gone (transaction committed), the remaining R2 URLs exist nowhere ("the cascade takes the pointing rows with it and afterwards nothing can enumerate the objects" — the file's own comment), so those images stay publicly fetchable at their pub-*.r2.dev URLs forever — the exact H9 failure mode the function exists to close. The retention sweep (retention.ts:120-135) runs EVERY due account's purge inside one function invocation, so a wave of deletions maturing on the same night compounds it, and a timeout also skips the sweep's final `writeAudit` (retention.ts:151), leaving no record the sweep ran. adminDeleteUser (admin-actions.ts:59) awaits the same loop inside a Server Action, so deleting a prolific member can time out and show the admin an error although the row delete succeeded. Bonus defect: `deleted += 1` counts every attempt because delImage swallows failures, so the audit line "N stored image(s) removed" records attempts, not deletions.
W1-161.evidence: account-purge.ts:108-113: `let deleted = 0; for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; } return { ok: true, imagesDeleted: deleted };` — sequential, unbatched, post-commit. account-purge.ts:78-80 comment: "URLs are collected FIRST, because the cascade takes the pointing rows with it and afterwards nothing can enumerate the objects" — which is precisely why a mid-loop death is unrecoverable. upload-shared.ts:21 `MAX_PHOTOS_PER_ACCOUNT = 1000`. vercel.json contains no functions/maxDuration block; grep for maxDuration across src returns nothing.
W1-161.fixDirection: Batch the deletes with S3 DeleteObjectsCommand (R2 supports up to 1000 keys per call) or chunked Promise.all; and make the purge resumable by persisting the collected URL list (e.g. a PurgeQueue row written in the same transaction as the user delete) that the nightly sweep drains and retries, so a timeout loses nothing. Cap purges-per-sweep-invocation. Count only successful deletes (have delImage report success) in imagesDeleted. Consider an explicit `export const maxDuration` on /api/retention/sweep.
W1-161.gateOrTest: Unit test on a refactored purge that asserts object deletion is batched and that an injected failure leaves a resumable record; the existing audit entry should assert real deletions.
W1-161.reproPlan: code-argument-only (any live proof deletes real member data).

W1-162.title: All three telemetry writers (recordLoginAttempt, logSearch, recordView) are floating promises with no after() wrapper — the writes die non-deterministically once the response is sent on Vercel
W1-162.expected: Post-response bookkeeping on Vercel must be registered via after()/waitUntil (the codebase's own established pattern: layout.tsx:63, feed/actions.ts:180, email-queue.ts:373) or it is not guaranteed to execute.
W1-162.actual: recordLoginAttempt fires `void prisma.loginAttempt.create(...).catch(...)` (login-attempt.ts:46) and is called synchronously seven times in auth.ts's authorize; the credentials route responds the moment authorize returns, racing the insert against the instance freeze. users/search:72 and places/search:127 do `void logSearch({...})` immediately before `return NextResponse.json(...)`. The four content pages do `void recordView(...)` during render. None are inside after(). Consequence in production only: LoginAttempt rows (the audit-H4/H6 'who cannot sign in' admin panel — blocked members, rate-limited members), SearchLog rows and ContentView counters are silently lost at random, so the owner's support and analytics surfaces undercount in a way dev never reproduces. The queue drain and collection copy already demonstrate the correct after() pattern in the same repo.

Contrast (main)/layout.tsx:63 `after(async () => { await drainMailQueue(); ... })` — the repo knows the rule; these nine call sites predate or missed it.
W1-162.fixDirection: Wrap each fire-and-forget in `after(() => ...)` from next/server (with the existing try/catch-throws fallback pattern scheduleDrain uses for non-request contexts, since authorize may run where after() throws). Behaviour for the member is unchanged; the write simply survives the response.
W1-162.gateOrTest: Extend src/lib/security-regressions.test.mjs (or a new unit test) to assert the call sites route through an after()-wrapping helper; live: compare LoginAttempt row count to attempted sign-ins on production over a day.
W1-162.reproPlan: Read-only-ish live proof: perform a failed sign-in and a people-search on production with a test account, then check (via admin analytics pages) whether rows appeared; repeat ~20x and count the shortfall.

W1-163.title: Message-to-admin composer uploads attachments with no client size check and no downscale; any image over ~4.5MB fails with 'Try again in a moment?' — a permanent condition presented as transient
