W1-208.title: Deleting or editing a post from the feed leaves the stale card on screen: the client posts state has no removal/update path
W1-208.expected: After the author deletes a post (or saves an edit in the quick-edit dialog), the card disappears (or shows the new text) immediately, the way admin moderation and fresh posting already do.
W1-208.actual: The card stays on screen with its old content until the member navigates away and back or reloads. Delete shows no success feedback at all; edit shows a success toast while the card keeps the old text.
W1-208.evidence: PostCard.handleDelete is `const result = await deletePost(post.id); if (result.error) toast.error(result.error);` — there is NO success branch: no setRemoved, no callback to the list. EditPostDialog.handleSubmit on success does only `toast.success(...); onClose();`. The feed list lives in CLIENT state: PostFeed holds `const [posts, setPosts] = useState<PostData[]>([])`, filled by `loadPosts` in an effect keyed on `[fetchPosts, reloadKey, groupId, scope, sortBy, search, timeFilter]` — deletePost's `revalidatePath("/feed")` re-renders server components but can never touch that useState, and nothing bumps reloadKey (FeedColumn only bumps it via the composer's onPosted). The asymmetry is visible in the same file: the ADMIN path does handle it (`if (!result.error) setRemoved(true)` in handleModerationConfirm, with the comment "Removed optimistically ... rather than waiting on the revalidatePath round trip"), and CommentsSection removes deleted comments locally via removeLocally(). Only the author's own delete and edit were left out. Same gap in ProfileAuthorFeed (same PostCard, same client state) and the saved-posts masonry.
W1-208.fixDirection: Give PostCard an onDeleted callback (mirroring onBookmarkChange) that the author-delete success path calls, plus setRemoved(true) locally; have PostFeed/ProfileAuthorFeed/SavedPostsFeed drop the id from their state. For edits, return the saved content from editPost (it already returns success) and either lift it into local card state (a `const [content, setContent] = useState(post.content)` mirror) or pass an onEdited callback that patches the posts array. Do the same for EditPostDialog used from the letters card.
W1-208.gateOrTest: Playwright: create a post as the test account, delete it from its card menu, `expect.poll` the card count to drop without navigation; edit a post and assert the card text updates in place.
W1-208.reproPlan: Live, test account: post something on /feed, open the card's menu, Delete, confirm — observe the card remain until reload. Then edit a post's text via the dialog and observe the old text persist behind the success toast.

W1-209.title: votePoll double-click: unhandled P2002 on the vote unique constraint throws the action and leaves the poll permanently disabled
W1-209.expected: Two rapid taps on poll options record one vote; the second attempt is absorbed (P2002 treated as already-voted, like reportUser does), and the UI settles on the truth.
W1-209.actual: Both requests pass the check-then-insert (`const existing = await prisma.pollVote.findUnique(...); if (existing) {...} else { await prisma.pollVote.create(...) }`), the loser hits `@@unique([userId, postId])` and the action THROWS. Client-side, `handleVote` has `if (submitting) return` but `setSubmitting(true)` hasn't re-rendered between two same-frame taps, and it has no try/catch: `const result = await votePoll(postId, optionId)` rejects, so `setSubmitting(false)` on line 111 never runs — every option button carries `disabled={submitting}`, so the poll is dead until the page is remounted, with the optimistic vote still painted.
W1-209.evidence: actions.ts 284-307 is a bare find-then-create with no catch; the file's ONLY P2002 handler is in reportUser (report-action.ts:189 `err.code === "P2002"`), which proves the pattern was known and applied elsewhere. poll-display.tsx: `async function handleVote(optionId){ if (submitting) return; setSubmitting(true); ... const result = await votePoll(postId, optionId); if (result.error) {...revert...} setSubmitting(false); }` — no try/finally, so a rejected action skips both the revert and the re-enable.
W1-209.fixDirection: Server: wrap the create in try/catch, treat P2002 as success (or better: use `prisma.pollVote.upsert({ where: { userId_postId }, create: {...}, update: { pollOptionId } })`, which also removes the read-modify-write). Client: wrap the await in try/finally so setSubmitting(false) always runs, and revert optimistic state in catch.
W1-209.gateOrTest: A unit test on the action calling votePoll twice concurrently for one user (or an integration test asserting upsert semantics); a security-regressions-style test asserting the action returns {success} not a throw on duplicate.
W1-209.reproPlan: Live, test account on a test poll: double-tap two options as fast as possible; watch the network tab for a 500/digest error and the poll buttons stay disabled. Safe (only writes one PollVote row for the test account).

W1-210.title: toggleLike / toggleCommentLike / toggleBookmark check-then-write races throw unhandled P2002/P2025; no client handler catches the rejection
W1-210.expected: Double-tapping a heart (the single most common gesture in the app) ends in a consistent state: one like or none, matching what the UI shows.
W1-210.actual: Two concurrent calls both run `findUnique` then branch. Like path: both see null → both `create` → the loser throws P2002 (`@@unique([userId, postId])`, schema.prisma:465). Unlike path: both see the row → both `delete({ where: { id: existing.id } })` → the loser throws P2025 (record not found). The thrown action rejects the client await; handleLike in PostCard (`const result = await toggleLike(post.id); if (result.error) {...revert...}`), CommentItem.handleLike and handleBookmark all lack try/catch, so the revert never runs: an unhandled rejection is logged and the heart/count is left disagreeing with the DB until reload. LoveButton fires onToggle unconditionally on every click with no in-flight guard, so nothing upstream prevents the concurrency.
W1-210.evidence: actions.ts:486-494: `if (existing) { await prisma.like.delete({ where: { id: existing.id } }); } else { await prisma.like.create({ data: { userId, postId } }); ... }` — no catch anywhere in the four toggle actions. love-button.tsx handleClick: `function handleClick() { if (!liked) { setAnimate(true); ... } onToggle(); }` — no disabled/in-flight state.
W1-210.fixDirection: Server: make the toggles idempotent — catch P2002 as 'already liked' and use `deleteMany({ where: { userId_postId } })`-style deletes (deleteMany never throws on zero rows), or upsert/delete-by-compound-unique. Client: add try/catch around every toggle await with the existing revert logic, and/or an in-flight ref in the handlers.
W1-210.gateOrTest: Unit test firing toggleLike twice concurrently for one (user, post) and asserting both resolve without throwing and exactly one Like row remains.
W1-210.reproPlan: Live, test account: double-tap a heart rapidly on a test post; observe a rejected server-action response in the network tab and the heart state diverging from a reloaded page. Writes only the test account's own Like row.

W1-211.title: Replying to a reply notifies the ROOT comment's author, not the person the UI says you are replying to
W1-211.expected: The composer says "Replying to B" — B should receive the reply notification.
W1-211.actual: B never hears about it unless B also wrote the root comment. The 1-level-depth redirect rewrites parentId to the root BEFORE the notification target is chosen, and the client itself sends the root's id while displaying the reply author's name.
W1-211.evidence: Server (actions.ts 591-593): `if (parent.parentId) { parentId = parent.parentId; // reply to the root comment instead }` — then 639-657 notifies `parentComment.authorId` where parentComment is fetched by the REWRITTEN parentId, i.e. the root's author. Client (comments-section.tsx 343-352) makes it structural even without the redirect: replies' onReply sets `id: comment.deleted ? reply.id : comment.id` (the ROOT's id) while `name: reply.author!.name` — so the pill and placeholder read "Reply to <reply author>" (line 421) while the payload targets the root. The person named on screen is never the notification recipient for any reply-to-reply.
W1-211.fixDirection: Carry the ORIGINAL target through: keep the depth redirect for threading, but remember the pre-redirect parent's authorId (or accept a separate replyToUserId field validated to be a comment on the same post) and notify that person; keep notifying the root author only if they are a distinct third party, as today. Client: send the actual reply's id and let the server do the root redirect (it already does).
W1-211.gateOrTest: Unit/integration test: A posts, B comments, C replies to B, D replies to C's reply — assert D's action produces a notification for C (and post author A), not for B only.
W1-211.reproPlan: Live with two test accounts: reply to a reply, then check the named person's bell — no notification arrives; the root author gets "replied to your comment" instead.

W1-212.title: editPost caps plain posts at 5000 chars while createPost accepts 20000, so a legitimately created long post can never be edited
W1-212.expected: Per the letters spec ("content max becomes conditional: 5000 for 'post', 20000 for 'letter'"), the create and edit paths enforce the same per-kind cap; anything you could post you can edit.
W1-212.actual: postSchema is a flat `content: z.string().min(1).max(20000)` for BOTH kinds, and the composer has no length limit on the contentEditable (only a soft "This might make a lovely Letter" nudge at 600 chars). So a member can post 5001-20000 chars as a plain post through the normal UI. editPost then enforces `const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000; if (!content || content.length > cap) return { error: ... }` — opening the edit dialog on such a post and saving (even with zero changes) is refused with "Content must be between 1 and 5000 characters".
W1-212.evidence: validators.ts:154 `content: z.string().min(1, "Post cannot be empty").max(20000)` with no kind conditionality; actions.ts:395-399 `const isLetter = post.kind === "letter"; const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000; if (!content || content.length > cap) { return { error: \`Content must be between 1 and ${cap} characters\` }; }`. create-post-form.tsx has no maxLength on the editor (LETTER_NUDGE_LEN = 600 is explicitly "no red numbers, no limits messaging: just a hint").
W1-212.fixDirection: Make the caps agree: either refine postSchema to a conditional max (5000 when kind !== 'letter') so creation matches the spec, or raise editPost's post cap to 20000 to match what creation already allows. Pick one number and enforce it in both places from one shared constant.
W1-212.gateOrTest: Unit test: create a 6000-char kind:'post' payload through postSchema and through editPost's validation, asserting the two verdicts agree.
W1-212.reproPlan: Live, test account: paste ~6000 chars into the composer, post it (succeeds), then Edit and Save unchanged — refused with the 5000 error. Delete the test post after.

W1-213.title: createComment never verifies parentId belongs to postId: a crafted reply renders inside another post's thread and inflates the wrong post's count
W1-213.expected: Server actions are public HTTP endpoints: parentId must be validated as a comment ON the same post the comment is being written to (6c: Zod-validate everything including IDs and their relationships).
W1-213.actual: The parent check selects only `{ parentId: true, deletedAt: true, isHidden: true }` — never postId — so a caller who can view post A can pass a parentId from post B. The row is created with postId=A, parentId=(root on B). Consequences: (1) loadComments' rows query has NO postId constraint — `OR: [{ id: { in: rootIds }, ...VISIBLE_COMMENT }, { parentId: { in: rootIds }, ...VISIBLE_COMMENT }]` — so the comment RENDERS as a reply inside post B's thread while (2) it counts toward post A's `_count.comments` (which filters by postId), permanently desyncing A's count from A's visible thread; (3) the reply notification goes to B's root author even when B sits inside a private group the caller was never checked against (canViewPost ran on A only).
W1-213.evidence: actions.ts 581-594: `const parent = await prisma.comment.findUnique({ where: { id: parentId }, select: { parentId: true, deletedAt: true, isHidden: true } });` — no postId in the select and no `parent.postId !== parsed.data.postId` comparison anywhere. actions.ts 1147-1152 quoted above shows the thread fetch keyed purely on rootIds.
W1-213.fixDirection: Select postId in the parent lookup and refuse when `parent.postId !== parsed.data.postId` (same "That comment is gone" answer to avoid an oracle). Optionally also add `postId` to the loadComments rows where-clause as defense in depth.
W1-213.gateOrTest: Unit test on the action: comment on post A with a parentId from post B must be refused. A -rule-style test is not possible (needs DB), so an integration test or a code-review regression grep.
W1-213.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would write a malformed row into the shared production database).

W1-214.title: Feed time filters (today/week/month/year) compute boundaries in server UTC, shifting every window 5h30m for IST members
W1-214.expected: "Today" for a member in India means since midnight IST; "This week/month/year" likewise anchor to IST boundaries.
W1-214.actual: getTimeFilterDate runs inside the server action on Vercel (UTC): `new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate())` is UTC midnight = 05:30 IST. A post written at 01:00 IST today is excluded from "Today" until it silently reappears the member's tomorrow; "This week" starts Sunday 05:30 IST (`d.setDate(d.getDate() - d.getDay())` on the UTC date); on the 1st of a month before 05:30 IST, "This month" still shows last month's window. This is the deeper query-window instance of the IST class — distinct from the already-tracked display-side toLocaleDateString note in bugs.md item 6.
W1-214.evidence: actions.ts 742-760: `case "today": return new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate());` etc., with `const now = new Date()` in a server action; the filter is applied as `createdAt: { gte: timeDate }` at line 831. Members are IST (brief), servers UTC.
W1-214.fixDirection: Compute the boundary in Asia/Kolkata: derive the IST calendar date (e.g. via Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone 'Asia/Kolkata' or by adding 330 minutes before truncating, then subtracting them back) and use that instant for gte. One helper, unit-testable with fixed clock values either side of 18:30 UTC.
W1-214.gateOrTest: Unit test on the extracted boundary helper: at 2026-08-21T20:00:00Z (01:30 IST Aug 22), 'today' must start at 2026-08-21T18:30:00Z, not 2026-08-21T00:00:00Z.
W1-214.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof needs a post written 00:00-05:30 IST and the filter checked before 05:30 IST).

W1-215.title: Keyset 'Load more' silently truncates the feed when the cursor post has been deleted
W1-215.expected: Pagination survives a row deleted at the page boundary: the next page picks up from the cursor's position or degrades gracefully.
W1-215.actual: The cursor is the last post's id (`cursor: { id: keysetCursor }, skip: 1`). deletePost is a HARD delete, so if that exact post is deleted between pages (author or admin), Prisma cannot locate the cursor row and `findMany` returns an empty list; the code then computes `hasMore = rows.length > PAGE_SIZE` = false and `nextCursor = null` — the member's "Load more" quietly ends the feed even though older posts exist, until a full refresh. The same failure exists for comment threads (loadComments cursors on a root comment id) in the narrower case of a root hard-deleted by account purge (soft deletes keep the row, so the ordinary delete path is safe there).
W1-215.evidence: actions.ts 874-885: `const keysetCursor = opts?.cursor && !opts.cursor.startsWith("offset:") ? opts.cursor : undefined; rows = await prisma.post.findMany({ where, include, orderBy: [{ createdAt: "desc" }, { id: "desc" }], take: PAGE_SIZE + 1, ...(keysetCursor ? { cursor: { id: keysetCursor }, skip: 1 } : {}) });` — Prisma's documented behavior for a non-existent cursor row is an empty result set, and nothing here distinguishes that from a genuine end of feed. Secondary: the offset branch (line 888) does `parseInt(opts.cursor.slice(7), 10) || 0` with no lower bound, so a crafted "offset:-1" makes Prisma throw on negative skip (self-inflicted only).
W1-215.fixDirection: Switch the cursor to VALUES rather than a row reference: pass the last row's (createdAt, id) and use a where-clause seek (`OR [ createdAt < c, { createdAt: c, id < lastId } ]`), which is immune to the cursor row disappearing. Alternatively detect the empty-page-with-cursor case and retry without the cursor from the last known createdAt. Clamp the offset branch to >= 0 while there.
W1-215.gateOrTest: Integration test: load page 1, delete the 20th post, request page 2 with the stale cursor, assert older posts still return.
W1-215.reproPlan: Live, test account, feed with 21+ posts: scroll to get a cursor, delete the boundary post from another tab, press Load more — the feed ends early. Requires deleting only a test post.

W1-216.title: Post reports have no per-(reporter, post) dedupe: one member can file report after report on the same post, each paging the admins and opening a new thread
W1-216.expected: Same as user-flags: a second report of the same post by the same member is answered "we've already got it" without a second AdminThread or a second admin notification (reportUser does exactly this).
W1-216.actual: reportPost goes straight from the existence check to `prisma.report.create` — no findFirst against (reporterId, postId), and the schema constraint cannot help: `@@unique([reporterId, reportedUserId])` with the schema's own comment "Post reports carry reportedUserId = NULL, and Postgres treats NULLs as distinct in a unique index, so this constrains only user-to-user reports and leaves post reporting unaffected." Every duplicate creates a Report row, an AdminThread, a reporter notification, and notifyAdmins — bounded only by rateLimit('reports') at 10/24h plus the thread budget, so one motivated member can generate ~10 duplicate admin pages a day per post, indefinitely.
W1-216.evidence: report-action.ts 90-117: `const post = await prisma.post.findUnique(...); if (!post) return ...; const report = await prisma.report.create({ data: { targetType: "post", postId, reporterId: session.user.id, reason: trimmed } ... }); const thread = await openReportThread(...); await notifyAdmins(...)` — contrast reportUser's lines 166-172 (`const already = await prisma.report.findFirst({ where: { reporterId, reportedUserId, targetType: "user" } }); if (already) return { success: true, alreadyFlagged: true };`) plus its P2002 fallback.
W1-216.fixDirection: Mirror reportUser: findFirst on { reporterId, postId, targetType: 'post' } and return { success, alreadyFlagged } without a new thread; back it with a partial unique index in a manual migration (`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON "Report" ("reporterId", "postId") WHERE "targetType" = 'post'`) and catch P2002 the same way, since Prisma's schema can't express the partial index (same pattern as the lower() indexes note).
W1-216.gateOrTest: Unit/integration: reportPost twice for the same (reporter, post) → second returns alreadyFlagged and creates no second AdminThread row.
W1-216.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would page the real admin account twice).

W1-217.title: deletePost/deleteDraft delete R2 images BEFORE the row delete, inverting the ordering rule account-purge documents; a failed row delete strands a live post with dead images
W1-217.expected: Bytes are deleted only after the row delete succeeds — account-purge.ts states the invariant: "bytes are deleted only AFTER the row delete succeeds, because if the delete throws and rolls back, the member still exists and their images must keep rendering."
W1-217.actual: deletePost runs `await deletePostImages(post.images); await prisma.post.delete({ where: { id: postId } });` and deleteDraft the same. If `post.delete` then fails (pooler timeout, transient DB error — exactly the 6k chaos case), the post survives with every image URL returning 404/broken forever; delImage is irreversible. deleteDraft has the identical ordering for draft letters. (The reverse leak — row gone, delImage silently failing — is bounded and acknowledged, but this direction is user-visible corruption.) Related orphan in the same file: editPost's draft image rewrite (lines 409-445) replaces the `images` array without deleting the R2 objects for URLs dropped from the draft, and no cron/sweep exists anywhere under src/app/api to collect unreferenced upload objects.
W1-217.evidence: actions.ts 336-339: `// Delete image files\n  await deletePostImages(post.images);\n  await prisma.post.delete({ where: { id: postId } });` — and 250-252 in deleteDraft. account-purge.ts 79-86 quotes the correct ordering with its rationale, written by the same codebase for the same operation.
W1-217.fixDirection: Swap the order in deletePost and deleteDraft: delete the row first, then best-effort delImage of the collected URLs (delImage already never throws). For editPost's draft image swap, diff old vs new arrays and delImage the removed ones after a successful update.
W1-217.gateOrTest: Code-level regression test or review gate asserting `post.delete` precedes deletePostImages in both actions (grep-based check in the write-path reviewer's checklist).
W1-217.reproPlan: code-argument-only (proving it live requires inducing a DB failure mid-action).

W1-218.title: Missing indexes on hot foreign keys: Like.postId, Bookmark.postId, PollVote.postId/pollOptionId, CommentLike.commentId, Comment.parentId, Post.authorId
W1-218.expected: Every column the feed aggregates or cascades on has an index; at 2,000 users the Like table (plausibly 10^5-10^6 rows) must never be sequentially scanned per feed page.
W1-218.actual: Like, Bookmark, PollVote and CommentLike each carry only `@@unique([userId, ...])` — userId-leading, unusable for lookups by postId/commentId/pollOptionId. Every loadPosts/loadSavedPosts page computes `_count: { select: { comments: {...}, likes: true } }` plus per-option `_count: { select: { votes: true } }`, which Prisma resolves as aggregates keyed by postId/pollOptionId — full scans of those tables per page without the index. Postgres also checks FK references on every DELETE: a hard post delete scans Like/Bookmark/PollVote by postId, and a user purge cascade scans Comment by parentId (unindexed) once per deleted comment. Post has `@@index([groupId, createdAt])`, `([kind, createdAt])`, `([createdAt])` but nothing on authorId, so the profile Posts tab and collectImageUrls filter by authorId unindexed. Only Comment(postId, ...) was ever indexed (manual migration 2026-07-18).
W1-218.evidence: schema.prisma Like: `@@unique([userId, postId])` and nothing else (lines 457-466); Bookmark: `@@unique([userId, postId])` (428); PollVote: `@@unique([userId, postId])` only (616); CommentLike: `@@unique([userId, commentId])` only (627); Comment relations (447-450) with `@@index([postId, createdAt]) @@index([postId, isHidden])` but no parentId index; Post indexes at 414-416 lack authorId. grep of prisma/migrations-manual/ shows only Comment_postId_isHidden_idx was ever added by hand.
W1-218.fixDirection: Add `@@index([postId])` to Like and Bookmark, `@@index([postId])` and `@@index([pollOptionId])` to PollVote, `@@index([commentId])` to CommentLike, `@@index([parentId])` to Comment, `@@index([authorId, createdAt])` to Post — via a dated idempotent file in prisma/migrations-manual/ (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, never db push) plus the schema.prisma lines and prisma generate, per the repo's schema-change rule.
W1-218.gateOrTest: EXPLAIN ANALYZE the feed page's like-count aggregate before/after in Supabase (read-only), or the check-suite gaining a schema lint that every relation scalar has a covering index.
W1-218.reproPlan: Read-only: run EXPLAIN on `SELECT "postId", count(*) FROM "Like" WHERE "postId" = ANY($1) GROUP BY 1` against the live DB and observe Seq Scan.

W1-219.title: No error handling on any feed client data path: a failed load leaves an infinite skeleton, a failed action leaves controls stuck disabled
W1-219.expected: 6k: DB slow/down mid-request — the member sees something actionable (an error line, a retry), and controls recover.
W1-219.actual: Every fetch is `promise.then(...)` with no .catch and every handler awaits without try/catch: (1) PostFeed's first-page effect — on rejection `setLoading(false)` never runs, the skeleton spins forever with no message; (2) handleLoadMore — `setLoadingMore(false)` skipped, the button reads "Loading..." permanently; (3) CommentsSection's initial loadComments — same infinite skeleton; (4) the IntersectionObserver page fetch — `loadingMoreRef.current = false` never resets, killing infinite scroll for the rest of the session; (5) comment handleSubmit — `setSubmitting(false)` skipped so the send button stays disabled with the member's text captive in the box; (6) same shape in ProfileAuthorFeed and SavedPostsFeed. On flaky mobile networks (the community's dominant access) these are routine, not exotic.
W1-219.evidence: post-feed.tsx 118-138: `fetchPosts(null).then((data) => { ... setLoading(false); ... });` — no catch. comments-section.tsx 166-173 inside the observer: `loadingMoreRef.current = true; const data = await loadComments(...); ... loadingMoreRef.current = false;` — an async IO callback with no try/finally. handleSubmit 191-205: `const result = await createComment(formData); ... setSubmitting(false);` — a rejection skips the last line.
W1-219.fixDirection: Wrap each await in try/catch/finally: finally resets the pending flag; catch shows a toast ("Couldn't load the feed — check your connection") and, for list loads, renders a retry affordance instead of the skeleton. A tiny shared helper (e.g. safeAction wrapper returning { error } on throw) would cover all seven sites uniformly.
W1-219.gateOrTest: Playwright with route interception: abort the loadPosts action response and assert an error/retry state renders instead of a perpetual skeleton.
W1-219.reproPlan: Live via chrome-devtools MCP: open /feed, use network emulation to fail the next server-action request, trigger Load more — observe the button stuck at "Loading...".

W1-220.title: List queries lack the author self-exemption the single-post rule has: your own city-scoped post vanishes from your own feed, profile and letters index if you remove that city
W1-220.expected: decidePostVisibility establishes the rule: "Your own post is always yours" (authorId check before every scope check). The list queries should agree: an author always sees their own posts in their feed, their profile Posts tab, and the letters index.
W1-220.actual: loadPosts (non-admin) appends `cityScopeWhere(viewerCities)` unconditionally to AND, and cityScopeWhere is only `OR: [{ cityScope: null }, { cityScope: { in: viewerCities } }]` — no `{ authorId: viewer.id }` arm. A member who posts "Bengaluru only" and later removes Bengaluru from their UserPlaces loses sight of their OWN post everywhere it is listed (main feed, ProfileAuthorFeed via the same loadPosts, /letters index which spreads the same fragment), while canViewPost would still admit them — so a notification deep-link works but the lists deny the post exists, and they can no longer reach its card to edit or delete it. The batch-targeting OR (lines 838-843) has the same gap for legacy targetBatches rows.
W1-220.evidence: actions.ts:820 `if (!isAdmin) andConditions.push(cityScopeWhere(viewerCities));` composed into baseWhere with no author arm; city-scope.ts 20-27 shows the fragment; post-visibility-rule.ts:74 `if (post.authorId === viewer.id) return { ok: true, post };` is the single-post exemption the lists never mirror.
W1-220.fixDirection: Add `{ authorId: viewerId }` as an extra OR arm inside cityScopeWhere (take the viewer id as a parameter), and add the same arm to the batch-targeting OR in loadPosts and the letters index, so the list rule equals decidePostVisibility.
W1-220.gateOrTest: Extend post-visibility-rule.test.mjs's philosophy with an integration test: author with zero matching cities still receives their own city-scoped post from loadPosts.
W1-220.reproPlan: Live, test account: add a city, post scoped to it, remove the city in settings, reload /feed and the profile Posts tab — the post is gone from both while its direct letter/notification URL still opens.

W1-221.title: Letter reading page and its generateMetadata skip the targetBatches check the visibility rule enforces — batch-targeted letters readable by direct URL
W1-221.expected: decidePostVisibility refuses "other-batch": a post/letter with targetBatches is visible only to viewers whose `${batchType}-${batchYear}` key appears in it. The letter page should give the same 404 it gives for other-city and drafts.
W1-221.actual: LetterPage hand-rolls the checks — isHidden, draft+author, group membership, canViewCityScope — but never consults targetBatches, so any signed-in member with the URL reads a batch-targeted letter in full (and generateMetadata leaks its real title the same way). This is precisely the divergence post-visibility.ts warns about ("security logic pasted into several files and then quietly diverging"); the page predates/bypasses the shared canViewPost. Mitigating: the current composer never sets targetBatches (no formData.set for it in create-post-form.tsx), so only legacy rows are affected today — but loadPosts, the letters index, and decidePostVisibility all still enforce it, so the field is live in every OTHER path.
W1-221.evidence: letters/[id]/page.tsx 93-106: the full check sequence is `if (isDraft && !isAuthor) notFound(); if (letter.groupId) {...membership...}; if (!(await canViewCityScope(letter.cityScope, session.user))) notFound();` — targetBatches never read. post-visibility-rule.ts 100-105: `if (post.targetBatches) { const key = \`${viewer.batchType}-${viewer.batchYear}\`; if (!post.targetBatches.includes(key)) { return { ok: false, reason: "other-batch" }; } }`.
W1-221.fixDirection: Replace the page's hand-rolled sequence (and generateMetadata's) with one call to canViewPost(letter-as-GuardedPost) / decidePostVisibility — the row is already fetched with every needed column — keeping the author-draft special handling it already gets from the rule.
W1-221.gateOrTest: Add a case to post-visibility-rule.test.mjs-style coverage asserting the letter page path uses the shared rule (integration test: other-batch viewer + targeted letter URL → 404).
W1-221.reproPlan: Live only if a legacy targetBatches letter exists (read-only check: query Post where targetBatches is not null); otherwise code-argument-only.

W1-222.title: Unverified members cannot save letter drafts, contradicting the codebase's own documented intent that drafts stay ungated
W1-222.expected: Per publishDraft's own comment: "Drafts themselves stay ungated on purpose: writing privately harms nobody, and somebody waiting on a confirmation email should not lose what they were working on." The gate should bite at publish, not at save.
W1-222.actual: The FIRST save of a fresh draft goes through createPost, which runs `requireVerifiedMember()` before ever reading saveAsDraft — and the gate requires both emailConfirmed AND verifyState === 'verified' (Stage 2). Resumed-draft autosave and manual saves go through editPost, which gates identically ("Editing is publishing again"). So a Stage 0/1 member who writes a long letter at /letters/new and clicks "Save as draft" is refused; their work exists only in the browser tab, which is exactly the loss the comment says the design avoids. Only deleteDraft and publishDraft's own flow treat drafts as private.
W1-222.evidence: actions.ts 48-57 (createPost): `const gate = await requireVerifiedMember(); if (!gate.ok) return { error: gate.error };` runs unconditionally; the saveAsDraft branch is only consulted at line 133. actions.ts 207-210 (publishDraft) carries the quoted intent comment. member-gate.ts 59-60: `if (!session.user.emailConfirmed) return {...EMAIL_UNVERIFIED}; if (session.user.verifyState !== "verified") return {...MEMBER_UNVERIFIED};`.
W1-222.fixDirection: In createPost, evaluate isDraft (kind letter + saveAsDraft) BEFORE the member gate and skip the gate for drafts (keep the rate limit); in editPost, skip the gate when the target row is the caller's own draft (the author+status check already runs). publishDraft keeps the gate, which is what actually protects the community.
W1-222.gateOrTest: Integration test: a user with verifyState 'pending' can createPost(saveAsDraft) and editPost their draft, but publishDraft is refused with MEMBER_UNVERIFIED.
W1-222.reproPlan: Live with an unverified test account: write at /letters/new, Save as draft — observe the verification dialog/toast instead of a saved draft.

W1-223.title: Like toggling is un-rate-limited and mints a fresh notification on every re-like: unbounded bell spam for the author
W1-223.expected: Toggling a heart on and off does not multiply notifications; write actions are metered (the file's own M2 pattern: posts and comments both call rateLimit).
W1-223.actual: toggleLike and toggleCommentLike have NO rateLimit call (grep confirms the file's only two are 'posts' at line 60 and 'comments' at line 561), and each like-after-unlike creates a brand-new Notification row (`prisma.notification.create` inside the create branch, with no dedupe against an existing like-notification for the same (actor, post) and no cleanup on unlike). A member holding the heart in a toggle loop generates one DB write pair + one notification per cycle, limited only by network round-trip: the author's bell fills with dozens of identical "X liked your post" rows. The 100-per-user prune bounds the table, not the experience, and votePoll/toggleBookmark share the missing meter (bookmark at least writes no notification).
W1-223.evidence: actions.ts 465-475: gate then straight to the toggle — no `rateLimit(` in the function; 496-511: `if (post && post.authorId !== session.user.id) { await prisma.notification.create({ data: { userId: post.authorId, type: "like", message: \`${session.user.name} liked your post\`, ... } }); }` runs on every create, unconditionally.
W1-223.fixDirection: Add a generous rateLimit bucket for engagement toggles (e.g. 60/10m per user) to toggleLike/toggleCommentLike/votePoll/toggleBookmark; dedupe the notification (skip create if an unread 'like' notification from this actor for this post already exists, or delete the notification on unlike).
W1-223.gateOrTest: Integration test: like-unlike-like the same post; assert the author holds exactly one like notification.
W1-223.reproPlan: Live with two test accounts: toggle a heart 5 times on the second account's post, open its bell — five identical rows.

W1-224.title: Account purge hard-deletes a member's comments, silently promoting other members' replies to top-level — the exact corruption the soft-delete design exists to prevent
W1-224.expected: Deleting an account removes the member's words the way deleteComment does: content blanked, row kept as structure, so surviving replies keep their "[deleted]" anchor and threads keep their shape.
W1-224.actual: purgeUserAccount runs `prisma.user.delete`, which cascades Comment rows via `author User @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade)`. The self-referencing parent relation has no onDelete, so it defaults to SetNull — and the schema's own comment on deletedAt states the consequence verbatim: "a hard delete would orphan them (the FK is SetNull, which silently promotes replies to top level) and the thread would lie about its shape." The owner hit this live on 2026-08-13 for single-comment deletes and the fix was the soft delete; the purge path (admin delete + 60-day retention sweep, both calling purgeUserAccount) re-introduces it wholesale: every reply anyone ever wrote under the purged member's comments becomes a context-free top-level comment.
W1-224.evidence: account-purge.ts 99-102: `await prisma.$transaction([ prisma.report.deleteMany({ where: { reporterId: userId } }), prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } }) ]);` — no comment tombstoning. schema.prisma 447-450: `author User @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)` and `parent Comment? @relation("CommentReplies", fields: [parentId], references: [id])` (no onDelete → SetNull), plus the 438-443 design comment quoted above.
W1-224.fixDirection: Before the user.delete in purgeUserAccount's transaction, soft-tombstone their comments instead of letting the cascade take them: `updateMany({ where: { authorId: userId }, data: { deletedAt: now, content: "" } })` will not survive the cascade, so either detach authorship (make Comment.authorId nullable with SetNull, matching AdminMessage's pattern) or excise the rows properly (delete their childless comments, tombstone the ones with replies by reassigning to a system user). The AdminMessage model (authorId String? with SetNull, comment: "Null ... for anyone whose account is later deleted") is the in-repo precedent.
W1-224.gateOrTest: Integration test: A comments, B replies, purge A → B's reply must still render under a [deleted] stub, not as a top-level comment.
W1-224.reproPlan: code-argument-only (proving it live means purging an account against the shared production database).

W1-225.title: createPost and createComment double-submit windows: no unique guard exists for either, and the comment form lacks even the in-flight check
W1-225.expected: 6c: double-invocation before pending state disables the control must not create duplicate rows; the DB unique constraint is the only real guard.
W1-225.actual: Post and Comment have no unique constraint that could dedupe (nor could they, being free text), so the only guard is client pending state — and it is incomplete. CommentsSection.handleSubmit checks `if (!newComment.trim()) return;` but never `if (submitting) return` (contrast PollDisplay.handleVote, which has the guard); the submit control's `disabled` only takes effect after React re-renders, so two submissions in the same frame (Enter keydown + click, or key repeat racing the render) both reach createComment and write two identical comments plus two notifications. CreatePostForm.handleSubmit has the same missing guard (`if (!content.trim()) return;` then straight to work) with the same disabled-after-render window on the Post button — duplicates here are whole duplicate posts. Server-side nothing dedupes: rateLimit(10/10m posts, 30/10m comments) admits both.
W1-225.evidence: comments-section.tsx 181-184: `async function handleSubmit(e){ e.preventDefault(); if (!newComment.trim()) return; setSubmitting(true); ...` — no submitting check. create-post-form.tsx 497-500: `async function handleSubmit(saveAsDraft = false) { if (!content.trim()) return; if (saveAsDraft) setSavingDraft(true); else setSubmitting(true);` — same. poll-display.tsx:81 `if (submitting) return;` shows the intended pattern.
W1-225.fixDirection: Add `if (submitting || savingDraft) return;` as the first line of both handleSubmit functions (state read is the render-scope value, so also guard with a ref for same-frame safety: an inFlightRef.current check set synchronously). Optionally, server-side, a cheap recency dedupe (identical content by same author on same post within a few seconds → return the existing row) as backstop.
W1-225.gateOrTest: Playwright: dispatch two submit events in one tick on the comment form; assert one comment row appears.
W1-225.reproPlan: Live, test account: hold Enter in the comment box on a slow connection (or dispatch form.requestSubmit() twice from the console) and observe duplicate comments.

W1-226.title: PollDisplay: tapping your already-chosen option optimistically inflates its count without adjusting the total (percentages exceed 100%)
W1-226.expected: Re-selecting the option you already voted for is a no-op visually.
W1-226.actual: handleVote's optimistic map gives the tapped option +1 in its first branch and only decrements prevVoted in the second — when they are the SAME option the +1 wins and no -1 happens, while localTotal is unchanged (`prevVoted ? t : t + 1`). One voter tapping their own choice renders 2 votes on the option over a total of 1 → the bar and CountUp show 200%. The server call succeeds (vote-switch to the same option), so the revert never runs and the lie persists until reload.
W1-226.evidence: poll-display.tsx 90-101: `voteCount: o.id === optionId ? o.voteCount + 1 : o.id === prevVoted ? o.voteCount - 1 : o.voteCount` — with optionId === prevVoted the first arm shadows the second; `setLocalTotal((t) => (prevVoted ? t : t + 1));` leaves the denominator alone.
W1-226.fixDirection: Early-return when `optionId === voted` (nothing to do), or make the map handle the equal case (net zero).
W1-226.gateOrTest: Component test: vote option A, tap A again, assert A's displayed count unchanged.
W1-226.reproPlan: Live, test account on a test poll: vote, then tap the same option — watch its percentage jump.

W1-227.title: PostFeed 'Load more' has no cancellation: a stale page from the previous filter/sort is appended after the filters change; offset sorts also duplicate rows across pages
W1-227.expected: Out-of-order completion never clobbers newer state (6b class 3), and a paginated list never renders one post twice.
W1-227.actual: handleLoadMore captures nothing to cancel: click Load more, then switch sort/search — the first-page effect (which DOES have a `cancelled` guard) replaces posts for the new filter, then the in-flight loadMore resolves and blindly runs `setPosts((prev) => [...prev, ...data.posts])`, appending old-filter posts under the new list, with cursor/hasMore overwritten by the stale response. Separately, the count-based sorts fall back to OFFSET paging (`skip: offset` while like/comment counts shift between requests), so a post can straddle a page boundary and appear twice; keys are `key={post.id}` with no dedupe in PostFeed (CommentsSection's mergeComments dedupes; PostFeed does not), producing React duplicate-key warnings and visibly duplicated cards.
W1-227.evidence: post-feed.tsx 152-159: `async function handleLoadMore() { setLoadingMore(true); const data = await fetchPosts(cursor); setPosts((prev) => [...prev, ...data.posts]); ... }` — no generation counter or cancelled flag; actions.ts 887-905 is the offset branch (`skip: offset` on a live-reordering orderBy).
W1-227.fixDirection: Keep a request-generation ref (incremented whenever filters change or a new fetch starts); handleLoadMore discards its response if the generation moved. Dedupe on append the way mergeComments does (filter incoming ids already present).
W1-227.gateOrTest: Component test: resolve a delayed loadMore after a filter change; assert posts contains only the new filter's page.
W1-227.reproPlan: Live: throttle network in devtools, click Load more, immediately switch to Most liked — old-sort posts append below the new list.

W1-228.title: Silent hard caps with no pagination: saved posts stop at 120, the letters index at 40 — older items become unreachable with no indication
W1-228.expected: Either pagination or an honest "showing the latest N" line on every capped list.
W1-228.actual: loadSavedPosts is `take: 120` with no cursor support and SavedPostsFeed fetches once with no load-more — a member's 121st-oldest bookmark silently ceases to exist anywhere in the UI (the header even asserts the visible count as the total: "{visibleCount} saved posts"). The letters index is `take: 40` with no load-more either; once the community passes 40 published letters, older ones are reachable only through feed search or a profile page. At 2,000 users over a few years both caps will be hit in normal use.
W1-228.evidence: actions.ts 963-980: `const rows = await prisma.bookmark.findMany({ ... orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }, take: 120, ...})` and no cursor parameter in the function signature; letters/page.tsx 60-62: `orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }, take: 40,` with no pagination UI in the render.
W1-228.fixDirection: Add keyset pagination to loadSavedPosts (cursor on bookmark createdAt/id) with a Load more in SavedPostsFeed; give the letters index either a Load more (same keyset shape loadPosts already implements) or reuse PostFeed with scope 'letters'.
W1-228.gateOrTest: Integration: seed 41 letters / 121 bookmarks for a test account and assert the UI can reach the oldest one.

W1-229.title: Fire-and-forget DB writes in server components (feed search log, letter view counter) can die on serverless before committing; recordView also fires before the visibility checks
W1-229.expected: 6f: nothing runs after the response without after()/waitUntil — the codebase already knows this (createPost wraps its Collection copy in `after()`). Analytics writes should either use after() or accept documented loss; a view should only be recorded for content the viewer was actually allowed to see.
W1-229.actual: FeedPage runs `void logSearch({...})` and LetterPage runs `void recordView(session.user.id, "letter", letter.id)` as bare unawaited promises inside RSC render — on Vercel the function can freeze after the stream ends with the prisma write un-flushed, so both metrics undercount unpredictably (both helpers swallow their own errors, so nothing crashes — this is a loss, not a 500). Additionally recordView is called at line 85 BEFORE the draft/group/city notFound() checks at 91-106, so a member probing a private group letter's id records a "view" of content they were then refused; and unlike profiles (`if (kind === "profile" && viewerId === targetId) return`), letter self-views are counted, so an author polishing their own letter inflates its open count.
W1-229.evidence: feed/page.tsx 29-32: `if (q) { const s = await auth(); void logSearch({ scope: "feed", query: q, userId: s?.user?.id }); }`; letters/[id]/page.tsx 85 sits above `if (isDraft && !isAuthor) notFound();` at 93. content-view.ts 26: only the profile kind drops self-views.
W1-229.fixDirection: Wrap both calls in `after(() => ...)` (already imported and used in feed/actions.ts); move recordView below the last notFound() and add `viewerId === letter.authorId` to the self-view drop (or extend the kind check in recordView).
W1-229.gateOrTest: Code-review gate: grep for `void logSearch|void recordView` outside after() in server components.
W1-229.reproPlan: code-argument-only (loss is probabilistic on serverless freeze).

W1-230.title: Blocked members' posts and comments remain in every feed under their linked name while the directory excludes them
W1-230.expected: A consistent policy for a blocked account's existing content: either it stays visible by explicit decision, or feeds filter it the way the directory does (schema comment on line 67: a deletion-requested account is "held out of the directory and search the same way a blocked one is").
W1-230.actual: `isBlocked` ends sessions (credentialVersion revocation) and hides the person from directory/search, but loadPosts/loadComments/letters queries have no `author: { isBlocked: false }` condition — a member blocked for abusive content keeps every post, comment and letter live in the feed with a working link to their profile until an admin soft-hides each item one by one. Suspected rather than confirmed as a defect because keep-content-visible is a defensible moderation policy; flagged because the directory and feed currently disagree and no comment records the choice.
W1-230.evidence: actions.ts baseWhere (822-832) filters `isHidden`, PUBLISHED_ONLY, batch, city — nothing about the author's standing; grep of the feed/letters queries finds no isBlocked reference anywhere in the territory.
W1-230.fixDirection: Owner decision first: if blocked content should vanish, add `author: { isBlocked: false }` to loadPosts/loadSavedPosts/loadComments/letters queries (indexed via the User pk join, cheap); if it should stay, record the decision in the schema comment so the asymmetry is deliberate.
W1-230.gateOrTest: Once decided: integration test blocking a fixture author and asserting feed behavior matches the decision.
W1-230.reproPlan: code-argument-only (blocking a real account is an admin write).

W1-231.title: Email normalization inconsistent across signup/login/reset: mixed-case signups can never receive a password reset and must match case exactly at login
W1-231.expected: One email address = one account, findable by every flow regardless of how the case was typed. Signup, login lookup, and reset lookup should all normalize (trim + lowercase) identically before touching User.email.
W1-231.actual: Signup stores the address AS TYPED (zod v4 z.email() validates format only, no lowercasing; registerUser writes parsed.data.email straight through). Login looks up the RAW typed value case-sensitively. Password reset is the only flow that lowercases before lookup, so it can never find a row stored with any uppercase letter — and it answers { ok: true } either way, so the member gets no error and no mail, forever.
W1-231.evidence: Signup (src/components/auth/actions.ts:146-149): `user = await prisma.user.create({ data: { name, email: parsed.data.email, ...` — validators.ts:18 is `email: z.email("Please enter a valid email")`, no .toLowerCase(), and signup-form.tsx does not lowercase client-side (verified by grep). Login (src/lib/auth.ts:102-104): `const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } })` — the raw credentials value; only the rate-limit key is normalized (`const acctKey = email.trim().toLowerCase()` at auth.ts:62), so the lookup itself is case-sensitive against a case-sensitive Postgres unique. Reset (src/components/auth/email-actions.ts:160-166): `const raw = ((formData.get("email") as string) ?? "").trim().toLowerCase(); ... prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email: raw } })` then `if (!user?.password) return { ok: true };` — a mixed-case-stored account silently falls into the no-account branch. Three concrete symptoms: (a) a member who signed up as "Ravi@Gmail.com" (phone keyboards capitalize; habit) requests a reset with any casing and receives nothing, with a success message on screen; (b) the same member typing "ravi@gmail.com" at login gets "Invalid email or password" (reason no-account); (c) the same mailbox can register twice under two casings — User.email @unique (schema.prisma:13) is case-sensitive, so both rows coexist, confounding roster matching and the reset flow. dev-login (route.ts:91) also looks up raw. LoginAttempt (schema.prisma:1063) documents "Lowercased as submitted" for its own analytics, showing normalization was understood as needed but never applied to the account flows.
W1-231.fixDirection: Introduce one normalizeEmail(s) = s.trim().toLowerCase() helper and apply it at every entry: registerUser before validation/store, authorize() before findUnique, requestPasswordReset (already does), dev-login. Then a one-off manual migration lowercasing existing User.email rows — first SELECT for case-insensitive duplicates (lower(email) collisions) and resolve any by hand (the adminMergeUsers action exists for this) before adding/relying on the lowercase invariant. Also lowercase AuthToken.sentTo comparisons if any are case-sensitive.
W1-231.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof requires creating a mixed-case account in the SHARED production database; the quoted lookups make the argument complete without it)
W1-231.gateOrTest: New unit test (e.g. src/lib/normalize-email.test.mjs) asserting the shared helper is used by feeding a mixed-case address through signupSchema+registerUser path and asserting the stored/queried value; add to the 14-test suite npm run check runs.

W1-232.title: Onboarding updateProfile action validates nothing: seven profile columns writable with no length caps (up to the 25MB action body limit)
W1-232.expected: Every write path to a profile column enforces the same caps profileSchema does (bio 1000, currentCity 100, workplace 100, jobTitle 100, phone 24, instagram 100, linkedin 200), because the server, not a maxLength attribute, is the guard.
W1-232.actual: The /onboarding page's server action writes bio, currentCity, workplace, jobTitle, phone, instagram, linkedin with zero validation — no Zod, no length caps, no phone normalization, nothing but a trim. The page's own <textarea maxLength={1000}> is the only cap, and it is client-side. With serverActions.bodySizeLimit raised to "25mb" (next.config.ts:112, for photo uploads), a signed-in account can POST a multi-megabyte bio or currentCity directly to this action.
W1-232.evidence: src/app/(auth)/onboarding/actions.ts:12-27 in full: `const data: Record<string, string | null> = {}; const fields = ["bio", "currentCity", "workplace", "jobTitle", "phone", "instagram", "linkedin"]; for (const field of fields) { const value = formData.get(field) as string | null; if (value && value.trim()) { data[field] = value.trim(); } } if (Object.keys(data).length > 0) { await prisma.user.update({ where: { id: session.user.id }, data }); }` — no schema import, no caps. Reachable: page.tsx:16 `import { updateProfile } from "./actions"` and :26 `await updateProfile(formData)`; /onboarding is listed in src/proxy.ts:33. Contrast the settings path writing the same columns: profileSchema (validators.ts:53-111) caps every one, and the newer wizard actions (src/components/onboarding/actions.ts:30-40) Zod-validate everything. Blast radius: currentCity and workplace are serialized into the directory page for every viewer (directory/actions.ts PERSON_SELECT includes currentCity, jobTitle, workplace), so one oversized value bloats the directory HTML for the whole community — a stability problem, not just a data-hygiene one. phone is stored un-normalized here (every other path runs normalizePhone).
W1-232.fixDirection: Run the collected fields through the corresponding subset of profileSchema (or a local zod object with identical caps) before the update; run phone through normalizePhone; alternatively delete this legacy action/page if the /welcome wizard (components/onboarding) has superseded it — verify with the owner which onboarding surface ships.
W1-232.reproPlan: Local dev, own test account: submit the /onboarding form with devtools after removing maxLength, with a ~5k-char bio — confirm it stores. (Write to a test account only; shared DB.) Code argument is sufficient without it.
W1-232.gateOrTest: Extend src/lib/gate-coverage.test.mjs (or add a validation-coverage test) asserting every "use server" file that writes User columns imports a validator; minimally a unit test calling updateProfile with an oversized field and asserting an error.

W1-233.title: updateUserPlaces and adminUpdatePlaces have no schema: unbounded label/city strings, unbounded lat/lng, FK crash on bogus placeId
W1-233.expected: The same placeSchema the onboarding wizard already has (label/city trimmed, 1..160 chars; placeId int-or-null; lat/lng bounded) applied to both bulk city writers, since UserPlace.label mirrors into User.currentCity and renders on the directory for every member.
W1-233.actual: Both actions accept the places array on faith: no length cap on label/city (25MB possible per the action body limit), no numeric bounds or type check on lat/lng, no existence/int check on placeId, and .map(p => p.label.trim()) throws a raw TypeError on any non-string payload. cleaned[0].label is mirrored into User.currentCity, which the directory serializes for every viewer; lat/lng feed the alumni map's cluster math.
W1-233.evidence: src/components/settings/actions.ts:150-159: `const cleaned = places.map((p) => ({ placeId: p.placeId, label: titleCase(p.label.trim()), city: titleCase(p.city.trim()), lat: p.lat, lng: p.lng })).filter((p) => p.label.length > 0).slice(0, 30);` — the ONLY cap is the row count (30). Then :162-181 writes them wholesale and `currentCity: cleaned[0]?.label ?? null`. adminUpdatePlaces (admin/people/actions.ts:139-169) is a verbatim twin. W1-234.title: /directory?year=<non-integer> passes NaN or a float into a Prisma Int filter and error-pages the whole directory
W1-234.expected: A mangled or hand-edited URL param (?year=abc, ?year=2004.5, a truncated shared link) degrades to "no filter" or an empty result, never an error page.
W1-234.actual: buildDirectoryWhere does `filters.year ? Number(filters.year) : null` and then `typeof showingYear === "number"` — NaN IS typeof "number", so where.batchYear becomes NaN; "2004.5" becomes a float. Prisma rejects a non-integer for an Int filter with PrismaClientValidationError, thrown during the page's Promise.all of queries; the only boundary is the root src/app/error.tsx, so the visitor gets the full error page. The same filters flow through the loadDirectoryPage server action (Load more), which throws a digest error.
W1-234.evidence: src/app/(main)/directory/where.ts:27-33: `const showingYear = filters.year === "faculty" ? "faculty" : filters.year ? Number(filters.year) : null; ... } else if (typeof showingYear === "number") { where.batchYear = showingYear; }` — no Number.isInteger guard. yearFrom/yearTo (:29-30, 49-54) are only accidentally NaN-safe because NaN is falsy in `if (yearFrom || yearTo)`, but "2004.5" passes and lands as `{ gte: 2004.5 }` — same throw. The page feeds raw searchParams: page.tsx:205-216 builds filters from params and calls buildDirectoryWhere(filters) with no sanitization; find over src/app shows only the root error.tsx exists, so the crash is a whole-page error state. Prisma's runtime validation of Int arguments rejects float/NaN values ("Invalid value provided. Expected Int").

W1-235.title: createPost accepts 20,000 chars for a plain post but editPost caps plain posts at 5,000 — long posts become uneditable
W1-235.expected: The create cap and the edit cap for the same kind of content are the same number, so any post a member was allowed to write they are allowed to edit.
W1-235.actual: postSchema.content is `z.string().min(1).max(20000)` regardless of kind (the 20000 was sized for letters but applies to plain posts too, and the composer's textarea has no maxLength — only the title has 160). editPost then applies `const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000` — so a 5,001-20,000-char plain post is created fine and every subsequent edit is refused with "Content must be between 1 and 5000 characters" until the member deletes content.

So the server is the only cap and the two paths disagree by 4x.

W1-236.title: Post.targetBatches has no length cap or format validation and is LIKE-scanned by every main-feed query
W1-236.expected: targetBatches is a short comma list of "ISC-2004"-style tokens: capped (~500 chars) and shape-validated, since it participates in the feed's hot-path where clause.
W1-236.actual: `targetBatches: z.string().optional()` — no max, no format. With the 25MB action body limit, a verified member can store a multi-megabyte string in the column. Every main-feed page for every member then evaluates `{ targetBatches: { contains: userBatch } }` against that value, and because loadPosts uses `include` (not select), the full scalar row — the giant column included — is shipped from Postgres to the function whenever the row matches the page window.

The hot path: feed/actions.ts:836-843 — main-feed where always contains `OR: [ { targetBatches: null }, { targetBatches: "" }, { targetBatches: { contains: userBatch } } ]`, an unindexed LIKE against the column for every row scanned on every feed load. loadPosts' `include` at :846-867 returns all Post scalars, so the oversized value also rides back over the pgbouncer connection. There is also no membership check that the named batches are real ("garbage" simply hides the post from everyone including its author, a lesser confusion).
W1-236.fixDirection: Cap at e.g. .max(400) and validate shape (comma-joined `(ISC|ICSE)-\d{4}` tokens, ≤ ~40 entries) in postSchema; reject rather than store anything else. Optionally switch loadPosts to an explicit select to stop over-fetching big text columns (images/content) it does not need for hidden branches.
W1-236.reproPlan: code-argument-only (storing the oversized value would pollute the shared feed).
W1-236.gateOrTest: Unit test on postSchema refusing an oversized/misshapen targetBatches.

W1-237.title: Lookup endpoints accept unbounded query strings: users/search builds one AND-clause per whitespace token
W1-237.expected: Type-ahead endpoints cap query length (~100 chars) and token count (~8) before building SQL, so one request is bounded work regardless of what is pasted.
W1-237.actual: users/search splits the raw q on whitespace with no cap on length or token count and emits one `{ name: { contains: term } }` AND-condition per token — a single request with tens of thousands of space-separated tokens produces tens of thousands of ILIKE clauses and bind params (Postgres caps bind parameters at 65,535; below that it is just an expensive parse+plan per request). places/search interpolates the raw q (any length) into prefix/contains ILIKE patterns over the 234k-row gazetteer. The 120/min rate limit bounds request count, not per-request cost.
W1-237.evidence: users/search/route.ts:30-41: `const q = req.nextUrl.searchParams.get("q")?.trim(); ... const terms = q.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean); const users = await prisma.user.findMany({ where: { AND: terms.map((term) => ({ name: { contains: escapeLike(term), ...insensitive } })), ...` — no q.length cap, no terms.slice(). places/search/route.ts:89-104: `const raw = req.nextUrl.searchParams.get("q")?.trim() ?? ""; if (raw.length < 1) ...` — a minimum but no maximum; `containsPattern = \`%${escaped}%\`` goes into `"altNames" ILIKE ${containsPattern}` for any q ≥ 4 chars. logSearch truncates to 120 chars for storage (search-log.ts:19,45) — the endpoints themselves never got the same cap.
W1-237.fixDirection: At the top of both routes: refuse or truncate q beyond ~100 chars; in users/search additionally `terms.slice(0, 8)`. Mirror in the feed search path (loadPosts opts.search is a single contains, lower risk, but a cap costs nothing).
W1-237.reproPlan: Local dev: GET /api/users/search?q=<10k tokens> signed in and watch the query time / error; harmless read-only.
W1-237.gateOrTest: Unit test on a extracted buildPeopleWhere(q) asserting the token cap; or an e2e asserting 400/trimmed behavior for an oversized q.

W1-238.title: Whitespace-only display name passes profileSchema then titleCase collapses it to empty string
W1-238.expected: A name that is only whitespace is refused (the letterhead path already does this: updateProfileField trims first, then checks length ≥ 2).

BirdAvatar happens to guard (`!user.name ? null : getInitials(...)` at bird-avatar.tsx:700), which also means getInitials' own crash on empty input is dodged, but every text surface shows a nameless account.
W1-238.evidence: validators.ts:54: `name: z.string().min(2).max(100),` — contrast signupSchema:16-17 (`firstName: z.string().trim().min(1...`) and profile-actions.ts:80-87 (`const value = raw.trim(); ... if (value.length < 2) return { error: ... }`), both of which trim before the length check. settings/actions.ts:94 `const cleanName = titleCase(parsed.data.name);` and :112 `name: cleanName,` — normalize.ts:81-82: `const trimmed = input.trim().replace(/\s+/g, " "); if (!trimmed) return trimmed;` returns "" for whitespace-only input. So "  " (or NBSP/ideographic spaces, which JS \s and trim() both match) → stored name "".
W1-238.fixDirection: Change profileSchema to `name: z.string().trim().min(2).max(100)` (zod applies trim before min). While there, reconcile the three name caps (settings 100, letterhead 80, signup up to 101 joined) to one constant.
W1-238.reproPlan: Local dev, own test account: save the settings form with a two-space name; reload and observe the blank byline.

W1-239.title: Negative pagination values reach Prisma unclamped and throw: loadPosts "offset:-1" cursor and loadPhotos page:-1
W1-239.expected: Pagination inputs are clamped to ≥ 0 so a crafted or corrupted cursor degrades to page one, not a thrown server-action error.
W1-239.actual: loadPosts parses the offset cursor with `parseInt(opts.cursor.slice(7), 10) || 0` — radix and NaN are handled but a NEGATIVE offset ("offset:-5") passes straight into `skip: offset`; loadPhotos uses `const page = opts?.page ?? 0` then `skip: page * PAGE_SIZE` with no bound. Prisma rejects negative skip with a PrismaClientValidationError, which neither action catches, so the caller gets the generic digest error instead of an empty page.
W1-239.evidence: feed/actions.ts:887-901: `const offset = opts?.cursor?.startsWith("offset:") ? parseInt(opts.cursor.slice(7), 10) || 0 : 0; ... rows = await prisma.post.findMany({ where, include, orderBy, take: PAGE_SIZE + 1, skip: offset });` — `-5 || 0` is -5. collection/actions.ts:445 `const page = opts?.page ?? 0;` and :473-481 `skip: page * PAGE_SIZE`. Server actions are public POST endpoints, so the values are attacker-choosable; no legitimate client sends them, hence Low.
W1-239.fixDirection: `Math.max(0, ...)` at both sites (and clamp an upper bound, e.g. 10_000, while there).
W1-239.reproPlan: Local dev: invoke loadPosts({cursor:"offset:-1"}) from the console on any feed page; observe the digest error.
W1-239.gateOrTest: Unit-level test of the two clamps.

W1-240.title: Check-then-create toggles have the unique constraints but no P2002 handler; togglePhotoLove and markNotificationRead also throw raw on stale ids
W1-240.expected: Per the double-submit rule: the DB unique is the guard AND a P2002 handler turns the losing race into an idempotent success (the pattern reportUser at report-action.ts:185-193 and createCatchup already implement).
W1-240.actual: toggleLike, toggleBookmark, toggleCommentLike, votePoll, togglePhotoLove, toggleEntryLove all do findUnique-then-create with no try/catch: two rapid invocations both see "no existing", both create, the loser hits the @@unique (Like/Bookmark/CommentLike/PollVote/PhotoLove/CatchupEntryLove all carry one in schema.prisma) and the action THROWS — surfacing as a digest error/toast instead of a no-op. togglePhotoLove additionally never checks the photo exists, so an unknown photoId raises a P2003 FK error. markNotificationRead uses `update` with a compound where, so a stale/foreign notification id raises P2025.

Catchups' toggleEntryLove is wrapped by runAction (catchups/actions.ts:162-172) so it degrades to a friendly error, showing the intended pattern; the feed/collection files have no equivalent wrapper.
W1-240.fixDirection: Wrap each create in try/catch treating P2002 as success (liked: true); for deletes treat P2025 as success (liked: false); markNotificationRead → updateMany; togglePhotoLove → catch P2003 or precheck the photo. Alternatively give feed/collection actions a runAction-style wrapper like catchups has.

W1-240.gateOrTest: Unit/integration test double-invoking one toggle and asserting both resolve without throw.

W1-241.title: markFeedSeen accepts arbitrary future dates and its monotonic guard makes the mistake permanent
W1-241.expected: The "new since you were last here" marker only ever advances to a timestamp ≤ now (it is defined as the createdAt of a post that exists).
W1-241.actual: The action validates only that the string parses as a date: `const seenAt = new Date(newestCreatedAt); if (Number.isNaN(seenAt.getTime())) return;` then writes it through `updateMany({ where: { OR: [{ feedSeenAt: null }, { feedSeenAt: { lt: seenAt } }] }, data: { feedSeenAt: seenAt } })`. A call with "9999-01-01" (crafted, or a future client bug passing the wrong field) sets feedSeenAt to year 9999, and the deliberately monotonic WHERE then refuses every legitimate smaller value forever — the divider is permanently dead for that account with no self-serve fix.
W1-241.evidence: feed/actions.ts:1236-1246 quoted above; no upper bound anywhere. Only self-harm (the where pins the row to session.user.id), which caps severity, but the failure is irreversible without SQL.
W1-241.fixDirection: Clamp: `if (seenAt.getTime() > Date.now() + 60_000) seenAt = new Date()` (small skew allowance), or refuse future values.
W1-241.reproPlan: code-argument-only (the write is permanent per account; do not run against the shared DB).

W1-242.title: Fire-and-forget telemetry writes without after(): search logs and login attempts can be lost when the serverless instance freezes
W1-242.expected: Per the platform rule the codebase itself applies elsewhere (requestPasswordReset wraps its enqueue in after(), email-queue.ts:373 tries after() first): post-response work is scheduled with after()/waitUntil so it survives the response.
W1-242.actual: Both lookup routes fire `void logSearch({...})` and return the response immediately; recordLoginAttempt internally does `void prisma.loginAttempt.create(...).catch(...)` and authorize() returns (or throws CredentialsSignin) without awaiting it. On Vercel the instance can freeze after the response is sent, silently dropping the insert — undercounting exactly the zero-result searches and failed logins the analytics room was built to surface. Telemetry-only loss; nothing user-facing breaks.
W1-242.evidence: users/search/route.ts:72-78: `void logSearch({ scope: "people", query: q, userId: session.user.id, results: users.length }); return NextResponse.json(users);`. places/search/route.ts:127-134 same shape. login-attempt.ts:46-58: `void prisma.loginAttempt.create({...}).catch(...)` with the comment "Deliberately not awaited" — deliberate for latency, but after() gives the same latency without the loss. Contrast email-actions.ts:185 `after(async () => { ... enqueueMail ... })` — the codebase knows the pattern.
W1-242.fixDirection: Wrap the logSearch calls in after(() => logSearch(...)); in recordLoginAttempt, accept an optional scheduling: keep void-in-authorize (authorize runs outside a request scope where after() may not be available — verify) but at minimum move route-level calls to after().
W1-242.reproPlan: code-argument-only (loss is probabilistic on production infra; not reproducible deterministically in dev).
W1-242.gateOrTest: grep-based lint/check: no `void logSearch` outside after() — add to the check suite's static assertions (security-regressions.test.mjs style).

W1-243.title: Actions that shape input with .map/.trim before validating throw raw TypeErrors on crafted non-string/non-array payloads
W1-243.expected: A server action is a public POST endpoint; its very first move on caller data is a schema parse (the pattern joinCatchupByToken and every catchups action follow: typeof checks / zod before any property access).
W1-243.actual: updateContactMethods calls `input.phones.map((p) => p.trim())` and `input.links.map(...)` BEFORE contactMethodsSchema runs — a payload where phones is a string or links is null throws TypeError; updateUserPlaces/adminUpdatePlaces call `p.label.trim()` on unvalidated entries; updateProfileField calls `raw.trim()` on an unvalidated second argument; adminUpdatePerson calls `titleCase(edit.name)` / `edit.batchYear.trim()` on unvalidated fields. All throw before any write (no corruption), surfacing as generic digest errors rather than the friendly { error } contract every action otherwise keeps.
W1-243.evidence: profile-actions.ts:207-216: `const cleaned = { ... phones: input.phones.map((p) => p.trim()).filter(...), ... links: input.links.map((l) => ({ label: l.label.trim(), url: l.url.trim() }))... }; const parsed = contactMethodsSchema.safeParse(cleaned);` — the map precedes the parse. settings/actions.ts:150-153 `places.map((p) => ({ ... label: titleCase(p.label.trim()) ...`. profile-actions.ts:80 `const value = raw.trim();`. people/actions.ts:84 `const name = titleCase(edit.name);` and :93 `const yearRaw = edit.batchYear.trim();`. No throw reaches a write in any of them (verified by reading each function to its first await of prisma).
W1-243.fixDirection: Parse first: give each a zod schema over the RAW input (z.array(z.string()) etc.) and only then normalize; or wrap the shaping in try/catch returning { error: "Invalid request." }.
W1-243.reproPlan: Local dev: invoke updateContactMethods({ phones: "x", links: null, ... }) from the console; observe the digest error today.
W1-243.gateOrTest: Unit tests feeding wrong-typed payloads to each and asserting { error } instead of a throw.

W1-244.title: Cross-path validation caps disagree for the same columns: name 100 vs 80 vs 101, years capped at current-year vs 2100, phone min 4 vs none
W1-244.expected: One cap per column, whichever write path carries the value, so a value accepted by one surface is never refused (or silently out-of-range) on another.
W1-244.actual: (a) name: settings allows 100 (validators.ts:54), the profile letterhead allows 80 (profile-actions.ts:86 `if (value.length > 80)`), signup can store up to 101 (two 50-char halves + space, actions.ts:118) — an 85-char name saved in settings cannot be edited on the profile. (b) years: profileSchema caps yearJoined at the current year and batchYear at +7 (validators.ts:104-106), but updateProfileField accepts any year up to 2100 for the same columns (profile-actions.ts:28-29 `const YEAR_MAX = 2100` used in the default branch :130-133) — "Batch of 2100" is storable from the letterhead but would be refused by settings. (c) phones: profileSchema requires min(4) per entry (validators.ts:73) while contactMethodsSchema has no min (validators.ts:127), so "+" survives normalizePhone (normalize.ts:132-137 returns "+" for a bare plus) and stores as a one-character phone via the contact block.

W1-244.fixDirection: Extract shared per-column constants (NAME_MAX, YEAR_MIN/MAX, PHONE_MIN/MAX) into validators.ts and use them in profile-actions.ts and signup; make signup's joined-name length respect NAME_MAX; give contactMethodsSchema the same phone min(4).
W1-244.reproPlan: Local dev, own test account: save a 90-char name in settings, then try to edit it on the profile letterhead → refused.
W1-244.gateOrTest: A validation-consistency unit test asserting the letterhead caps equal the schema caps for the shared fields.

W1-245.title: "This week in Letters" rail module surfaces city-scoped letters to every member sitewide (content leak + guaranteed 404 on click-through)
W1-245.expected: A letter published with a city audience ("Bangalore only", set at the letters desk) is visible only to members with a matching UserPlace, everywhere it is surfaced — the letters index and the feed both enforce this via cityScopeWhere.
W1-245.actual: The feed rail's LettersModule picks the newest main-feed letter with NO viewer context and NO cityScope filter, so a city-scoped letter's title, excerpt, author and read time are shown to every member on /feed. An out-of-city member who clicks it hits the reading page's canViewCityScope check and gets notFound() — a teaser to a 404, for as long as that letter is the newest of the week.
W1-245.evidence: letters-module.tsx where clause is only: `where: { kind: "letter", isHidden: false, groupId: null, ...PUBLISHED_ONLY, createdAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now() - WEEK_MS) } }` — it selects `title, content, author` and renders `letterTitle(letter.title, letter.content)` plus `plainExcerpt(letter.content)`. Compare letters/page.tsx which adds `...(isAdmin ? {} : { AND: [cityScopeWhere(viewerCities)] })`. The reading page then blocks: `if (!(await canViewCityScope(letter.cityScope, session.user))) notFound();` (letters/[id]/page.tsx:106). FeedRail mounts `<LettersModule />` unconditionally for every viewer (feed-rail.tsx:35). W1-245.fixDirection: Pass the viewer (session) into LettersModule (or into FeedRail) and add the same audience filters the letters index uses: `...(isAdmin ? {} : { AND: [cityScopeWhere(viewerCities)] })` plus the targetBatches OR-fragment for symmetry with loadPosts. Since the rail is per-request server-rendered this is one extra Promise.all leg; alternatively query the newest 3 letters and pick the first the viewer may see.
W1-245.gateOrTest: New unit/integration test: a letter with cityScope='X' and a viewer without X — assert LettersModule renders null / a different letter. Also a Playwright check that the rail teaser never 404s on click for a non-admin member.
W1-245.reproPlan: Live proof (test accounts): member A (city Bangalore) publishes a letter scoped 'Bangalore only'; member B (no Bangalore UserPlace) loads /feed — the rail shows the letter; clicking it 404s.

W1-246.title: Every like/comment/reply notification links to /feed#<postId>, which never scrolls to the post and is structurally wrong for group posts and letters
W1-246.expected: Clicking "X liked your post" / "X commented on your post" lands the member on that content: a letter's thread at /letters/[id], a group post at its group feed, a feed post scrolled into view.
W1-246.actual: All four write sites hard-code `link: \`/feed#${postId}\`` regardless of the post's kind or groupId. (1) Group posts never appear in the main feed (loadPosts filters `groupId: null`), so the link lands on /feed with nothing to show. (2) A letter's comments are not rendered in the feed (the feed shows a compact letter card; the thread lives at /letters/[id]), so a comment notification on a letter cannot reach the comment. (3) Even for plain feed posts the fragment never works: PostFeed is a client component that fetches posts via the loadPosts server action after mount, so at the moment router.push(notif.link) commits, no element with id=postId exists and there is no hash-handling anywhere in the feed (grep for hash/scrollIntoView in post-feed.tsx returns nothing). The member always lands at the top of the feed. Bonus copy bug: `message: \`${session.user.name} liked your post\`` fires for letters too.
W1-246.evidence: feed/actions.ts toggleLike: `link: \`/feed#${postId}\`` with only `select: { authorId: true }` on the post (no kind/groupId read); createComment: `link: \`/feed#${parsed.data.postId}\``; reply notification: same; toggleCommentLike: `link: \`/feed#${comment.postId}\``. The anchor exists (`<article id={post.id}>` post-card.tsx:189) but only after client fetch. notification-bell.tsx:168 `router.push(notif.link)`.
W1-246.fixDirection: At each notification write, read kind and groupId alongside authorId, and build the link: letters -> `/letters/${postId}` (optionally `#comment-<id>`), group posts -> `/groups/${groupId}#${postId}`, feed posts -> `/feed#${postId}` plus a small client hash-handler in PostFeed that, after the first page loads, scrolls to location.hash if present (and ideally fetches the single post by id if it is not on page 1). Fix the copy to say "your letter" when kind=letter.
W1-246.gateOrTest: Unit test on the notification writers asserting link shape per kind/groupId; Playwright: like a group post as B, click A's notification, assert URL is the group page and the post is visible.
W1-246.reproPlan: Live: in a group, member B likes member A's group post; as A, click the bell notification — observe landing on /feed with no such post.

W1-247.title: Admin bell notifications still deep-link to the retired /admin?thread=<id>#messages, which nothing handles anymore
W1-247.expected: The admin clicks "X wrote: ..." / "X replied about ..." / "X reported a post ..." in the bell and lands in that conversation (the canonical route is now /admin/messages/[id]; the admin worklist and reports list both link there).
