W1-248.title: A letter draft's city audience is invisible and unchangeable at the desk: editPost drops cityScope, and the desk never hydrates it
W1-248.expected: The audience a writer picks at the letters desk is what the letter publishes with, and the desk always shows the draft's current audience.
W1-248.actual: Three interlocking gaps. (1) editPost's update writes only `{ content, title?, images? }` — cityScope is never read from the form, so choosing a city (or 'Everyone') while resuming a draft is silently ignored. (2) The edit page's select fetches `id, kind, status, authorId, title, content, images, isHidden` — not cityScope — and LetterDesk/CreatePostForm have no initialCityScope prop; `audienceCity` always initialises to null, so a draft saved as 'Bangalore only' renders with no audience chip, looking like 'Everyone'. (3) Even in one sitting: first "Save as draft" stores cityScope via createPost, then onDraftSaved does router.replace to the edit route, remounting the desk with audienceCity reset to null — the chip the writer just set disappears. Net effect: a member can publish a letter believing it goes to everyone when it is city-limited, or believe they limited it when their change was dropped.
W1-248.evidence: feed/actions.ts editPost: `await prisma.post.update({ where: { id: postId }, data: { content, ...(isLetter ? { title: title?.trim() || null } : {}), ...imagesUpdate } })` — no cityScope. create-post-form.tsx: `const [audienceCity, setAudienceCity] = useState<string | null>(null);` with no initial prop; handleSubmit only does `if (audienceCity) formData.set("cityScope", audienceCity)` which editPost ignores. letters/[id]/edit/page.tsx select list omits cityScope. publishDraft flips status only, preserving whatever cityScope sits on the row.
W1-248.fixDirection: Fetch cityScope on the edit page, add an initialCityScope prop threaded LetterDesk -> CreatePostForm to seed audienceCity, and make editPost accept a cityScope field for the author's own letter drafts, re-validated against the author's UserPlace list exactly as createPost does (including explicit clearing to null when 'Everyone' is chosen — note the current `if (audienceCity)` guard cannot express clearing; send the field unconditionally for drafts).
W1-248.gateOrTest: Unit test: save draft with cityScope, resume, change to Everyone, publish — assert row cityScope is null; and resume-render shows the stored city chip.
W1-248.reproPlan: Live (test account): at /letters/new pick a city, Save as draft, observe the chip vanish after the route replace; reload /letters/<id>/edit, pick 'Everyone', publish, then query/view as an out-of-city member — the letter is still city-limited.

W1-249.title: IST members see the wrong calendar date on letters: server-rendered dates use the UTC day
W1-249.expected: A letter published at 00:30 IST on 21 Aug reads "21 Aug" for its IST readership.

W1-249.evidence: utils.ts: `return new Date(date).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric" })` — no timeZone option. letters/page.tsx and letters/[id]/page.tsx are async server components (no "use client").

W1-249.reproPlan: code-argument-only (local dev machine is IST, so the bug only manifests on Vercel UTC; provable by running node with TZ=UTC).

W1-250.title: Clicking a notification whose row was pruned/retired throws un-caught P2025 and the click silently does nothing (no navigation)
W1-250.expected: Clicking any notification row always navigates to its link; a row deleted server-side is treated as already-read.
W1-250.actual: markNotificationRead uses `prisma.notification.update({ where: { id: notificationId, userId: session.user.id }, ... })` with no P2025 handling — update throws when no row matches. The bell's handler does `await markNotificationRead(notif.id)` BEFORE `router.push(notif.link)` with no try/catch, so the rejection aborts the handler: the member clicks and nothing happens. Rows under a displayed panel can vanish: (a) the 100-prune runs on every first-page bell open on ANY device, deleting rows beyond the 100th — a second device's panel scrolled past 100 now holds dead rows; (b) the nightly retention sweep deletes rows older than 365 days while a panel is open.
W1-250.evidence: notifications/actions.ts:77-84 has no try/catch and no updateMany; notification-bell.tsx:160-171: `if (!notif.read) { await markNotificationRead(notif.id); ... } if (notif.link) { router.push(notif.link); }`. Prune: `await prisma.notification.deleteMany({ where: { userId, createdAt: { lt: cutoff[0].createdAt } } })`. Retention: `prisma.notification.deleteMany({ where: { createdAt: { lt: cutoff(365) } } })`.
W1-250.fixDirection: Switch markNotificationRead to `updateMany({ where: { id, userId, read: false } })` (idempotent, never throws on missing rows), or wrap in try/catch; in the bell, navigate regardless of the mark call's outcome (fire the mark without blocking router.push).
W1-250.gateOrTest: Unit test: markNotificationRead on a nonexistent id resolves without throwing.
W1-250.reproPlan: Live: delete a notification row directly is a write — instead prove with two sessions: open bell and scroll past 100 rows on device A, open bell on device B (prune fires), click an old row on A; observe dead click in console.

W1-251.title: Bell unread badge is a page-load snapshot, desynced from the panel it opens; revalidatePath("/") purges nothing members are on
W1-251.expected: The badge count and the "Mark all read" affordance agree with the rows the panel actually shows.
W1-251.actual: initialUnreadCount is computed once (layout/feed page render) and only ever mutated locally. handleOpen re-fetches the first PAGE on every open but never reconciles the count, and getNotifications does not return one. Concrete desyncs a member will see: (1) notifications arriving after page load show as highlighted unread rows in the panel while the badge shows 0 and the "Mark all read" button is absent (`{unreadCount > 0 && (<button ...Mark all read)}`) — the only way to un-highlight them is clicking each one; (2) after reading on the phone, the desktop badge keeps its stale count indefinitely (no polling; and the actions' `revalidatePath("/")` targets only the route "/" — members live under /feed, /letters, etc., and a layout-wide purge would need revalidatePath("/", "layout")); (3) double-clicking one unread row decrements the badge twice (both click handlers read the pre-render `notif.read === false`). Also the decaying shake-on-rise animation is dead code in practice, since unreadCount can never rise client-side.
W1-251.evidence: bell: `const [unreadCount, setUnreadCount] = useState(initialUnreadCount);` — the only setters are the local decrements/zeroing; handleOpen sets notifications/nextCursor/hasMore/loaded only. notifications/actions.ts markNotificationRead/markAllNotificationsRead: `revalidatePath("/")`. Layout count: prisma.notification.count({ where: { userId, read: false } }) at layout render.
W1-251.fixDirection: Return the unread count from getNotifications (one extra count query, or derive from page-1 rows plus a count) and setUnreadCount on every open; make handleClickNotification idempotent per id; drop the ineffective revalidatePath("/") calls or change to ("/", "layout") if a server-driven refresh is actually wanted.
W1-251.gateOrTest: Component test: open panel with fresh unread rows and initialUnreadCount=0 — assert Mark-all-read renders and badge matches row state.
W1-251.reproPlan: Live: sign in on two browsers; generate a like for user A from user B; without navigating, open A's bell — rows highlight but badge stays 0 and no Mark-all-read button.

W1-252.title: createPost accepts 20,000-char plain posts but editPost caps posts at 5,000 — long posts become permanently uneditable
W1-252.expected: One cap per kind, enforced identically on create and edit (spec: 5,000 for posts, 20,000 for letters), with the composer surfacing the limit.
W1-252.actual: postSchema validates `content: z.string().min(1).max(20000)` for BOTH kinds, while editPost enforces `const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000`. The composer has no counter or client cap (only the soft letter nudge at 600 chars), so a member can write and publish a 6,000-20,000 char plain post — and then can never edit it: every edit attempt returns "Content must be between 1 and 5000 characters" even for a one-word typo fix, because editPost validates the full body.
W1-252.evidence: validators.ts:154: `content: z.string().min(1, "Post cannot be empty").max(20000),` with no kind-conditional refine. feed/actions.ts:396-399: `const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000; if (!content || content.length > cap) { return { error: ... } }`. create-post-form.tsx has no maxLength on the contentEditable and no counter (LETTER_NUDGE_LEN is a hint only).
W1-252.fixDirection: Add a superRefine to postSchema: content ≤ 5000 when kind !== 'letter' (createPost then matches editPost), and surface a counter in the composer past ~4500 chars for posts. Decide what to do for already-stored oversize posts (grandfather them in editPost by only enforcing the cap when length grew, or migrate).
W1-252.gateOrTest: Unit test: postSchema rejects kind='post' content of 5001 chars; editPost accepts an edit that does not grow an oversize legacy row.
W1-252.reproPlan: Live (test account): paste 6,000 chars into the composer, Post (succeeds), then Edit and change one character (fails with the 5000 error).

W1-253.title: Two tabs/devices editing the same letter draft silently clobber each other (autosave last-write-wins, no version check)
W1-253.expected: Concurrent editing of one draft either merges, blocks, or at least warns; a stale surface cannot silently destroy newer writing.
W1-253.actual: The desk autosaves the FULL body 2.5s after any keystroke via editPost, which does an unconditional `prisma.post.update` with no updatedAt/version precondition. A member with the draft open on laptop and phone who writes three paragraphs on the laptop, then later taps one character on the still-open phone tab, has the phone's stale full content overwrite everything — no warning, and the desk on both devices says "Saved".
W1-253.evidence: Autosave effect: `fd.set("content", content); ... const result = await editPost(postId, fd);` — whole-document write. editPost: `await prisma.post.update({ where: { id: postId }, data: { content, ... } })` — no `updatedAt` guard, no baseUpdatedAt token from the client.
W1-253.fixDirection: Send the draft's updatedAt (from page load / last successful save) with each editPost call and make the update conditional (`updateMany({ where: { id, authorId, updatedAt: base } })`); on 0 rows updated, surface "This letter changed somewhere else — reload before continuing" instead of overwriting.
W1-253.gateOrTest: Unit test on editPost with a stale base timestamp returning a conflict; manual two-tab check.
W1-253.reproPlan: Live (test account): open the same draft in two tabs, type in tab A (autosaves), type one char in tab B, reload — tab A's writing is gone.

W1-254.title: Letters desk autosave fails silently: errors leave "Saving..." stuck forever and the writer keeps writing into a draft that is no longer being saved
W1-254.expected: If autosave stops working (session expired, content over the 20,000 cap, network/DB error), the desk says so; the status line never lies.
W1-254.actual: The autosave callback does `onAutosaveState?.("saving"); ... const result = await editPost(postId, fd); if (!result.error) onAutosaveState?.("saved");` — on ANY error the state is left at "Saving..." permanently and nothing else happens: no toast, no retry, no distinction between transient and permanent failure. A letter that crosses 20,000 chars stops autosaving forever with no signal (editPost returns the cap error on every subsequent tick). If editPost THROWS (network drop), the rejection is unhandled inside setTimeout — same stuck state plus an unhandled rejection. Secondary defect: the in-flight guard `if (submitting || savingDraft) return;` reads STALE closure values — the effect's deps are `[content, title, images, postId]`, so a Publish click after the last keystroke does not refresh or cancel the pending timer, and the autosave editPost can run concurrently with publishDraft (benign today only because the payloads are identical).
W1-254.evidence: Effect at create-post-form.tsx:209-232; deps comment: `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n  }, [content, title, images, postId]);` — submitting/savingDraft excluded; no catch around `await editPost`; no error branch after `if (!result.error)`.
W1-254.fixDirection: Add an error path: set a third autosave state ("error", shown as 'Not saved — check your connection' with the last-saved time), wrap the await in try/catch, and clear the pending timer when submitting/savingDraft flips (add them to deps or clear the timer inside handleSubmit). Treat the over-cap error specially (surface the count).
W1-254.gateOrTest: Component test: editPost mock returning {error} — assert the desk leaves 'Saving...' and shows the failure state.
W1-254.reproPlan: Live: resume a draft, kill the network, type — 'Saving...' stays forever with no error.

W1-255.title: A fresh unsaved letter has zero navigation guard: back-swipe, the back link, or a closed tab discards the entire piece silently
W1-255.expected: A page whose whole purpose is long-form writing warns before discarding unsaved text (beforeunload + in-app navigation confirm), or autosaves from the first keystroke.
W1-255.actual: Autosave only runs `if (!postId)`-never for a FRESH letter (comment: "a fresh letter has no row to update until the first explicit Save as draft"), and there is no beforeunload handler anywhere in the repo (grep for beforeunload: zero hits). The desk's "All letters" back link is always active. A member 40 minutes into a letter who back-swipes on a phone, taps the back link, or lets the tab die loses everything with no prompt. The composer's outside-click guard only prevents pill-collapse, not navigation, and doesn't apply to the immersive desk at all.
W1-255.evidence: letter-desk.tsx renders a plain `<Link href="/letters">` above the sheet; create-post-form.tsx autosave effect begins `if (!postId) return;`; repo-wide grep `beforeunload|onbeforeunload` returns nothing.
W1-255.fixDirection: Register a beforeunload handler while `content.trim() && !postId && dirty` on the desk (and ideally while a resumed draft has unsaved changes), and intercept the back link with a confirm when dirty. Better still: create the draft row automatically on the first pause (first autosave tick creates via createPost saveAsDraft and adopts the id through the existing onDraftSaved path), which the plumbing already supports.
W1-255.gateOrTest: Playwright: type into /letters/new, trigger navigation, assert the confirm appears (or that a draft row exists).
W1-255.reproPlan: Live: type a paragraph at /letters/new, click 'All letters' — content is gone, no prompt, no draft row.

W1-256.title: /notice/[id] legacy resolver is non-idempotent: concurrent or retried opens mint duplicate "Notes from the admins" threads
W1-256.expected: Resolving an old admin_note notification into a thread happens exactly once per notification, however many times or how concurrently the page is opened.
W1-256.actual: The page does check-then-create-then-update during a GET render with no idempotency key: `if (notification.link?.startsWith("/messages/")) redirect(...)` else `openAdminNoticeThread(...)` then `notification.update({ link, read: true })`. Two concurrent first opens (two tabs, a double-tap, or a retried request) both pass the link check and both create a thread — the member's /messages list then shows the same moderation note twice, each a full 'notice' AdminThread with memberUnread=true. If the notification.update fails after the create, EVERY future open creates yet another thread. AdminThread has no unique key tying it to the source notification, so the database cannot stop this.
W1-256.evidence: notice/[id]/page.tsx:36-48 quoted above; openAdminNoticeThread is a bare `prisma.adminThread.create`. No transaction, no unique constraint on (memberId, kind, subject) or a sourceNotificationId.
W1-256.fixDirection: Make resolution idempotent: first `updateMany({ where: { id, link: null (or not-yet-/messages/) }, data: { link: RESOLVING } })`-style claim, or store the thread id on the notification inside one $transaction with the create; simplest: add a nullable unique `sourceNotificationId` column on AdminThread and upsert on it.
W1-256.gateOrTest: Unit test: call the resolution logic twice concurrently for one notification; assert one thread.
W1-256.reproPlan: code-argument-only (needs a legacy admin_note row with a /notice link; racing writes on prod data is not acceptable).

W1-257.title: Letters index silently truncates at 40 with no pagination — older letters vanish from the archive surface
W1-257.expected: The letters page is the archive of long-form pieces; every published letter stays reachable from it (paginated or 'load more').
W1-257.actual: `take: 40` with `orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }` and no cursor, no 'More letters' affordance, no count — the 41st-newest letter simply stops existing on /letters. At 2,000 members this is months away, and unlike the feed there is no infinite scroll fallback on this page (old letters remain findable only via feed scroll or search). The drafts strip has the same shape (take: 20) — a 21st draft is invisible but still occupies a row.
W1-257.evidence: letters/page.tsx: `orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }, take: 40,` then `letters.map((l) => (...))` with nothing rendered after the list. Drafts: `take: 20`.
W1-257.fixDirection: Add keyset pagination (same (createdAt,id) pattern as loadPosts) with a 'More letters' button or infinite scroll; at minimum a link to the feed pre-filtered to kind=letter. For drafts, 20 is fine but consider a count so 'you have 23 drafts' is at least visible.
W1-257.gateOrTest: Seed 41 letters in a test DB; assert the 41st is reachable from /letters.
W1-257.reproPlan: code-argument-only (production has fewer than 40 letters today; the truncation is arithmetic).

W1-258.title: The 100-notification prune deletes UNREAD rows, including moderation/admin notices the member never saw
W1-258.expected: Per the brief's explicit question: whether the prune can destroy unread signal. High-importance rows (admin_note, admin_message, report_update) should outlive a flood of likes, or unread rows should be exempt.
W1-258.actual: The prune keys purely on recency: `deleteMany({ where: { userId, createdAt: { lt: cutoff[0].createdAt } } })` with the cutoff at the 100th-newest row regardless of read state or type. A member whose letter draws 100+ like/comment notifications before they next open the bell loses every older UNREAD row — including an admin_note attached to a removed post. The signal partially survives elsewhere (the AdminThread still sits in /messages with memberUnread=true), but the notification channel for it is silently destroyed, and the unread count self-corrects only on the next layout render. Off-by-one and tie-handling are clean (skip KEEP-1/take 1; `lt` keeps ties), and the prune correctly skips cursored pages.
W1-258.evidence: actions.ts:44-57 quoted; no `read` or `type` condition in either the cutoff query or the deleteMany.
W1-258.fixDirection: Either exempt unread rows (`read: true` in the deleteMany where, accepting slower shrink for hoarders), or exempt the admin/moderation types, or both: delete read rows past 100 plus unread rows past a larger ceiling (e.g. 500).
W1-258.gateOrTest: Unit test: 150 rows, rows 120-150 unread admin_note — open bell, assert admin_note rows survive.

W1-259.title: Thread pages load every message with no take: an unbounded query on both the member and admin conversation views
W1-259.expected: Bounded reads on every list (2,000-user headroom rule): a conversation view pages or windows its messages.
W1-259.actual: Both thread pages fetch `messages: { orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" }, select: {...} }` with no take. The per-member throttle is 40 messages/hour ACROSS all threads (isMessageRateLimited counts by authorId), so one long-running conversation can legally accumulate thousands of rows over months; each open then serializes the entire history (bodies up to 4,000 chars each) into one RSC payload. Retention deletes messages older than 730 days, which caps growth eventually but leaves plenty of room for a multi-MB page. The admin list page correctly loads headers+last message only, so this is the one unbounded read in the messages feature.
W1-259.evidence: messages/[id]/page.tsx:40-52 — no take on the messages include; admin-threads-server.ts:35-41 shows the rate limit is per-author, not per-thread; retention.ts adminMessages: 730 days.
W1-259.fixDirection: Add `take: -200` (last 200) with an 'earlier messages' loader, or plain take with keyset paging — the Conversation component already receives a flat array so windowing is contained.
W1-259.gateOrTest: Seed a 1,000-message thread in a test DB; assert page payload stays bounded.

W1-260.title: Letter view telemetry (recordView) fires before the visibility checks and is un-awaited on serverless
W1-260.expected: A 'view' is recorded only for letters the viewer is actually allowed to read, and the write reliably lands.
W1-260.actual: `void recordView(session.user.id, "letter", letter.id);` runs after only the kind/isHidden check but BEFORE the draft-author, group-membership and city-scope gates — a non-author probing a draft id, or a non-member hitting a group letter, is counted as a reader of content they were refused (the analytics this exists for, 'read click-through rates', over-count). Separately, the promise is fired-and-forgotten without after(): it usually completes because the render continues through further awaits, but on the fast path (all checks cached/fast) the lambda can freeze before the upsert commits, dropping views. Prisma upsert's find-then-create race under two concurrent first views throws P2002, which the internal catch swallows in production — acceptable, but development-only logging means a production failure mode is invisible.
W1-260.evidence: letters/[id]/page.tsx: recordView at :85, `if (isDraft && !isAuthor) notFound();` at :93, group check at :96-102, city check at :106. content-view.ts catch: `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") console.error(...)`.
W1-260.fixDirection: Move the recordView call below all three visibility gates, and wrap it in `after(() => recordView(...))` so it survives the response without delaying it.
W1-260.gateOrTest: Unit test: recordView not invoked when the page 404s for a non-author draft.

W1-261.title: letterTitle and the letters-index excerpt leave a stray "!" for letters opening with image markdown — the exact bug already fixed in plainExcerpt
W1-261.expected: All three teaser/title derivations strip image markdown identically (plainExcerpt's comment records the '!banyan' bug and fixes it by stripping `![alt](url)` BEFORE the link rule).

W1-261.reproPlan: Live (test account): publish an untitled letter starting with `![banyan](x)` and view /letters.

W1-262.title: Transient Resend failures permanently fail queued mail: all 4 attempts burn back-to-back in one drain pass with no backoff and no transient/permanent error distinction
W1-262.expected: MAX_ATTEMPTS exists so 'a permanently bad address (someone typed gmial) must not be retried forever' (comment at email-queue.ts:103-105). A transient provider error (Resend 429 rate limit, 5xx, network blip) should be retried later, spread over time, and must never terminally fail a queued password reset.
W1-262.actual: A row whose send fails transiently is requeued with status 'queued' and its original createdAt, so the very next iteration of the SAME drain pass re-selects it (it is still the oldest eligible row under orderBy [priority asc, createdAt asc]). Four failures in four consecutive iterations, seconds apart, hit MAX_ATTEMPTS and the row is terminally 'failed'. One BATCH=8 pass during an outage terminally kills 2 rows; every authenticated page view spawns another pass (layout after()), so a ~5-minute Resend outage or 429 storm at launch traffic converts the entire backlog, resets included, to permanent 'failed'. Nothing retries after the outage ends ('failed' is terminal); recovery is the admin clicking retryMail one row at a time. A reset requester was already told { ok: true } ('check your inbox') and sees nothing, ever.
W1-262.evidence: The loop re-picks the same row: `const next = await prisma.outboundEmail.findFirst({ where: { status: "queued", kind: { in: eligibleKinds }, attempts: { lt: MAX_ATTEMPTS } }, orderBy: [{ priority: "asc" }, { createdAt: "asc" }], ... })` (461-475) — a requeued row keeps createdAt so it stays at the head. claimAndSend increments attempts on every claim (`attempts: { increment: 1 }`, 162) and computes `const afterFailure = spent >= MAX_ATTEMPTS ? "failed" : "queued"` (174); every failure path writes `status: afterFailure` (224, 231) with no delay, no nextAttemptAt, and no inspection of the error class — sendMail collapses a Resend 429, a 5xx and a genuinely invalid address into the same `{ ok: false, error }` (email.ts:188-199). There is no code path that returns a 'failed' row to 'queued' when the day or the provider recovers.
W1-262.fixDirection: Two changes. (1) Add a nextAttemptAt (or reuse claimedAt semantics) set with exponential backoff on failure, and add `nextAttemptAt: { lte: now }` to the drain's findFirst, so retries spread across passes instead of burning in one. (2) Classify errors in sendMail (Resend returns error names/status: rate_limit_exceeded, daily_quota_exceeded, validation errors): provider-level/transient errors must not increment toward terminal failure (or must use a much higher ceiling), while validation/'invalid to address' errors may fail fast. At minimum, a failure whose error indicates rate/quota should leave the row queued without burning an attempt.
W1-262.gateOrTest: New unit test beside the 14 in npm run check: stub sendMail to fail twice then succeed, run drainMailQueue once, assert the row ends 'sent' (or at least not 'failed') and that attempts were not all consumed within a single pass.
W1-262.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would require making real Resend calls fail, which risks real sends from the shared DB).

W1-263.title: deletion-scheduled emails can never be sent: the drain's eligibleKinds list omits the kind, so every account-deletion confirmation sits queued forever
W1-263.expected: requestAccountDeletion enqueues kind 'deletion-scheduled' at priority 20 as 'the only warning a person gets that their account is going away' and the takeover alarm for the 60-day grace window. The drain should send it just behind resets, as PRIORITY, ENQUEUE_LIMIT and render() all provide for.
W1-263.actual: The drain can never select the row. `eligibleKinds` is `["verify", "reset", "password-changed"]` or `["reset", "password-changed"]` — 'deletion-scheduled' appears in neither branch, and findFirst filters `kind: { in: eligibleKinds }`. The only other caller of claimAndSend is verificationMailState, which reads `kind: "verify"` rows only. So every deletion-scheduled row sits status 'queued' forever: the member who requested deletion never gets the written confirmation, a victim of an account takeover never gets the alarm during the 60-day undo window, the admin panel's 'Waiting to go' count is permanently inflated, admin retryMail cannot help (requeued rows are still ineligible) and dismissMail refuses non-'failed' rows. After 180 days the retention sweep silently deletes the never-sent row (deleteMany on createdAt with no status filter).
W1-263.evidence: email-queue.ts:468-469: `const eligibleKinds = live.verifyRemaining > 0 ? ["verify", "reset", "password-changed"] : ["reset", "password-changed"];` and 472: `where: { status: "queued", kind: { in: eligibleKinds }, ... }`. Yet the kind is fully wired everywhere else: type MailKind includes it (53), `"deletion-scheduled": 20` in PRIORITY (68), an ENQUEUE_LIMIT entry (281), a render branch (394), and settings/actions.ts:338-341 enqueues it: `await enqueueMail({ kind: "deletion-scheduled", to: me.email, userId, ... })`. verificationMailState's findFirst is `where: { userId, kind: "verify" }` (565-566), so it can never send it either.
W1-263.fixDirection: Add "deletion-scheduled" to both branches of eligibleKinds (it is a priority-20 security notice exactly like password-changed, so it belongs wherever password-changed is). Better: derive the always-eligible list from PRIORITY's keys minus 'verify' so a future fifth kind cannot repeat this bug. Then sweep the database for stranded queued deletion-scheduled rows and re-send or hand-notify.
W1-263.gateOrTest: Unit test: for every key of PRIORITY, enqueue a row and assert one drainMailQueue pass (with sendMail stubbed ok) marks it 'sent'. This pins the invariant that no MailKind is ever un-drainable.
W1-263.reproPlan: Read-only live proof: query OutboundEmail for kind='deletion-scheduled' rows with status='queued' and old createdAt (any that exist prove it in production data). Do not exercise the deletion flow on a real account.

W1-264.title: Email case never normalized at signup/login but lowercased in the reset flow: a mixed-case account silently never receives password-reset mail, and one mailbox can register twice
W1-264.expected: One address is one account regardless of casing, and a password-reset request for any casing of a registered address reaches that account (6e: email case normalization consistent between signup, login and reset).
W1-264.actual: Signup stores the email exactly as typed: the Zod schema is `email: z.email("Please enter a valid email")` with no transform, and the create writes `email: parsed.data.email`. Login's authorize also looks up as-typed (`where: { email }`, auth.ts:103; only the rate-limit key is lowercased at line 62). But requestPasswordReset lowercases before lookup: `const raw = ((formData.get("email") as string) ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();` then `findUnique({ where: { email: raw } })`. Any member whose stored address contains an uppercase letter (pasted 'Ravi.Kumar@gmail.com', a corporate autofill) gets `{ ok: true }` — 'check your inbox' — and no email is ever enqueued; the anti-oracle design means no error surfaces anywhere. They are permanently locked out of password recovery. Separately, 'foo@x.com' and 'Foo@x.com' both pass the exact-match duplicate check and the case-sensitive Postgres unique, so one mailbox can hold two accounts.
W1-264.evidence: validators.ts:18 has no `.toLowerCase()`; auth/actions.ts:103-104 `const existing = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email: parsed.data.email } })` and 149 `email: parsed.data.email`; email-actions.ts:160-165 lowercases then `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email: raw } })`; the signup form input (signup-form.tsx:573-580) applies no client-side lowering either. schema.prisma User.email is a plain `String @unique` (case-sensitive).
W1-264.fixDirection: Normalize once, at the boundary: add .trim().toLowerCase() (on the local-part-preserving-display variant if the owner cares, but store the canonical lowercase in User.email) in the signup schema, in authorize(), and keep the reset flow as is. Then run a one-off data check for existing mixed-case rows and for case-duplicate pairs before enforcing (a manual SQL SELECT lower(email), count(*) GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*)>1).
W1-264.gateOrTest: Unit test: register 'Foo@X.com' (mocked), assert requestPasswordReset('foo@x.com') enqueues a reset row; second registration with different casing is refused.
W1-264.reproPlan: Read-only live proof: SELECT count(*) FROM "User" WHERE email <> lower(email) — any nonzero count is a member already exposed.

W1-265.title: Bounce/complaint webhook flips a sent row's status to 'failed', which resurrects daily-budget slots and lets the app send past Resend's real 100/day cap
W1-265.expected: dailyBudget's 'used' should count every message Resend accepted today (that is what spends the provider's quota), so the app's DAILY_CAP=95 stays under Resend's 100 with the deliberate 5-message margin.
W1-265.actual: dailyBudget counts `{ status: "sent", sentAt: { gte: startOfUtcDay() } }`. The webhook's bounce patch sets `status: "failed"` (and complaint likewise) while leaving sentAt in place — so every same-day bounce or complaint removes a message from 'used' that Resend already counted against the real quota. Each bounce resurrects one phantom budget slot. The webhook file's own motivation is launch mail 'bouncing off stale addresses' in the hundreds; a dozen same-day bounces already exceeds the entire 5-message headroom, after which the drain keeps sending while Resend hard-rejects — and each rejection burns attempts toward terminal 'failed' (see the Critical retry finding), failing exactly the messages the reserve exists to protect. mailHealth.sentToday undercounts the same way, so the admin panel under-reports the day.
W1-265.evidence: route.ts:117-118: bounce patch includes `status: "failed"` (and 128 for complaints), with no compensating field; email-queue.ts:258-260: `const used = await prisma.outboundEmail.count({ where: { status: "sent", sentAt: { gte: startOfUtcDay() } } });`. The margin's whole justification (comment 74-79) is absorbing miscounts of ~a retry or two, not a launch-day bounce rate.
W1-265.fixDirection: Count acceptance, not current status: change dailyBudget (and mailHealth.sentToday) to `where: { sentAt: { gte: startOfUtcDay() } }` with no status filter (sentAt is only ever written on a real provider accept, and the webhook never clears it), or keep bounce state in bouncedAt/bounceKind without overwriting status. If status:'failed' stays (the admin worklist depends on it), the budget query must switch to sentAt-only. Also confirm with Resend docs/support whether the 100/day refusal is hard-fail (the code currently assumes it).
W1-265.gateOrTest: Unit test: create a row with status 'failed', sentAt = today, bouncedAt set; assert dailyBudget().used counts it.
W1-265.reproPlan: code-argument-only (proving it live needs a real bounce against the production sending domain, which damages reputation).

W1-266.title: Drain concurrency is unbounded: every authenticated page view and every enqueue schedules a full drain pass, so launch traffic fans out well past Resend's ~2 req/s and past the budget cap via uncounted in-flight sends
W1-266.expected: The claim (one row, one sender) is safe, but the SYSTEM should also bound how many drain passes send concurrently, because Resend rate-limits to roughly 2 requests/second (the code's own comment at email-queue.ts:93-95) and the budget check must not be overshootable by more than the 5-message margin.
W1-266.actual: There is no global coordination at all. Every authenticated page view runs `after(drainMailQueue)` (layout.tsx:63-69) and every enqueueMail calls scheduleDrain (350). K overlapping passes do not collapse: when two race for the head row, the loser gets 'lost-claim' and simply moves to the NEXT row (comment at 481-482), so K concurrent passes send K different rows in parallel. At launch (steady page views over a 100+ row backlog) that is a self-inflicted 429 storm against a 2 rps provider limit — and every 429 burns an attempt toward terminal failure (Critical finding above). Independently, the budget check is per-pass check-then-send: rows in status 'sending' are not counted by dailyBudget (it counts 'sent' only), so with K passes in flight the cap can be exceeded by up to K messages, past the 5-message headroom, producing hard provider rejections.
W1-266.evidence: layout.tsx:63-65: `after(async () => { try { await drainMailQueue(); } ...` on every render of the authenticated layout; email-queue.ts:452/462: `const budget = await dailyBudget(); ... const live = await dailyBudget(); if (live.remaining === 0) break;` — both reads count `status: "sent"` rows only (258-260), never in-flight 'sending' rows; 481-482: `// lost-claim: another process took the row ... the loop just looks for the next one.` — the mechanism by which concurrent passes parallelize instead of deduplicating.
W1-266.fixDirection: Serialize or throttle drains with a lease row (NOT a pg advisory lock — session-level locks do not survive the pgbouncer transaction pooler): e.g. a single QueueLock row claimed with a conditional updateMany + stale takeover exactly like claimedAt, so at most one (or N) pass sends at a time; other passes return immediately. Alternatively count 'sending' rows into 'used' when computing remaining, which bounds overshoot even with concurrency. Add a small inter-send sleep or honor Resend's rate-limit headers inside the pass.
W1-266.gateOrTest: Unit test with sendMail stubbed slow: fire drainMailQueue twice concurrently over a 10-row queue with remaining=1 budget and assert total sent <= budget + lease bound (today it sends 2).
W1-266.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof means real bulk sends).

W1-267.title: sendMail reports ok:true without an API key in development when EMAIL_DEV_SEND=1, so a dev drain marks real members' queued mail 'sent' off a console print (shared production DB)
W1-267.expected: The 2026-08-12 incident rule, stated twice in comments: 'Nothing may record a send on the strength of a console.log' (email.ts:155-159), and queueIsSendable's all-or-nothing contract — a process that cannot genuinely send must not touch queued rows (email-queue.ts:113-124).

The suppression branch in sendMail is bypassed (EMAIL_DEV_SEND===1), then the no-key branch in non-production prints the message and returns `{ ok: true }`. claimAndSend records `status: "sent", sentAt: now, providerId: null` on a real member's row. 'sent' is terminal: the member's verification or reset is never retried and never arrives, and verificationMailState tells them to go look in their inbox.

W1-267.fixDirection: Make the no-key dev branch return `{ ok: false, error: "RESEND_API_KEY is not set" }` (keep the console print as the dev convenience), and/or make queueIsSendable's dev arm require the key too: `EMAIL_DEV_SEND === "1" && !!process.env.RESEND_API_KEY`. Either alone closes it; both honor the all-or-nothing contract.
W1-267.gateOrTest: Add to src/lib/security-regressions.test.mjs (which already pins deleted endpoints): with NODE_ENV=test, EMAIL_DEV_SEND=1 and no RESEND_API_KEY, sendMail must not resolve ok:true.
W1-267.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live repro would, by definition, corrupt a real member's queue row in the shared DB).

W1-268.title: claimAndSend's outcome writes are not scoped to its claim, so a send slower than the 2-minute stale window causes duplicate emails and can flip an already-'sent' row back to 'queued' for a third send
W1-268.expected: After the stale-claim reclaim hands a row to a second sender, the first (slow, still-running) sender's eventual outcome must not overwrite the second's bookkeeping: writes should be conditional on still owning the claim.
W1-268.actual: The Resend call has no timeout (api.emails.send with no AbortSignal, email.ts:181-187), so a hung connection can easily outlive STALE_CLAIM_MS=2min. Sequence: drain A claims (attempts→1), its send hangs; after 2 min the reclaim (`where: { status: "sending", claimedAt: { lt: ... } }` → status 'queued') releases the row; drain B claims (attempts→2), sends successfully, writes status 'sent' + its providerId. Drain A's call finally errors; A's failure path runs `prisma.outboundEmail.update({ where: { id: row.id }, data: { status: afterFailure /* "queued" — A read attempts=1 */, ... } })` — unconditional on id — flipping the SENT row back to 'queued'. A later pass sends it a third time. The member gets 2-3 copies; for verify/reset each re-send's mint burns the prior token so earlier copies carry dead links (confusing 'already used' screens); budget is spent multiply; and B's providerId is overwritten on the failure path (lastError clobber) or, in the A-succeeds-too variant, A's success write replaces B's providerId so B's bounce webhook finds no row.
W1-268.evidence: Success write 192-204 and failure writes 222-225 / 228-235 all use `where: { id: row.id }` with no `status: "sending"` or claimedAt guard, while the claim itself (160-163) IS guarded (`where: { id: row.id, status: "queued" }`) — the pattern was applied to acquisition but not release. Reclaim at 447-450 has no way to tell a dead process from a slow one because nothing identifies the claimant.
W1-268.fixDirection: Stamp the claim with a unique value (the claimedAt Date already read into a local, or a random claim token column) and make every outcome write conditional: `updateMany({ where: { id, status: "sending", claimedAt: myClaim }, ... })`; treat count 0 as 'lost the row, do nothing'. Additionally set a timeout/AbortSignal (e.g. 30s) on the Resend call so a hang cannot outlive the stale window, and pass Resend's Idempotency-Key header (row.id + attempt) so an at-least-once retry cannot double-deliver.
W1-268.gateOrTest: Unit test: claim a row, manually reclaim + re-claim it (simulating drain B), then run the first claimant's failure path and assert the row still reads 'sent'.
W1-268.reproPlan: code-argument-only (needs an induced multi-minute provider hang).

W1-269.title: Stale-claim reclaim can return a row to 'queued' with attempts already at MAX_ATTEMPTS, where the drain's filter ignores it forever: a wedged row that is neither sent, failed, nor dismissible
W1-269.expected: Every queued row is eventually either sent or terminally 'failed' (visible in the admin 'Gave up' list); nothing can be permanently stuck in 'queued'.
W1-269.actual: The claim increments attempts BEFORE the send (162). If a process claims a row for its final attempt (attempts 3→4) and dies mid-send, the reclaim sweep writes it back to `status: "queued"` with attempts=4 and no attempts guard. The drain's findFirst requires `attempts: { lt: MAX_ATTEMPTS }`, so the row is invisible to every future pass, yet it is not 'failed': mailHealth counts it in 'waiting' forever, the admin 'Waiting to go' section shows it indefinitely, and dismissMail refuses it ('Only a message that gave up can be cleared', actions.ts:61-63). For kind 'verify' there is an accidental escape hatch — verificationMailState claims queued rows with no attempts filter (597-599), so the member's own page view un-wedges it — but a reset, password-changed or deletion-scheduled row has no such path: the member's reset silently never arrives and never surfaces as failed. The 180-day retention sweep then deletes the undelivered row silently (retention.ts:103-106 filters on createdAt only).
W1-269.evidence: Reclaim 447-450: `updateMany({ where: { status: "sending", claimedAt: { lt: new Date(Date.now() - STALE_CLAIM_MS) } }, data: { status: "queued", claimedAt: null } })` — attempts untouched; drain filter 472: `attempts: { lt: MAX_ATTEMPTS }`; claim-then-increment 160-163 means a claim always spends an attempt even when no send was ever transmitted.
W1-269.fixDirection: In the reclaim sweep, split by attempts: rows with attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS go to `status: "failed", lastError: "process died mid-send on final attempt"` (making them visible and dismissible), the rest to 'queued'. Alternatively increment attempts on outcome rather than on claim, so a died-mid-send claim does not consume the final attempt.
W1-269.gateOrTest: Unit test: row with status 'sending', attempts=4, stale claimedAt; run drainMailQueue; assert the row ends 'failed' (today it ends 'queued' and is never selected).
W1-269.reproPlan: Read-only live proof: SELECT * FROM "OutboundEmail" WHERE status='queued' AND attempts >= 4 — any hit is a wedged row.

W1-270.title: resendVerification maps verificationMailState 'failed' to 'imminent', so after a terminal send failure the banner tells the member 'A link has been sent to your email'
W1-270.expected: The state contract is explicit (email-actions.ts:47-50 and the whole 'the app must not lie about where a message is' design): 'sent' only when the provider accepted, 'queued' only when budget is spent, 'imminent' only when in flight or seconds from retry. A terminal failure must not be reported as mail on its way.
W1-270.actual: verificationMailState can return `{ state: "failed" }` immediately after the button-triggered send attempt (skip path 181-187 marks the row failed on token rate limit; 607 returns 'failed' after a failed inline claimAndSend, e.g. an address whose earlier mail hard-bounced, undeliverable-TLD refusal, or the last attempt burning out). resendVerification's mapping has no 'failed' arm: `state: state.state === "sent" ? "sent" : state.state === "queued" ? "queued" : "imminent"` — failed (and none) collapse to 'imminent'. The banner's imminent copy asserts 'A link has been sent to your email. Tap on it to verify your account.' with the resend button removed (banner 207-209: no button while imminent). The member with a broken address is told to check an inbox nothing was sent to, with the retry control hidden — the exact 2026-08-13 class of lie this subsystem was rebuilt to prevent.

W1-270.fixDirection: Add a 'failed' arm to the action's return type and mapping, and give the banner a failed presentation ('That address would not accept mail. Check it and try again') with the send button visible — the VerificationMailState type already models it; only the action and banner drop it.
W1-270.gateOrTest: Unit test on the mapping: given verificationMailState returning failed, resendVerification must not answer 'imminent'/'sent'.
W1-270.reproPlan: code-argument-only (forcing a real failed send would spend real budget).

W1-271.title: Failed sends consume the token-mint rate limit (a mint per attempt), so after one dead row the member's next genuine reset request is terminally skipped as 'token rate limit' without a single send
W1-271.expected: The token rate limit (reset: 4 per 30 min) exists to cap how many LIVE links reach an inbox. Send attempts that never left the building should not spend it, and the skip path's own justification ('one of them is almost certainly still live in their inbox', email-queue.ts:405-408) assumes mints correlate with delivered mail.
W1-271.actual: render() mints a fresh token on every claim attempt, including all retries of a failing row. A reset row that burns its 4 attempts during a transient provider failure (seconds, per the Critical finding) also creates 4 AuthToken rows in the 30-minute window — none of which produced an email. When the member then submits forgot-password again, the new row's first drain hits mintToken's `recent >= limit.max` (4 >= 4), render returns `{ skip: "token rate limit" }`, and claimAndSend marks the NEW row terminally 'failed' with that lastError — no retry when the window reopens, no signal to the member (requestPasswordReset already answered ok). Net: one transient provider blip locks that member out of password recovery for up to 30 minutes, with both rows dead and only the admin panel knowing.
W1-271.evidence: email-queue.ts:403: `const minted = await mintToken(row.userId, kind, row.to);` runs inside claimAndSend's per-attempt render; auth-tokens.ts:81-84: `const recent = await prisma.authToken.count({ where: { userId, kind, createdAt: { gte: since } } }); if (recent >= limit.max) return { ok: false, reason: "rate-limited" };` — counts every mint ever created in the window, sent or not; email-queue.ts:182-186 turns the skip into `status: "failed"` (terminal) rather than deferring.
W1-271.fixDirection: Two options, either sufficient: (a) treat the token-rate-limit skip as a deferral, not a failure — leave the row queued (without incrementing toward MAX_ATTEMPTS) with a nextAttemptAt past the window; (b) only count tokens that correspond to sent mail (e.g. mint after a successful provider accept is wrong for link-liveness, so instead pass a 'burnOnly' reuse: reuse the still-unused latest token when re-attempting the same queue row rather than minting anew per attempt).
W1-271.gateOrTest: Unit test: fail sendMail 4 times for one reset row, enqueue a second reset, drain, and assert the second row is not status 'failed' with lastError 'token rate limit'.

W1-272.title: verificationMailState performs a synchronous, timeout-less Resend send inside the authenticated layout's render for unconfirmed members, and repeats it on every page view while the send keeps failing
W1-272.expected: The design accepts 'one Resend call inside one page load, once' (email-queue.ts:561-562). Page render must never be hostage to a third-party API's worst-case latency, and the 'once' must hold.
W1-272.actual: The layout awaits verificationMailState inside the render Promise.all (layout.tsx:44-46), and with a queued row plus available budget that path runs mintToken + a live Resend HTTP call (claimAndSend at email-queue.ts:598) before the page can stream. The Resend call has no timeout or AbortSignal (email.ts:181-187), so during a provider brown-out every page view by an unconfirmed member blocks for the full hang, up to the Vercel function ceiling — a blank page instead of a feed, on every route, for exactly the newest members. And 'once' is untrue under failure: a transient failure requeues the row (status back to 'queued', attempts+1), so the NEXT page view repeats the synchronous send, four page views burn the row to terminal 'failed' (see Critical finding). The comment's cost model only covers the success path.

Promise.resolve(null) : verificationMailState(session.user.id)` inside the awaited Promise.all that gates render; email-queue.ts:597-599: `if (row.status === "queued") { const outcome = await claimAndSend(row); ... }` — the synchronous send; contrast with the drain, which the same layout deliberately pushes into after() at 63-69 'because this one makes network calls to Resend ... or every page in the app would wait on somebody else's welcome email' — the identical network call is awaited pre-response three lines up when it is the member's own mail.
W1-272.fixDirection: Give the state function a fast path for render: return 'imminent' immediately and hand the actual send to after() (the claim mechanism already makes that safe), or keep the inline send but wrap it in a short timeout (2-3s AbortSignal) falling back to 'imminent'. Fixing the retry/backoff finding also caps the repeat-on-every-view behavior.
W1-272.gateOrTest: After the fix, an integration test with sendMail stubbed to hang: layout render (or verificationMailState) must resolve under the timeout budget.
W1-272.reproPlan: code-argument-only (live proof requires degrading the real provider).

W1-273.title: Double-submit of forgot-password creates two reset rows: the dedupe fold is a check-then-insert TOCTOU with no unique constraint behind it
W1-273.expected: The fold rule ('a verify or reset for somebody who already has one WAITING is folded into the existing row', email-queue.ts:290-293) should hold under concurrency; per taxonomy 6c the DB unique constraint is the only real guard, and there is none.

ON "OutboundEmail"("userId", kind) WHERE status IN ('queued','sending')` (Prisma schema can't express partial uniques; document it beside the model), and catch P2002 in enqueueMail returning the fold result. W1-273.gateOrTest: Unit test: two concurrent enqueueMail calls for the same user/kind resolve to one queued row.
W1-273.reproPlan: Live proof possible read-safely against a test account: double-fire the forgot-password action for a dev test address and count rows — but it writes rows to the shared DB, so prefer code-argument-only.

W1-274.title: A very fast bounce webhook can outrun the providerId write and is silently dropped, leaving the row 'sent' forever
W1-274.expected: Every authentic delivery event should eventually land on its row; the webhook's whole purpose is that a bounced launch invitation does not look identical to a delivered one.
W1-274.actual: providerId is written only by claimAndSend's success update, which runs AFTER `sendMail` returns (email-queue.ts:189-204). A bounce for an instantly-rejecting address can be dispatched by Resend in the window between its API accepting the message and our row update committing. The webhook's `updateMany({ where: { providerId } })` matches 0 rows, logs a warning, and returns 200 — which tells Svix the event is handled, so it is never retried. The row keeps status 'sent' with no bouncedAt forever; at launch this is precisely the 'sent vs delivered' blindness the webhook was built to remove, restored for the fastest-failing (deadest) addresses.
W1-274.evidence: route.ts:140-146: `const { count } = await prisma.outboundEmail.updateMany({ where: { providerId }, data: patch }); if (count === 0) { console.warn(...); }` then unconditional `return NextResponse.json({ ok: true })` at 154 — a 2xx for an event that updated nothing; the comment at 137-139 justifies tolerating missing rows for cross-environment mail but that reasoning also swallows this same-environment race.
W1-274.fixDirection: When count === 0 for a bounce/complaint event, return a 5xx (or 404) so Svix retries — its backoff (seconds to minutes) comfortably clears the write race; keep 200 for delivered/delayed events where the loss is tolerable, or bound retries by checking event age before refusing.
W1-274.gateOrTest: Unit test on the handler: bounce event whose providerId matches no row must return non-2xx (so the provider retries), delivered event may return 200.

W1-275.title: Account-deletion email prints the purge date in server UTC: requests made 00:00-05:30 IST name a date one day earlier than the member's local purge day

For any request made between 00:00 and 05:30 IST (18:30-24:00 UTC), the purge instant falls on the NEXT IST calendar day, so the email understates the deadline by one day (e.g. says '19 October 2026' when the member's clock reads 20 October at the purge moment). Understating is the safe direction for the cancel-by-signing-in flow, but the letter that confirms an irreversible action names a wrong date. W1-275.evidence: settings/actions.ts:344-348: `purgeDate: purgeAt.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })` — no `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"`, unlike admin/mail/page.tsx:94-100 which correctly passes `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` for the budget refill line.
W1-275.fixDirection: Add `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` to this toLocaleDateString (the audience is IST; the admin mail page already sets the precedent), or format at read-time in the recipient's terms. Fix together with the eligibleKinds repair since the same template is in play.

W1-276.title: Removing a contact row saves the pre-removal list: commitContacts reads a stale contactRows closure, so the removed phone/link/email silently survives in the DB
W1-276.expected: Clicking the X on a contact row removes that phone number / link / social from the member's stored contact methods.
W1-276.actual: The UI removes the row, but the server write persists the OLD list including the removed row. On the next page load the 'removed' phone number is back on the member's public Get in touch sheet.
W1-276.evidence: contacts-editor.tsx remove button (lines 226-229): `onClick={() => { onChange(rows.filter((r) => r.id !== row.id)); onCommit(); }}`. `onChange` is `setContactRows` and `onCommit` is `commitContacts` from letterhead-profile.tsx:423-429: `function commitContacts() { void run(async () => { const result = await updateContactMethods(rowsToPayload(contactRows)); ... }) }`. `commitContacts` closes over the `contactRows` state variable of the render in which the click happened — `setContactRows(next)` has not re-rendered yet when `onCommit()` executes in the same event handler, so `rowsToPayload(contactRows)` serialises the PRE-removal array and `updateContactMethods` writes it. The success then calls `router.refresh()`, but the client `contactRows` state (initialised once in `useState(() => draft ? buildRows(draft.contacts) : [])`, letterhead-profile.tsx:332-334) is preserved across refresh, so the UI keeps showing the row as gone while the DB still has it. The blur-commit path (PenValue onCommit) is safe because keystroke onChange events re-render before blur; only the same-tick onChange+onCommit of the remove button hits the stale closure. Removing a phone number is a privacy gesture: the member believes it is off their profile while every verified viewer still gets it in Get in touch and in the vCard.
W1-276.fixDirection: Make removal commit the list it just computed: either change ContactsEditor's remove handler to call a new `onRemove(next: ContactRow[])` prop that both sets state and saves `rowsToPayload(next)` directly, or change `commitContacts` to accept an explicit rows argument (`commitContacts(next)`) and have the remove button pass the filtered array. Same pattern commitPlaces/commitHouses already use (they pass `next` into the action).
W1-276.gateOrTest: New unit/component test: render ContactsEditor with two phone rows, click remove on one, assert updateContactMethods was called with a payload of ONE phone. Also a Playwright spec: remove a phone in edit mode, reload the profile, assert the number is absent from Get in touch.
W1-276.reproPlan: Live proof on a test account via chrome-devtools: sign in, open own profile, Edit, add two phone numbers, blur to save, click X on one, reload the page — the removed number reappears.

W1-277.title: A member cannot remove their email from the profile: deleting the email row saves displayEmail=null, and the page then falls back to exposing the sign-in email (and buildRows re-seeds the row on reload)

On next edit, buildRows (contacts-editor.tsx:126-127: `if (source.displayEmail || source.email) rows.push({ ... value: source.displayEmail || source.email })`) re-seeds the row from the account email, so the 'removed' row reappears. The X on the email row is a no-op that looks like a privacy control.

The profile page and vCard then use the fallback `user.displayEmail?.trim() || user.email` (page.tsx:177, 274), so the sign-in address ships to all verified members. W1-278.title: Account purge misses AdminMessage.imageUrl screenshots (and Group.coverImage): member deletion cascades the rows away and permanently orphans their R2 bytes at public URLs
W1-278.expected: purgeUserAccount's own contract (header comment: 'The one place that knows how to erase a member COMPLETELY... bytes in R2 that no cascade can reach... That is what made GDPR Art. 17 unachievable for images') collects EVERY stored-image URL the member's rows point at before the cascade destroys them.
W1-278.actual: collectImageUrls (account-purge.ts:37-68) reads only User.photoUrl, Post.images, Photo.{thumbUrl,url,originalUrl}, and CatchupEntry.images. It never reads AdminMessage.imageUrl ('one optional screenshot (WebP via /api/upload)', schema.prisma:587). AdminThread.member is `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:568) and AdminMessage.thread is `onDelete: Cascade` (line 590), so a deleted member's admin-thread messages — and with them the only rows pointing at their uploaded screenshots — are destroyed in the same transaction, leaving the WebP bytes publicly fetchable at their pub-*.r2.dev URLs forever with nothing able to enumerate them. (The `authorId SetNull` comment on AdminMessage only saves messages sitting in OTHER people's threads.) Same class: Group.coverImage (schema.prisma:195) with `creator ... onDelete: Cascade` (line 201) — legacy Group rows created by the member cascade away with an uncollected cover URL.
W1-278.evidence: account-purge.ts:38-46: `const [user, posts, photos, entries] = await Promise.all([ prisma.user.findUnique(...photoUrl...), prisma.post.findMany(...images...), prisma.photo.findMany(...), prisma.catchupEntry.findMany(...images...) ]);` — no adminMessage or group query. schema.prisma:590 `thread AdminThread @relation(... onDelete: Cascade)` + :568 `member User @relation("AdminThreadMember", ... onDelete: Cascade)` proves the member's threads and messages die with the user row.
W1-278.fixDirection: In collectImageUrls, add `prisma.adminMessage.findMany({ where: { thread: { memberId: userId } }, select: { imageUrl: true } })` (all messages in the member's threads, since the whole thread cascades) and, if legacy Group rows can exist, `prisma.group.findMany({ where: { creatorId: userId }, select: { coverImage: true } })`; push non-null URLs into the list. delImage already ignores URLs that are not ours, so collecting generously stays safe.
W1-278.gateOrTest: Extend the purge unit test (or add one): seed a user with an admin-thread message carrying imageUrl, run purgeUserAccount, assert delImage was called with that URL. A schema-audit check could also assert every String column whose comment mentions an upload URL appears in collectImageUrls.
W1-278.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would require deleting an account against the shared production database).

W1-279.title: Retention purge runs unbounded sequential R2 deletes AFTER the row cascade, inside a route with no maxDuration: a timeout mid-loop permanently orphans the remaining un-enumerable objects
W1-279.expected: The nightly sweep purges due accounts within the serverless duration budget, and a partial failure leaves a durable record of which R2 objects still need deleting.
W1-279.actual: purgeUserAccount deletes the rows first (correctly argued in its comment), then `for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; }` — one awaited DeleteObject round-trip per URL, sequential. retention.ts:115-136 loops over ALL due users (`findMany` with no take) and purges each in turn; the sweep route exports no `maxDuration` (grep across src/app finds none) so it runs at the platform default. A member with a large Collection contribution history (each Photo contributes 2-3 URLs) can push one purge into hundreds of sequential HTTP deletes; when the function times out after the row transaction has committed, the un-deleted URLs are orphaned with no row left pointing at them and no retry possible — exactly the un-enumerable-bytes failure the file's own header says it exists to prevent. The per-user audit entry and the sweep's closing 'retention.sweep' audit are also lost on timeout, so the failure is invisible in /admin/audit.
W1-279.evidence: account-purge.ts:108-113: `let deleted = 0; for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; } return { ok: true, imagesDeleted: deleted };` after the `prisma.$transaction([...user.delete...])` at :99-102. retention.ts:116-118: `const rows = await prisma.user.findMany({ where: { deletionRequestedAt: { lt: cutoff(DELETION_GRACE_DAYS) } }, select: {...} });` — unbounded, then sequential `await purgeUserAccount(row.id)` per row.
W1-279.fixDirection: Two independent hardenings: (1) make the object deletions durable-or-batched — write the collected URL list into the audit detail (or a small PurgeQueue table) BEFORE the row transaction, so a timeout leaves a retryable record; and/or delete in parallel batches (Promise.allSettled over chunks of ~25, or S3 DeleteObjects batching) to cut wall time an order of magnitude. (2) export `maxDuration` on the sweep route sized to the worst case, and cap users-per-sweep (take: N) so one heavy account cannot starve the rest — the sweep is already idempotent so the remainder purges tomorrow. Note the same slow-sequential-delete shape also applies to adminDeleteUser, which shares purgeUserAccount inside a user-facing server action.
W1-279.gateOrTest: Unit test purgeUserAccount with a mocked delImage asserting batched/parallel deletion; a test on runRetentionSweep asserting a `take` bound; verify the sweep route exports maxDuration.
W1-279.reproPlan: code-argument-only (cannot exercise deletion against the shared production database); timing can be argued from delImage being one awaited S3 round-trip per URL.

W1-280.title: updateUserPlaces takes its input entirely on trust: no Zod, no length caps on label/city, unvalidated lat/lng/placeId — the one profile writer without the M18-standard gate
W1-280.expected: Every server action validates everything, including types and lengths — the standard the codebase itself set when audit M18 added contactMethodsSchema because updateContactMethods 'used to write with NO validation at all'.
W1-280.actual: `export async function updateUserPlaces(places: {...}[])` is a public POST whose TypeScript parameter types are erased at runtime. The body does `places.map((p) => ({ placeId: p.placeId, label: titleCase(p.label.trim()), city: titleCase(p.city.trim()), lat: p.lat, lng: p.lng }))` with only `.filter((p) => p.label.length > 0).slice(0, 30)`. Consequences: (a) a non-array or a row with non-string label throws (`p.label.trim` is not a function) — an unhandled server-action exception instead of an error result; (b) label/city have NO length cap, so a crafted call stores 30 rows x arbitrary-length strings (megabytes) which then render on the profile facts row, the directory, and the vCard for every viewer, and mirror into User.currentCity; (c) lat/lng accept any number (NaN/Infinity/out-of-range floats) flowing into map surfaces; (d) a float placeId throws a Prisma Int validation error. Storage bloat/DoS is squarely the stability class this audit owns (the 2026-08-20 security pass covered authz/injection, not resource exhaustion).
W1-280.evidence: settings/actions.ts:144-159 (quoted above) — contrast with updateContactMethods in profile-actions.ts:217 (`contactMethodsSchema.safeParse`) and saveOnboardingHouses in onboarding/actions.ts:140 (`housesPayloadSchema.safeParse`), the two sibling list-writers that both parse first. File is uncommitted WIP; this is its current state.
W1-280.fixDirection: Add a `placesSchema = z.array(z.object({ placeId: z.number().int().nullable(), label: z.string().trim().min(1).max(120), city: z.string().trim().max(100), lat: z.number().min(-90).max(90).nullable(), lng: z.number().min(-180).max(180).nullable() })).max(30)` and safeParse before the transaction, returning { error } on failure — same shape as contactMethodsSchema per M18.
W1-280.gateOrTest: Unit test posting an over-long label and a non-numeric lat to updateUserPlaces expecting { error }, not a throw; the existing security-regressions test file is the natural home.
W1-280.reproPlan: Live on a test account: call the action from the console with a 100k-char label; confirm today it stores and renders. (Write is to the tester's own row and reversible.)

W1-281.title: Whole-list autosaves race: cities and houses commit the full list on every interaction with no ordering guard, so out-of-order completion silently persists an older list
W1-281.expected: Rapid consecutive edits (the house chain editor deliberately 'hands the panel straight to the next year' encouraging quick successive picks; the cities picker commits on every add/remove) end with the DB holding the final list.
W1-281.actual: Each interaction fires an independent full-list write: commitPlaces → updateUserPlaces (deleteMany + recreate, settings/actions.ts:162-181) and commitHouses → saveOnboardingHouses (one JSON overwrite, onboarding/actions.ts:150-153). Two in-flight writes A (older list) and B (newer) can complete B-then-A — server actions are independent POSTs with no sequencing — leaving the DB with the OLDER list while the client state shows the newer one. router.refresh() re-renders the server tree but the client `houses`/`places` useState persists, so the member sees all their picks; the loss surfaces only on the next full reload (house picks vanished). Most plausible on slow mobile networks, which is the member base (India, phones). The same shape applies to two tabs editing simultaneously (delete+recreate last-writer-wins wholesale).
W1-281.evidence: letterhead-profile.tsx:414-421: `function commitHouses(next) { setHouses(next); void run(async () => { const result = await saveOnboardingHouses(next); ... }) }` — invoked per pick from HouseChainEditor's toggle; nothing cancels or serialises the previous in-flight save. useAutoSave's `run` (pen.tsx:348) counts overlapping calls for the spinner but does not order them.
W1-281.fixDirection: Serialise per-list writes client-side: keep a per-key promise chain (start the next save only after the previous settles) or a monotonically increasing sequence stamp the client checks before treating a completion as current; alternatively debounce commitHouses/commitPlaces (~600ms trailing) so rapid picks coalesce into one write. Server-side, a `updatedAt`-style optimistic check would also close the two-tab case.
W1-281.gateOrTest: Component test with mocked actions resolving out of order: fire two commitHouses calls, resolve the second first, assert the FINAL persisted payload equals the last-issued list.
W1-281.reproPlan: Live with chrome-devtools network throttling (Slow 3G) on a test account: click through 4-5 house picks quickly, hard-reload, compare the chain against what was picked.

W1-282.title: Auto-save failure semantics: commitField marks the value saved BEFORE the write, so a failed save can never be retried by re-blurring, and useAutoSave silently swallows an error that finishes while another save is in flight
W1-282.expected: A field whose save failed (network blip, transient 500) is retried the next time the member commits it; an error is always surfaced.
W1-282.actual: commitField (letterhead-profile.tsx:392-401): `const value = form[key]; if (saved.current[key] === value) return; saved.current[key] = value;` — the value is recorded as saved before the request runs. If updateProfileField fails, saved.current still holds the value, so blurring the same field again (the natural retry gesture) returns early and never retries; the edit is lost unless the member changes the text. Compounding it, useAutoSave (pen.tsx:360-368): `inFlight.current -= 1; if (inFlight.current > 0) return; if (failed) { setState("error"); ... }` — when save A fails while save B is still in flight, A's completion returns early (counter > 0) and B's later success paints 'Saved', so the member is shown success while field A's edit was dropped, with no error ever displayed and no retry possible.
W1-282.evidence: Quoted lines above; the SaveMark comment itself says 'An error stays put... because the value on screen is not the value on file' — but the mechanism only holds for the last-finishing save, and the retry path is dead either way.
W1-282.fixDirection: In commitField, set saved.current[key] only after a successful result (or clear it in the failure branch). In useAutoSave, track failures across the in-flight window (e.g. accumulate `failed` in a ref and report it when the counter reaches zero) so one failure among overlapping saves still shows the error state.
W1-282.gateOrTest: Unit test on a commitField-like harness: mock action fails once then succeeds; blur twice with the same value; assert two calls were made and the second persisted. Second test: two overlapping runs, first rejects, second resolves — assert final state is 'error'.
W1-282.reproPlan: Live with chrome-devtools: set network offline, edit About, blur (error mark appears), go back online, blur the same field again — no request fires; press Done and reload: the edit is gone.

W1-283.title: Profile Photos grid links to /feed#<postId>, but the feed only renders the newest 20 posts — every older photo click dead-ends at the top of the feed

W1-283.actual: page.tsx:293: `href={`/feed#${ph.postId}`}`. The anchor target is `<article id={post.id}>` (post-card.tsx:189), which only exists if the post is in the feed's FIRST page — `const PAGE_SIZE = 20` (feed/actions.ts:762) with cursor-based load-more. W1-284.title: Profile client fetch/submit paths have no rejection handling: a transient failure leaves permanent skeletons, a stuck 'Loading...' button, a stuck photoBusy flag, or a silent no-op
W1-284.expected: When the DB or network hiccups mid-request the member sees something actionable (an error state, a retry), and busy flags reset.

W1-284.fixDirection: Wrap each in try/catch/finally: finally resets the busy flag; catch sets an inline error state with a retry affordance (feeds) or a toast ('That did not load/save. W1-284.reproPlan: Live with chrome-devtools: block the server-action request (network conditions offline) while opening a profile's Posts tab — skeleton persists indefinitely with a console unhandled-rejection.

W1-285.title: Undecodable-photo fallback ships the ORIGINAL file (allowed up to 15MB) through a server action capped at ~4.5MB: a large HEIC dies at the platform with no message instead of the friendly 'export as JPG' answer
W1-285.expected: The crop dialog exists precisely because 'a 6MB phone photo could die on Vercel's ~4.5MB serverless body cap' (letterhead-profile.tsx:363-365). Every upload path should stay under the cap or use presign.

When the browser cannot decode the file (HEIC on Chrome/Android — common for iPhone-exported photos), AvatarCropDialog's onDecodeError hands the ORIGINAL File back: letterhead-profile.tsx:1269-1275 `onDecodeError={(f) => { ...; void uploadAvatarBlob(f); }}` — 'Send the original to the server, whose sharp pipeline either handles it or answers with the friendly "export as JPG" message'. But updateAvatar is a plain server action (FormData through the function body), so a HEIC over ~4.5MB is rejected by Vercel with a 413 before the action runs; the friendly message never sends, the action call rejects, and (per the finding above) photoBusy sticks with no toast. MAX_AVATAR_INPUT = 15MB (settings/actions.ts:20) documents an input size the transport can no longer carry.

W1-285.fixDirection: Cap the fallback: in handlePhotoPick or onDecodeError, if the undecodable file exceeds ~4MB, show the 'export as JPG or PNG' guidance client-side instead of attempting the upload (the server's message for HEIC is already known text); or route the fallback through the existing presigned direct-upload path and process server-side from R2. Also align MAX_AVATAR_INPUT with what the transport actually permits for the direct-action path.
W1-285.gateOrTest: Component test: onDecodeError with a 6MB fake file asserts no server call and a visible message. Manual E2E once: upload a >4.5MB HEIC from Chrome.
W1-285.reproPlan: Live on a test account: craft a 6MB file with a .heic type (or a real iPhone HEIC), pick it as profile photo in Chrome — observe the silent failure and stuck busy state.
