W1-287.title: /api/account/export streams the member's entire history unbounded in one JSON response — a prolific member's export can exceed Vercel's ~4.5MB response cap and fail outright
W1-287.expected: The GDPR export succeeds for every member regardless of volume.
W1-287.actual: Every query is unbounded: `prisma.post.findMany({ where: { authorId: userId }, ... select: { content: true, images: true, ... } })`, likewise comments, likes, photos, catchupEntries, adminMessages (route.ts:87-135) — no take anywhere — then `JSON.stringify(body, null, 2)` (pretty-printed, roughly +30% bytes) into a single NextResponse. Post.content is capped at 20,000 chars (postSchema), comments at 1,000; a member with a few hundred long posts/letters plus comments crosses 4.5MB, at which point the serverless response is rejected by the platform and the member gets a generic failure — and has burned one of their 3/day export tokens (rateLimit is consumed at route.ts:35 before the work).
W1-287.evidence: Quoted query shapes; response built at route.ts:164-170 as one `new NextResponse(JSON.stringify(body, null, 2))`. The rate limit consumption ordering is at :35-41.
W1-287.fixDirection: Bound the memory and body: drop the pretty-print (stringify without indentation), and either stream the JSON, paginate the heavy sections into the same file via chunked reads, or generate the export to R2 (a private object with a short-lived signed URL) and respond with the link — which also removes the response-size ceiling entirely. Consider refunding the rate-limit token on failure.
W1-287.gateOrTest: Load-shaped test: seed a test user with ~300 max-length posts locally and assert the export route still answers; or a unit assertion that the serialized body stays under a stated budget per N rows.
W1-287.reproPlan: Code-argument plus arithmetic (225 x 20KB posts ≈ 4.5MB before indentation); a live proof would need seeding large volumes and is not worth the shared-DB risk.

W1-288.title: parseJsonArray(user.phones) has no element-type guard: one non-string element in the phones column crashes the entire profile page server-side for every viewer
W1-288.expected: Every JSON-in-string reader tolerates an old/manual row (the houses reader parseHouseYearEntries and links reader parseUserLinks both validate element shape and type).
W1-288.actual: parseJsonArray (utils.ts:28-36) returns `Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : []` — valid JSON arrays pass through with NO element validation, typed as string[]. page.tsx:182 `const parsedPhones = parseJsonArray(user.phones)` then :219 `value: formatPhoneDisplay(p)` where formatPhoneDisplay does `raw.trim()` (utils.ts:127) — a phones column of e.g. `[9876543210]` (numbers, from a manual fix-up or a future writer regression) throws TypeError during server render, 500ing the profile for everyone who views it, including its owner. Malformed JSON is safe everywhere (try/catch → []); the gap is exclusively element type. No current writer can produce non-strings (both writers JSON.stringify normalized string arrays), so the trigger is a legacy/manual row — but the blast radius when it happens is a whole-page crash.
W1-288.evidence: Quoted lines; contrast parseUserLinks (social.ts:66-76) which filters on `typeof e.label === "string" && typeof e.url === "string"`.
W1-288.fixDirection: Either make parseJsonArray filter to strings (`parsed.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === "string")` — check its other call sites, they all treat the result as string[]), or add a dedicated parsePhones that mirrors parseUserLinks' shape-checking.
W1-288.gateOrTest: Unit test: parseJsonArray('[123, {"a":1}, "+91"]') must yield only strings; a render test of the profile page with a hostile phones row.
W1-288.reproPlan: code-argument-only (would require writing a malformed row to the shared database).

W1-289.title: generateMetadata omits the deletionRequestedAt gate the page body enforces: the tab title can carry the name of an account the page pretends does not exist
W1-289.expected: The page's own rule: 'notFound() (not a 403) so the page never even hints the account exists' (comment at page.tsx:108-111) — applied consistently to the metadata.
W1-289.actual: generateMetadata (page.tsx:34-39) checks `if (!user || user.isBlocked) return { title: "Profile" }` but not `deletionRequestedAt`, while the page body 404s on all three (line 112). If Next.js applies the resolved metadata around the not-found boundary, a viewer hitting a grace-window member's URL gets a 404 body with the member's name in the tab title — a hint the page body was explicitly built not to give. Needs one live check of what title the 404 renders with.
W1-289.evidence: The two conditions quoted; the asymmetry is provable from the file alone.
W1-289.fixDirection: Add `|| user.deletionRequestedAt` to the generateMetadata guard so both paths return the neutral 'Profile' title.
W1-289.gateOrTest: Unit-level: a test asserting generateMetadata returns 'Profile' for a row with deletionRequestedAt set.
W1-289.reproPlan: Live read-only IF a deletion-requested account exists (unlikely on prod): open its /profile/<id> and read document.title on the 404. Otherwise code-argument.

W1-290.title: Deletion-scheduled email renders the purge date in server UTC: members acting between 00:00 and 05:30 IST are told a purge date one calendar day earlier than their own
W1-290.expected: The purge date in the confirmation email matches the member's calendar (members are IST, UTC+5:30).
W1-290.actual: settings/actions.ts:315 `const purgeAt = new Date(Date.now() + DELETION_GRACE_DAYS * 86_400_000);` then :344-349 `purgeDate: purgeAt.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })` — no timeZone option, so on Vercel (UTC) it formats the UTC date. A member confirming at 01:00 IST on 1 Sep produces purgeAt = 30 Oct 19:30 UTC; the email says '30 October' while in the member's timezone the moment is 31 October 01:00 — and the nightly sweep will actually purge at its first run after that instant, in IST terms on the 31st. The audit-log detail at :333 (`purgeAt.toISOString().slice(0, 10)`) has the same UTC framing (acceptable for an admin log, wrong for the member-facing mail).
W1-290.evidence: Quoted lines; DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 60 (account-purge.ts:26); sweep cutoff `deletionRequestedAt < now - 60d` (retention.ts:117).
W1-290.fixDirection: Format the member-facing date with `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` in the toLocaleDateString options (the audience is IST by product definition), or phrase the mail as '60 days from now (on or shortly after <date>)' to absorb both the timezone and the sweep-schedule slack.
W1-290.gateOrTest: Unit test on the purgeDate formatting with a fixed Date in the 18:30-24:00 UTC band asserting the IST calendar date.

W1-291.title: Dark-mode tile keys on the DB while the /dark-mode route keys on the device cookie: on a new device a dark-mode member is told 'Turning it off is one press' and then handed the full entry gauntlet
W1-291.expected: The theme controls describe the state of THIS device consistently (and per theme.ts:42's comment, 'a forgotten device should eventually drift back to the DB truth on next sign-in').
W1-291.actual: The profile edit tile reads the DB row: letterhead-profile.tsx:1194 `{draft?.theme === "dark" ? "Dark mode is on" : "Dark mode"}` and :1198 'You made it through the questions. Turning it off is one press.' The route it links to gates on the COOKIE: dark-mode/page.tsx:25 `if ((await getThemeCookie()) === "dark") return <LightsOn />;` else the DarkGauntlet. W1-291.reproPlan: Live on a test account: complete the gauntlet (sets DB+cookie), then clear only the rv-theme cookie in devtools and reload the profile edit view.

W1-292.title: No cross-field sanity on the year set: yearLeft < yearJoined, batchYear < yearLeft and similar combinations save silently, printing 'In the valley 2020–2010' and deriving a nonsense batchType
W1-292.expected: A typo'd pair (left before joined; batch year before leaving year) is caught at save, or at least never rendered as a backwards range or a wrong credential.
W1-292.actual: updateProfileField's year branch (profile-actions.ts:126-134) validates each year only in isolation (1926..2100), and profileSchema (validators.ts:104-106) likewise has no refine across yearJoined/yearLeft/batchYear. Consequences: rvYearsLabel (page.tsx:50) prints `${yearJoined}–${yearLeft}` = '2020–2010'; batchTypeFromLeaving (utils.ts:250-258) computes `12 - (batchYear - yearLeft)` — batchYear 2015 with yearLeft 2023 yields grade 20 → 'ISC' silently stored; the houses editor collapses to its fallback sentence because `yearLeft - 1 >= yearJoined` fails (house-chain-editor.tsx:121-124), so the member also loses the chain with no hint the years are the reason. Also note the inline editor allows years to 2100 while the (currently caller-less) profileSchema caps at currentYear+1 — a divergence to collapse when touching this.
W1-292.evidence: Quoted lines; no refine/cross-check exists in either writer.
W1-292.fixDirection: In updateProfileField's year branch, after computing the new value, read the counterpart(s) (it already fetches batchYear/yearLeft for the batchType derivation) and reject pairs where yearLeft < yearJoined or batchYear < yearLeft with a plain sentence ('The year you left can't be before the year you joined.'). Keep the check symmetrical so fixing either field clears it.
W1-292.gateOrTest: Unit tests on updateProfileField for the two inverted pairs expecting { error }; a render test that rvYearsLabel never receives an inverted pair.
W1-292.reproPlan: Live on a test account: set yearJoined 2020 then yearLeft 2010 in the inline editor; observe '2020–2010' on the sheet and the houses section replaced by the fill-in prompt.

W1-293.title: The generated vCard is spec-non-compliant: LF line endings instead of CRLF and unescaped commas/semicolons in FN/ADR/NOTE (gazetteer city labels contain commas), so strict contact apps may import it mangled
W1-293.expected: 'Save contact' produces a .vcf that iOS/Android contact apps import with fields intact.
W1-293.actual: page.tsx:270-284 builds the card with `.join("\n")` — RFC 2426/6350 require CRLF line delimiters — and interpolates raw values: `ADR:;;${c};;;;` where c is a UserPlace label like 'London, England, United Kingdom' (commas are multi-value separators inside a vCard component and must be backslash-escaped), and `NOTE:${batchLine(user)}, Rishi Valley community${houseNote}` with unescaped commas/semicolons. Lenient parsers cope; stricter ones split the city into multiple values or mis-parse the note. A member's name containing a comma (rare) would likewise corrupt FN.
W1-293.evidence: Quoted construction; cityLabels come from `user.places.map((p) => p.label)` (page.tsx:168-170), and UserPlace labels are stored as the disambiguated picker strings (normalize.ts shortPlaceLabel's comment: 'The gazetteer stores labels such as "London, England, United Kingdom"').
W1-293.fixDirection: Escape per vCard 3.0 (backslash-escape , ; \ and newline in text values), join with \r\n, and consider using the short city (`p.city`) in ADR instead of the long label.
W1-293.gateOrTest: Unit test on the vcard string: assert CRLF delimiters and escaped commas for a fixture user with a multi-part city label.
W1-293.reproPlan: Live read-only: download a Save-contact card for a member with a comma-bearing city and import into macOS Contacts / an Android device; inspect the address field.

W1-294.title: Admins get notFound() for blocked members' profiles too, so the profile's own block control is one-way: block someone from their sheet and the page (with the unblock toggle and admin note) becomes unreachable
W1-294.expected: An admin can still open a blocked member's profile (where AdminProfileTools renders the unblock control and the admin note).
W1-294.actual: page.tsx:112 `if (!user || user.isBlocked || user.deletionRequestedAt) notFound();` applies to every viewer including admins (isAdmin is computed at line 120, after the gate). adminBlockUser even does `revalidatePath(`/profile/${userId}`)` (admin-actions.ts:40) — the page the admin is standing on 404s on its next render. Unblocking requires knowing to go to /admin/people; the isBlocked/adminNote props passed to AdminProfileTools from this page are dead-true-branches. Not member-facing, but a real workflow dead-end for the one admin (the owner).
W1-294.evidence: Quoted gate ordering; AdminProfileTools receives isBlocked (page.tsx:344-350) yet can only ever render with isBlocked=false here.
W1-294.fixDirection: Let admins through: `if (!user || ((user.isBlocked || user.deletionRequestedAt) && session.user.role !== "admin")) notFound();`, ideally with a visible banner ('This account is blocked / scheduled for deletion') so the admin knows what they are looking at.
W1-294.gateOrTest: E2E as admin: block a seeded member, revisit their profile, assert the sheet renders with the unblock control instead of 404.
W1-294.reproPlan: code-argument-only against production; provable live on the demo/seed environment by blocking a seeded member.

W1-295.title: parseHouseSpans merges same-house entries across an unrecorded gap year, so the profile asserts a span covering a year the member never answered and the editor's grey pill lands out of chronological order
W1-295.expected: A member with Aravali recorded for 2014 and 2016 but nothing for 2015 shows two one-year Aravali pills with the unanswered year between them; a span label only covers years actually recorded.
W1-295.actual: parseHouseSpans (house-spans.ts:152-163): after sorting, `if (last && last.house.toLowerCase() === entry.house.toLowerCase() && entry.year >= last.toYear) { last.toYear = entry.year; }` — the condition is always true for any later same-house entry (entries are sorted ascending), so 2014-Aravali and 2016-Aravali collapse into ONE span rendered 'Aravali 2014-17', claiming the unanswered 2015-16 academic year. In the editor this compounds: firstGap finds 2015, but `indexOfYear(spans, 2015)` ('before the first span that starts later', house-chain-editor.tsx:354-357) finds no span starting after 2015 and places the grey 2015-16 pill AFTER the merged span — contradicting the code's own promise that 'clearing a year in the middle of a finished chain has to put the grey pill back where that year belongs'. Reachable in two clicks: chain Aravali/Ganga/Aravali across 2014-16, tap the Ganga pill, toggle Ganga off — the two Aravali pills instantly fuse into a three-year span with the grey pill dangling at the end.
W1-295.evidence: Quoted collapse condition (`entry.year >= last.toYear` cannot be false post-sort, so only the house-name check gates merging — gap size is never consulted); indexOfYear quoted.
W1-295.fixDirection: Make the merge require adjacency-or-repeat: `entry.year <= last.toYear + 1` (a repeated year still merges, a gap opens a new span). indexOfYear then places the mid-chain grey pill correctly with no further change.
W1-295.gateOrTest: Unit tests on parseHouseSpans: [{2014,A},{2016,A}] → two spans; [{2014,A},{2015,A}] → one span 2014-16 label; [{2014,A},{2014,A}] → one.
W1-295.reproPlan: Live on a test account: build the 3-year chain, remove the middle house, screenshot the fused pill and trailing grey pill.

W1-296.title: Deleting or editing a post never updates the on-screen list: the deleted card stays, the edited card shows the old text, on every surface that renders PostCard
W1-296.expected: After 'Delete this post? This cannot be undone.' is confirmed and the server succeeds, the card disappears. After 'Save' in the edit dialog, the card shows the new text.
W1-296.actual: Nothing visible happens. Every surface that renders PostCard (main feed, group feed, profile Posts/Letters tabs, Saved) holds its posts in client useState populated by the loadPosts/loadSavedPosts server actions. revalidatePath('/feed') in deletePost/editPost only re-renders the server component tree; the client `posts` state persists, so the deleted post remains on screen (clicking delete again errors) and the edited card keeps the pre-edit content until the member navigates away and back.
W1-296.evidence: post-card.tsx handleDelete does nothing locally on success: `const result = await deletePost(post.id); if (result.error) toast.error(result.error);` — no setRemoved, no callback, no router.refresh. Contrast the ADMIN path four lines below, which the author knew needed it: `async function handleModerationConfirm(note) { const result = await adminRemovePost(...); if (!result.error) setRemoved(true); }` with the comment 'Removed optimistically ... rather than waiting on the revalidatePath round trip.' EditPostDialog on success only does `toast.success(...); onClose();` — PostCard renders `post.content` from props, which never change. The lists are client state: post-feed.tsx `const [posts, setPosts] = useState<PostData[]>([]);` filled by `fetchPosts(null).then((data) => { setPosts(data.posts); ... })`; only creation refreshes it (feed-column.tsx `onPosted={() => setReloadKey((k) => k + 1)}` — there is no onDeleted/onEdited equivalent, confirmed by grep: reloadKey's only bump site is onPosted). deletePost's revalidatePath (actions.ts:340) cannot reach this state.
W1-296.fixDirection: Mirror the existing patterns: give PostCard an internal `setRemoved(true)` on successful member delete (exactly like handleModerationConfirm), and have EditPostDialog return the saved content/title to PostCard via an onSaved callback that PostCard mirrors into local state (add `const [content, setContent] = useState(post.content)` or an override state). Alternatively bump FeedColumn's reloadKey via an onChanged callback threaded down, but the local-state fix avoids a refetch and matches the admin path.
W1-296.gateOrTest: Playwright spec: create a post, delete it, expect.poll the card count to drop without navigation; edit a post, assert the card text updates. Pin in e2e/ next to sidebar.spec.ts.
W1-296.reproPlan: Live proof possible but writes to the shared production DB — use the demo deployment or code-argument-only. In demo: post, delete, observe the card persist until reload.

W1-297.title: A fresh letter (and any long feed post) has zero draft persistence: tab close, back-navigation, crash, or a failed submit silently loses everything written
W1-297.expected: The 6k question answered concretely: a session expiry or misnav mid-letter should not lose the draft — either a beforeunload/unsaved-changes guard, localStorage mirroring, or autosave from the first keystroke.
W1-297.actual: Autosave exists ONLY for resumed drafts: `useEffect(() => { if (!postId) return; ...`. /letters/new mounts CreatePostForm without postId (letter-desk.tsx passes it only on /letters/[id]/edit), so nothing is saved until the writer manually clicks 'Save as draft'. There is no beforeunload handler and no localStorage draft anywhere in src (grep for beforeunload/localStorage confirms: only tour/onboarding/celebration/theme keys exist). The 'All letters' back link in letter-desk.tsx is a plain <Link> with no unsaved-changes check. The feed composer is the same: content lives only in component state and an uncontrolled contentEditable. If createPost/publishDraft rejects (network drop, session revoked in another tab), handleSubmit has no try/catch, so the button also wedges (see the systemic finding) and the only recovery is a reload that erases the text.
W1-297.evidence: create-post-form.tsx:202-211: '/* Quiet autosave, resumed drafts only (a fresh letter has no row to update until the first explicit "Save as draft") */ ... useEffect(() => { if (!postId) return;'. letter-desk.tsx:41-50: `<Link href="/letters" ...>All letters</Link>` — no guard. Grep across src: zero `beforeunload` listeners; localStorage usage is only tour-local.ts, onboarding-local.ts, one-shot.ts, theme.
W1-297.fixDirection: Two cheap layers: (1) a beforeunload listener while `content.trim() && !submitting` in CreatePostForm (letter mode at minimum); (2) mirror the fresh-letter title/content into localStorage keyed by user id, offered back on next /letters/new mount ('Pick up where you left off?'), cleared on publish/save. Optionally create the draft row on first blur so the existing autosave takes over.
W1-297.gateOrTest: Unit test the localStorage mirror round-trip; Playwright: type into /letters/new, reload, assert the restore offer appears.
W1-297.reproPlan: Read-only live proof: type into /letters/new on the demo deployment, press the browser back button, return — the text is gone, no warning shown.

W1-298.title: Systemic: no client component handles a rejected server action — one network blip, deploy version-skew, or auth redirect leaves buttons wedged in their busy state, skeletons eternal, and optimistic state lying
W1-298.expected: A server action call can REJECT (it does not return {error}) on: network failure, 'Failed to find Server Action' version skew right after a deploy, and the proxy redirecting an expired/revoked session to /login. Each await site needs try/catch (or .catch) that resets its pending flag, reverts optimistic state, and tells the member something actionable — the standard the codebase itself sets in edit-post-dialog.tsx (try/finally), contribute-dialog.tsx (catch with a worded toast), avatar-crop-dialog.tsx, signup-form.tsx, and pen.tsx's useAutoSave ('That did not save. Check your connection.').
W1-298.actual: Almost every other await-an-action site assumes resolution. Consequences by class: (a) ETERNAL LOADING — post-feed.tsx initial load `fetchPosts(null).then((data) => {...})` has no .catch, so a rejection leaves `loading` true forever: the app's main page shows skeletons with no retry path. Same shape in comments-section initial load, saved-posts-feed, profile-author-feed, collection-client. (b) WEDGED CONTROLS — comments-section handleSubmit: `setSubmitting(true); ... await createComment(formData); ... setSubmitting(false)` with no try: a throw leaves submitting true and the comment box disabled forever; identical pattern wedges poll-display (whole poll disabled), message-composer Send, create-post-form Post/Save-as-draft (stranding the typed letter), notification-bell load-more (loadingMoreRef stuck true kills infinite scroll), comments-section IO callback (same ref), directory/collection/people-list Load more, people-panel keeper/remove/add, extend-deadline-card, console-collecting submit, accept-invite, publish-now-button, keeper-settings, letterhead-profile uploadAvatarBlob/handlePhotoRemove (photoBusy stuck). (c) LYING OPTIMISTIC STATE — post-card handleLike/handleBookmark, entry-love-button, photo-love-button, letter-engagement only revert when the action RESOLVES with {error}; on rejection the heart/ribbon stays flipped though the server never wrote it, until reload.
W1-298.evidence: Representative quotes. post-feed.tsx:118 `fetchPosts(null).then((data) => { if (cancelled) return; setPosts(data.posts); ... setLoading(false); });` — no .catch on the promise chain, setLoading(false) unreachable on rejection. comments-section.tsx:184-206 `setSubmitting(true); ... const result = await createComment(formData); if (result.error) {...} else {...} setSubmitting(false);` — no try/finally. poll-display.tsx:103-111 same. notification-bell.tsx:149-157 `loadingMoreRef.current = true; const data = await getNotifications({cursor}); ... loadingMoreRef.current = false;`. love callers: entry-love-button.tsx:34 `const result = await toggleEntryLove(entryId); if (result && "error" in result ...) { revert }` — a rejection skips the revert entirely. The correct in-repo counter-pattern proves feasibility: edit-post-dialog.tsx:49-59 wraps in try/finally; pen.tsx:354-359 `try { const result = await fn(); ... } catch { failed = "That did not save. Check your connection."; }`.
W1-298.fixDirection: Introduce one helper (e.g. `callAction(fn): Promise<{error?...}>` that catches rejection into `{ error: 'That did not go through. Check your connection.' }`) and route every client await-an-action through it; convert each setBusy pair to try/finally. Priority order: post-feed initial load and load-more, comments-section (all three sites), create-post-form handleSubmit, poll-display, message-composer, the four love/bookmark callers (revert in catch), notification-bell, directory/collection load-more, letterhead avatar paths, catchups controls.
W1-298.gateOrTest: Unit-test the helper; add one Playwright spec that blocks the action route (route.abort) and asserts the comment button re-enables with an error toast instead of wedging.
W1-298.reproPlan: Read-only live proof on any account: chrome-devtools emulate offline, click Load more on the feed — the button sticks at 'Loading...' forever and the console shows an unhandled rejection; go offline and submit a comment — composer wedges.

W1-299.title: Composer Post/Save buttons stay enabled while photo uploads are in flight: the post publishes without its photos, and the late uploads then attach themselves to the emptied composer
W1-299.expected: While `uploading` is true, Post and Save-as-draft are disabled (or the submit waits for the batch), so what the member attached is what publishes. message-composer.tsx gets this right: `const busy = sending || uploading; const canSend = body.trim().length > 0 && !busy;`.
W1-299.actual: On a slow connection a member attaches photos (spinner on the photo icon), types, and hits Post before the batch finishes: the post is created from the current `images` state — without the in-flight photos. When handleImageFiles later completes, it appends the uploaded URLs to the now-cleared arrays, so thumbnails reappear inside the empty, collapsed composer; the next post the member writes silently carries the previous post's photos. The uploaded R2 objects are orphaned if they never post.
W1-299.evidence: create-post-form.tsx:1087 `disabled={!content.trim() || submitting || savingDraft}` and :1059 the same for Save as draft — `uploading` absent from both, while it IS used to disable only the photo button itself (:832 `disabled: images.length >= 3 || uploading`). handleImageFiles is async and finishes with `setImages((prev) => [...prev, ...uploadedUrls]); setPreviews((prev) => [...prev, ...uploadedPreviews]);` (473-475) — functional updates that append to whatever the arrays hold at completion, including the `[]` a successful handleSubmit just set (564-570).
W1-299.fixDirection: Add `uploading` to both disabled conditions (label the button 'Uploading photo...' while so), and/or stamp a batch id when uploads start and drop the results if the composer was cleared meanwhile.
W1-299.gateOrTest: Unit-testable if the upload helper is injectable; otherwise Playwright with a throttled route: attach, submit immediately, assert the created post contains the image or the button was disabled.
W1-299.reproPlan: Requires a write — demo deployment: throttle to Slow 3G in chrome-devtools, attach a 5MB photo, type, press Post immediately; observe the post arrive without the photo and the thumbnail materialise in the empty composer.

W1-300.title: Double-tapping a heart (Instagram instinct) races an unguarded check-then-act toggle: unhandled P2002/P2025 rejection, heart desynced from the database until reload
W1-300.expected: Either the client serialises toggles per target (ignore clicks while one is in flight), or the server handles the P2002 (concurrent double-create) and P2025 (concurrent double-delete) that its own check-then-act shape makes inevitable, returning a coherent final state.
W1-300.actual: LoveButton fires onToggle on every click with no in-flight guard. Two rapid taps issue two concurrent toggleLike calls; both read `existing` before either writes (actions.ts:477 findUnique then create/delete with no transaction and no P2002/P2025 catch). The Like @@unique([userId,postId]) protects the DB, but the losing create/delete THROWS, the client has no catch (systemic finding), and PostCard's revert is additionally built on a stale snapshot — `setLiked(liked); setLikeCount(likeCount)` from the click-time closure (post-card.tsx:141-143) — so with two toggles in flight an error revert clobbers the newer state. Net: heart and count disagree with the server until reload, plus a Sentry exception per double-tap that races. Same shape in toggleCommentLike and the comment hearts.
W1-300.evidence: love-button.tsx handleClick: no disabled/pending state, calls `onToggle()` unconditionally. post-card.tsx:134-145: `const next = !liked; setLiked(next); setLikeCount(next ? likeCount + 1 : likeCount - 1); ... if (result.error) { setLiked(liked); setLikeCount(likeCount); }` — closure snapshot, not functional updates (entry-love-button/photo-love-button/letter-engagement use functional updates, correctly). actions.ts:477-489: `const existing = await prisma.like.findUnique(...); if (existing) { await prisma.like.delete(...) } else { await prisma.like.create(...) }` — no try, no upsert. schema.prisma:465 `@@unique([userId, postId])` makes the concurrent second create throw P2002.
W1-300.fixDirection: Client: track an in-flight ref per LoveButton caller and drop clicks while pending (still feels instant — the optimistic flip already happened), and use functional-update reverts in post-card. Server: wrap create in a try that treats P2002 as 'already liked' and delete P2025 as 'already unliked', returning the settled state.

W1-301.title: The notification badge can never rise during a session: no poll, no resync, and the 'new notification' shake is unreachable code
W1-301.expected: A member who keeps the app open (the feed is designed to be sat on) learns of new likes/comments/catchup events: the badge climbs and the bell plays its one decaying shake — which is exactly what the shake effect's comment says it is for ('one gentle decaying shake per new notification').

The only setters are the decrement on read (:166 `Math.max(0, c - 1)`) and zero on mark-all (:177). Nothing polls; handleOpen refetches the LIST but never the count. The sidebar bell mounts from the (main) layout, which persists across all soft navigations, so on mobile the badge shows the count from first page-load for the whole session. The header bell remounts only when the member navigates onto a page that passes unreadCount (the feed). The shake effect (:109-115, `if (unreadCount > prevUnread.current) setShakeKey(...)`) requires a rise no code path can produce — dead feature. Not the tracked bugs.md item 5 (that is about the bell being ABSENT from some page headers).
W1-301.evidence: Grep across src confirms the only setUnreadCount call sites are notification-bell.tsx:166 and :177, both decrements; initialUnreadCount flows from layout.tsx:35 / feed/page.tsx:34 into `useState(initialUnreadCount)` (:98) with no sync effect. No setInterval/poll exists in the file (verified in the timer sweep).
W1-301.fixDirection: Cheapest honest fix: have getNotifications also return the server's unread count and sync it in handleOpen; plus sync state when the prop changes (the adjust-state-during-render pattern already used in post-feed/image-viewer), so any router.refresh caused by other actions updates the badge. A slow interval poll (60-120s) would make the shake real; decide with the owner.
W1-301.gateOrTest: Unit test the reducer-ish sync (prop change updates state); or a Playwright two-context test: like a post from account B, refresh-free assert on account A after an action-triggered refresh.
W1-301.reproPlan: Live read-only-ish: sign in on two demo accounts; from B like A's post; observe A's badge never change despite navigation and actions.

W1-302.title: 'Load more' in flight across a filter change appends the old query's page to the new list, adopts the old cursor, and (feed/collection) can duplicate React keys
W1-302.expected: A page arriving for a superseded query is dropped, the way the same files' FIRST-page effects already do with their `cancelled` flags, and appended pages are deduped by id the way comments-section.mergeComments and notification-bell already do.
W1-302.actual: post-feed handleLoadMore: `const data = await fetchPosts(cursor); setPosts((prev) => [...prev, ...data.posts]); setCursor(data.nextCursor);` — no staleness token and no dedupe. Click Load more, then type a search or flip a filter while it flies: the filter effect replaces posts with the new query's page 1, then the old request lands and appends the OLD query's page 2 (possibly containing posts already present → duplicate `key={post.id}` → React key errors and auto-animate glitches), and the cursor now continues the OLD query for subsequent pages. collection-client is the same, plus offset pagination (`page: next`), so even without a filter change a photo approved between clicks shifts pages and duplicates a tile — and it has no dedupe either. directory-client dedupes ids but still adopts the stale cursor and mixes filtered sets.
W1-302.evidence: post-feed.tsx:152-159 quoted above; contrast :114-141 where the first-page effect carries `let cancelled = false; ... return () => { cancelled = true; }`. collection-client.tsx:163-172 `const data = await fetchPage(next); setPhotos((prev) => [...prev, ...data.photos]);` with fetchPage keyed on `page: p` (offset). directory-client.tsx:150-155 dedupes (`const seen = new Set(prev.map((u) => u.id))`) but `setCursor(data.nextCursor)` still lands after the filter-change resync.
W1-302.fixDirection: Give each list a monotonically bumped request/filter generation (the useUserSearch requestId pattern already in-repo); capture it before the await and discard results if it moved. Dedupe appended pages by id everywhere (lift mergeComments' pattern). Collection should also move to keyset (createdAt/id cursor) like the feed, but the client-side generation guard alone kills the mixed-list bug.
W1-302.gateOrTest: Component-level test with a deferred mock action: resolve the load-more after a filter change and assert the list contains only new-filter items.
W1-302.reproPlan: Read-only live proof: throttle network, click Load more on the feed, immediately type in search; observe old-filter posts appended below new results and a duplicate-key warning in the console.

W1-303.title: Server-rendered calendar dates format in UTC with an unpinned locale: IST members see yesterday's date on anything from 00:00-05:30 IST, and SSR'd client components hydrate to a different string (hydration failure)
W1-303.expected: Members are in IST (+5:30); servers run UTC. Every absolute date shown should be computed for Asia/Kolkata (the repo already knows this: wordle.ts pins `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"`), and any client component whose date string can differ between server and client render must guard it the way verify-email-banner.tsx does (its comment records the identical hydration crash 'caught live, 2026-08-13' and fixes it with useSyncExternalStore).
W1-303.actual: formatDisplayDate (`toLocaleDateString("en-GB", {day, month, year})` — no timeZone) and formatTimeAgo's >4-week branch (en-IN, no timeZone) render the UTC day. Two symptom classes. (a) Pure server components — letters index and reading page, collection permalink, catchups masthead/footer-tease/fresh-off-the-press, admin support/catchups — show a letter published at 00:30 IST on the 22nd as '21 Aug 2026' to everyone, permanently. (b) 'use client' components SSR'd with real props — archive-shelf, console-published, extend-deadline-card (locale `undefined` = server ICU vs browser), drafts-strip — produce a server string that differs from the client's re-render whenever the UTC and IST day (or server/browser locale format) differ: React 19 logs a hydration failure and re-renders the tree client-side (Sentry noise, animation replays), then shows the IST-correct date the server page never shows. formatTimeAgo in any SSR'd client tree (conversation.tsx inside the admin thread-view) adds occasional boundary mismatches ('just now' vs '1m ago').
W1-303.evidence: utils.ts:151-157: `return new Date(date).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "short", year: "numeric" })` — no timeZone option, so the server formats in UTC. extend-deadline-card.tsx:48 `at.toLocaleDateString(undefined, { weekday: "long", ... })` — locale AND zone unpinned in a component that SSRs (it is rendered with server-passed props inside catchup-home-shell). The proven-in-repo trap: verify-email-banner.tsx:113-120 'SSR said "5:30 am" where a 24-hour browser said "5:30", and React threw a hydration mismatch over the difference (caught live, 2026-08-13)'. The proven-in-repo fix for zone: wordle.ts:20 `toLocaleDateString("en-CA", { timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata" })`.
W1-303.fixDirection: Add `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` (and pin locales) inside formatDisplayDate and formatTimeAgo's date branch — one change fixes both symptom classes at every call site, and is correct for this audience per the wordle precedent. Sweep the remaining raw toLocaleDateString sites (archive-shelf, console-published, extend-deadline-card, drafts-strip, masthead, footer-tease, fresh-off-the-press, collection/[id], admin pages) onto the shared helpers.
W1-303.gateOrTest: Unit test formatDisplayDate with 2026-08-21T20:00:00Z asserting '22 Aug 2026'; visual suite would catch any format wobble across routes.
W1-303.reproPlan: Code-argument-only for the day-shift (needs a row timestamped 18:30-24:00 UTC); the hydration half is live-provable read-only: load /catchups as a keeper whose deadline crosses the boundary and read the hydration error in the console.

W1-304.title: Catch-up question reorder/remove is stale-props read-modify-write with no pending guard: quick successive clicks undo themselves or land out of order
W1-304.expected: A Keeper can click 'Move up' twice to move a question two slots; each click builds on the order the previous click produced, or the controls disable while a move is in flight.
W1-304.actual: handleMove swaps within `accepted` — a prop that only updates after onChanged() → router.refresh() completes a full roundtrip. A second click before the refresh recomputes from the ORIGINAL order: swapping the same pair again sends the original arrangement back to the server, so double-click-to-move-two-slots nets zero movement; and the two curatePrompt calls can also complete out of order server-side, letting the older order win. No busy state disables the arrows or the remove X (double-click remove fires a second call that errors).
W1-304.evidence: console-collecting.tsx:236-251: `const reordered = [...accepted]; [reordered[index], reordered[target]] = [reordered[target], reordered[index]]; const result = await curatePrompt({ action: "reorder", ..., orderedPromptIds: reordered.map((p) => p.id) }); ... onChanged();` — `accepted` comes from `edition.prompts` props (line 48), refreshed only by router.refresh; no useState mirror, no disabled flag on the arrow buttons (272-289) beyond boundary checks.
W1-304.fixDirection: Keep an optimistic local ordering in state (seeded from props, resynced on prop change) so consecutive clicks compound, and disable the row's controls while a curatePrompt is in flight; send the full ordered list (already the API shape) so the last write is self-consistent.
W1-304.gateOrTest: Component test: two rapid handleMove calls with a mocked slow action; assert the second payload reflects the first move.
W1-304.reproPlan: Requires writes — demo deployment: as Keeper with 4+ questions, double-click Move up on the last question with throttled network; observe it end where it started.

W1-305.title: Letter autosave failure is silent and the desk shows 'Saving...' forever: a writer signed out in another tab keeps writing an hour of letter that is never being saved
W1-305.expected: Autosave failure surfaces: the status flips to an error state that persists ('Not saved — check your connection'), the way pen.tsx's useAutoSave does for profile fields ('An error stays put. It is the one state that must not time itself out, because the value on screen is not the value on file').
W1-305.actual: The autosave timer runs `const result = await editPost(postId, fd); if (!result.error) onAutosaveState?.("saved");` — on an {error} result NOTHING is emitted, so the desk's status line (letter-desk.tsx:55) stays on whatever it last said ('Saving...' indefinitely, or a stale 'Saved' from the previous success); on a thrown rejection it is an unhandled rejection with the same stuck display. The onAutosaveState contract itself is `(s: "saving" | "saved")` — an error state is unrepresentable. A member whose session was revoked (password reset elsewhere bumps credentialVersion, ending every live session by design) gets a refusal from editPost every 2.5s-idle and no signal; their letter survives only as DOM state.
W1-305.evidence: create-post-form.tsx:218-227 quoted above; :117 `onAutosaveState?: (s: "saving" | "saved") => void;`. letter-desk.tsx:54-56 `{saveState === "saving" ? "Saving..." : saveState === "saved" ? "Saved" : ""}`. Contrast pen.tsx:331 `export type SaveState = "idle" | "saving" | "saved" | "error";` with catch at :357.
W1-305.fixDirection: Widen the contract to include "error" (message optional), emit it on {error} and in a catch around the editPost await, and render it persistently in letter-desk; on auth-flavoured errors offer the sign-in link. Pair naturally with finding 2's localStorage mirror.
W1-305.gateOrTest: Component test: mock editPost returning {error}, assert onAutosaveState('error'); letter-desk snapshot for the error line.
W1-305.reproPlan: Live provable on demo: open /letters/[id]/edit, sign out in a second tab, type; watch 'Saving...' persist with failed actions in the network panel.

W1-306.title: Profile field save error cannot be retried by re-blurring: the 'already saved' guard is stamped before the save succeeds
W1-306.expected: After 'That did not save. Check your connection.' the natural retry — click into the field, blur again — re-attempts the save.
W1-306.actual: commitField writes the dedupe ref optimistically: `if (saved.current[key] === value) return; saved.current[key] = value; void run(...)` — the ref is updated BEFORE the action runs, so after a failure every subsequent blur with the same (still-unsaved) text short-circuits on the first line. The persistent error banner (whose own comment says 'the value on screen is not the value on file') is then unfixable except by changing the text to something different, or editing away and back. Same pattern risk applies to any field the member retypes identically.
W1-306.evidence: letterhead-profile.tsx:392-401 quoted above; pen.tsx:362-367 shows the error state is designed to demand a retry ('must not time itself out').
W1-306.fixDirection: Move `saved.current[key] = value` into the success path of the run callback (set it after `!result.error`), or clear the key in the failure path; run() already reports which.
W1-306.gateOrTest: Component/unit test: mock updateProfileField to fail once then succeed; assert the second blur fires the action.
W1-306.reproPlan: Live on demo: edit About on your own profile, go offline, blur (error appears), go online, blur again — nothing is sent (network panel shows no second call).

W1-307.title: Mention dropdown shows the previous query's stale results while a new mention query loads
W1-307.expected: Starting a new @mention shows a fresh 'Searching...' (or nothing) rather than the candidate list from the last mention typed minutes ago.
W1-307.actual: `users` is never cleared: the effect early-returns when the query empties (`if (trimmedQuery.length < 1) return;`) and never resets state when the query changes. `visibleUsers = trimmedQuery.length > 0 ? users : []` means the instant a member types '@j' after an earlier '@san' search, the dropdown renders the 'san' candidates for the 200ms debounce plus the fetch, clickable, and `loading && users.length === 0` prevents the 'Searching...' row from replacing them. Clicking is not data-corrupting (you insert who you clicked) but the wrong people flash and can be mis-tapped on mobile.
W1-307.evidence: Lines 31-34 early return without cleanup of `users`; line 60 `const visibleUsers = trimmedQuery.length > 0 ? users : [];`; line 66 `loading && users.length === 0 ? "Searching..." : visibleUsers.map(...)`.
W1-307.fixDirection: setUsers([]) when trimmedQuery empties, and/or track the query each result set belongs to (the useUserSearch hook one directory over already does this — reusing it deletes the file's own fetch logic).
W1-307.gateOrTest: Component test: type q1, resolve, clear, type q2, assert no q1 rows render before q2 resolves.
W1-307.reproPlan: Read-only-ish on demo: in the composer type '@' + a name, erase it, type '@' + a different letter with throttled network; watch the old list flash.

W1-308.title: Feed and letter images render without dimensions: the page reflows under the reader as each lazy image loads
W1-308.expected: Images reserve their space (width/height attributes or aspect-ratio) so lazy loads don't shift the layout — the standard the Collection already meets: its Tile passes `width={photo.width} height={photo.height}` from the DB.
W1-308.actual: Post images are `` with no width/height and no stored dimensions (Post.images is a JSON array of URLs), so a card's height jumps when each image arrives — mid-scroll on the feed this yanks content, and on the letter reading page (letter-images.tsx, same shape) it jumps the paragraph the reader is on. With multi-image grids the max-h caps bound the shift but do not remove it (anything shorter than the cap lands at its own height).
